senses.definition: The fruit of the tree Malus domestica, chiefly with a green, red, or yellow skin, cultivated in temperate climates for cidermaking, cooking, and eating.

Often with a qualifying word: any fruit or vegetable, or any other thing (such as a cone or gall) produced by a plant, especially if from a tree and similar to the fruit of Malus domestica (noun sense 1.1).
Something which resembles the fruit of Malus domestica (noun sense 1.1) in shape (such as a ball, breast, or globe) or colour.
The round, fleshy part of a cheek between the eye and the corner of the mouth when a person is smiling.
The surface of revolution of a circular arc of an angle greater than 180° rotated about the straight line passing through the arc's two endpoints.
In full apple bowl: a round bowl of a tobacco pipe; also, a tobacco pipe with such a bowl.
In full old apple: a baseball.
According to postbiblical Christian tradition, the fruit of the tree of knowledge which was eaten by Adam and Eve despite God commanding them not to do so; the forbidden fruit.
Synonym of pome (“a type of fruit in which the often edible flesh arises from the swollen base of the flower and not from the carpels”).
An imaginary diminutive unit of height.
A tree of the genus Malus; especially Malus domestica which is cultivated for its edible fruit; the apple tree.

etymology.text: The noun is derived from Middle English appel (“Malus domestica fruit or tree, apple; any type of fruit, nut, or tuber; tree bearing fruit; (figurative) ball, sphere; (Christianity) forbidden fruit in Eden”), from Old English æppel (“apple; any type of fruit; (figurative) ball, sphere; eyeball”), from Proto-West Germanic *applu (“apple; any type of fruit”), from Proto-Germanic *aplaz (“apple; any type of fruit”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ébōl, *h₂ébl̥ (“apple”).

senses.definition: To make (something) appear like an apple (noun sense 1.1).

senses.definition: A product of fertilization in a plant, specifically

A sweet or sweetish vegetable, such as the petioles of rhubarb, that resembles a true fruit or is used in cookery as if it was a fruit.
An end result, effect, or consequence; advantageous or disadvantageous result.
Of, belonging to, related to, or having fruit or its characteristics; (of living things) producing or consuming fruit.
A homosexual man, especially an effeminate one.
An effeminate man.
Offspring from a sexual union.
A crazy person.

senses.definition: The act of preserving, guarding, or protecting; the keeping (of a thing) in a safe or entire state; preservation.

The discipline concerned with protection of biodiversity, the environment, and natural resources

The protection and care of cultural heritage, including artwork and architecture, as well as historical and archaeological artifacts
lack of change in a measurable property of an isolated physical system (conservation of energy, mass, momentum, electric charge, subatomic particles, and fundamental symmetries)

etymology.text: From Middle English happy (“fortunate, happy”), perhaps an alteration of Middle English happyn, happen (“fortunate, happy”), possibly related to or from Old Norse heppinn (“fortunate, happy”); and potentially assimilated to be equivalent to hap (“chance, luck, fortune”) + -y. Compare also Icelandic heppinn (“lucky”), Faroese heppin (“fortunate, lucky, happy”), Norwegian Nynorsk heppen (“lucky”), Scots happin (“fortunate, blessed”). See further at hap.
etymology.native: 「happy」源自中古英語 hapyn 或 happen，意為「幸運、幸福」，可能與古諾斯語 heppinn（意為「幸運」）有關；也可能與 hap（意為「機會、運氣」）+ -y 結合而成。可參照冰島語 heppinn（意為「幸運」）、法羅語 heppin（意為「幸運、幸福」）、挪威語 Nynorsk heppen（意為「幸運」）及蘇格蘭語 happin（意為「幸運、祝福」）。詳見 hap。

etymology.text: From Middle English malencolie, from Old French melancolie, from Ancient Greek μελαγχολία (melankholía, “atrabiliousness”) (from μέλας (mélas), μελαν- (melan-, “black, dark, murky”) + χολή (kholḗ, “bile”)), referring to the humour which ancient Hippocratic and later Galenic medicine associated with sadness and despondency. Compare the Latin ātra bīlis (“black bile”). The adjectival use is a Middle English innovation, perhaps influenced by the suffixes -y, -ly. Doublet of melancholia.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 malencolie，來自古法文 melancolie，再來自古希臘文 μελαγχολία（melankholía，意為「憂鬱」），此詞由 μέλας（mélas，意為「黑、暗、混濁」）與 χολή（kholḗ，意為「膽汁」）組成，指古代希波克拉底與蓋倫醫學所稱與悲傷與低落相關的體液。與拉丁文 ātra bīlis（「黑膽汁」）相對。形容詞用法為中世紀英文創新，可能受 -y、-ly 等後綴影響。此詞亦為 melancholia 的同源詞。

etymology.text: Adjective and noun from Middle English drye, dryge, drüȝe, from Old English drȳġe (“dry; parched, withered”), from Proto-West Germanic *drūgī, *draugī, from Proto-Germanic *drūgiz, *draugiz (“dry, hard”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰerǵʰ- (“to strengthen; become hard”), from *dʰer- (“to hold, support”). The verb derives from Middle English drien, from Old English drȳġan (“to dry”), from Proto-West Germanic *drūgijan, from Proto-Germanic *drūgiz (“hard, desiccated, dry”), from Proto-Indo-European
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 drye, dryge, drüȝe，來自古英語 drȳġe（「乾的；烤焦的」），源於原始西日耳曼語 *drūgī, *draugī，源於原始日耳曼語 *drūgiz, *draugiz（「乾的、堅硬的」），源於原始印歐語 *dʰerǵʰ-（「加強；變硬」），來自 *dʰer-（「持有、支撐」）。動詞源自中古英語 drien，來自古英語 drȳġan（「乾燥」），源於原始西日耳曼語 *drūgijan，源於原始日耳曼語 *drūgiz（「堅硬、脫水的、乾的」），源於原始印歐語...

examples.translation: 佛瑞德用花園水管向比利噴水。

examples.text: Tom poured milk down his nose and squirted it out of his eye.
examples.translation: 湯姆把牛奶倒進鼻子里，又從眼睛擠出來。

examples.text: Tom picked up the bottle of shampoo and squirted some in his hand.
examples.translation: 湯姆拿起洗髮精瓶子，擠了一些到手上。

examples.text: No pushing a fellow in and locking the door and squirting water at him through the window.
examples.translation: 別推人進屋、鎖門並從窗戶向對方噴水。

examples.text: The toothpaste squirted from the tube.
examples.translation: 牙膏從管中擠出來。

etymology.text: From Middle English squirten, squyrten, of uncertain origin; probably onomatopoeic. Akin to swirl. Compare Low German swirtjen (“to squirt”) and Swedish water onomatopoeias skvala, skvalp, skvimpa, and skvätta; Icelandic skvetta; and Norwegian skvette.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語，可能為擬聲詞；與旋渦相似。可比較低地德語及斯堪地納維亞語言中的類似發音。

senses.definition: Cold and damp, usually referring to hands or palms.

examples.translation: 最後你得到的只是一隻黏濕的握手。

examples.text: At the end, all you get is a clammy handshake.
examples.translation: 最後你得到的只是一隻黏濕的握手。

examples.text: Nobody enjoys a clammy handshake.

汗津津的、被汗水濕透的

etymology.text: From Middle English clam (“viscous, sticky; slimy”) + -y, from Old English clǣman (“to smear, bedaub”). Compare German klamm (“clammy”) and klemmen (“to be stuck, stick”). See also clam.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 clam（意為黏稠、黏糊）加上 -y，來自古英語 clǣman（意為塗抹、沾染）。可參照德語 klamm（意為黏糊）與 klemmen（意為卡住、黏住）。另見 clam。

senses.definition: In a state between dry and wet; moderately wet; moist.

examples.text: If a basement is damp, mosquitoes infest it.
examples.translation: 如果地下室潮濕，就會滋生蚊子。

etymology.text: From Middle English dampen (“to stifle; suffocate”), from Old English damp, from Proto-Germanic *dampaz.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 dampen（「抑制；扼殺」），來自古英語 damp，源自原始日耳曼語 *dampaz。

senses.definition: A hardened rectangular block of mud, clay etc., used for building.
Such hardened mud, clay, etc. considered collectively, as a building material.
Something shaped like a brick.
The colour brick red.

etymology.text: From Late Middle English brik, bryke, bricke, from Middle Low German and Middle Dutch bricke ("cracked or broken brick; tile-stone"; modern Dutch brik), ultimately related to Proto-West Germanic *brekan (“to break”), whence also Old French briche and French brique (“brick”). etymology.native: 來自中古英語 brik, bryke, bricke，源自低德語與中荷蘭語 bricke（意為「破裂的磚塊或瓦片」；現代荷蘭語 brik），最終源自古西德語 *brekan（意為「打破」），亦見於法語 briche 與 brique。亦可參見德語低德語 Brickje（意為「小木板或托盤」）。與 break 有關。

etymology.text: From Middle English chele, chile, from Old English ċiele, ċele (“cold; coldness”), from Proto-West Germanic *kali, from Proto-Germanic *kaliz, from Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“to be cold”). Closely related with Dutch kil. Also akin to cool, cold, gel, and congeal, which see.

Any vertebrate, including tetrapods.

senses.definition: A card game in which the object is to obtain cards in pairs or sets of four (depending on the variation), by asking the other players for cards of a particular rank.
senses.native: 一種卡片遊戲，目標是透過向其他玩家索取特定花色的牌來獲得成對或四張一組的牌（視變化而定）

examples.text: My father caught three fish yesterday.

examples.text: I felt like a fish out of water at this firm.

etymology.text: From Middle English fisch, from Old English fisċ (“fish”), from Proto-West Germanic *fisk, from Proto-Germanic *fiskaz (“fish”), from Proto-Indo-European *piskós (“fish”).

senses.definition: A hard, brittle, inorganic, nonmetallic material, made by firing a material such as clay at a high temperature.
An object made of this material.

examples.text: This store sells ceramics.
examples.translation: 這家店賣陶瓷製品。

examples.text: I have an interest in oriental ceramics.
examples.translation: 我對東方陶瓷有興趣。

examples.text: She became rich by making ceramic pieces.
examples.translation: 她靠製作陶瓷小物致富。

examples.text: Mary signed up for a ceramics class.
examples.translation: 瑪麗報名參加陶藝課程。

examples.text: Algeria can develop its ceramic industry.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞可以發展其陶瓷產業。

examples.text: Jack has a ceramic piggy bank in which he saves coins.
examples.translation: 傑克有一個陶瓷儲錢罐，他把硬幣存進去。

etymology.text: From Ancient Greek κεραμικός (keramikós, “potter's”), from κέραμος (kéramos, “potter's clay”), perhaps from a pre-Hellenic word or from Proto-Indo-European *kerh₂- (“to heat, burn, fire”).
etymology.native: 來自古希臘語 κεραμικός（keramikós，意為「陶匠的」），源自 κέραμος（kéramos，意為「陶匠的黏土」），可能來自前希臘語詞或印歐語系原始詞 *kerh₂-（意為「加熱、燃燒、火」）。

senses.definition: Darkness where light, particularly sunlight, is blocked.
Subtle insults.
Something that blocks light, particularly in a window.
A variety of a color, in particular one obtained by adding black (compare tint).
A subtle variation in a concept.
An aspect that is reminiscent of something.
A very small degree of a quantity, or variety of meaning
A ghost or specter; a spirit.
A postage stamp showing an obvious difference in colour/color to the original printing and needing a separate catalogue/catalog entry.
A cover around or above a light bulb, a lampshade.
A candle-shade.

examples.text: I won't sell this tree shade.
examples.translation: 我不會賣這個樹影的。

examples.text: Park the car in the shade.
examples.translation: 把車停到陰影裡。

examples.text: Why aren't you wearing your shades?
examples.translation: 為何你不戴太陽眼鏡？

examples.text: They sat in the shade of that big tree.
examples.translation: 他們在那棵大樹的樹蔭下坐了下來。

examples.text: There's no light without shade, and no shade without light.
examples.translation: 不存在沒有陰影的光明，也不存在沒有光明的陰影。

examples.text: Even crooked tree gives shade.
examples.translation: 即使是彎樹也能遮陰。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English schade, from Old English sċeadu, from Proto-West Germanic *skadu, from Proto-Germanic *skaduz, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ḱh₃tús, from *(s)ḱeh₃-. Doublet of shadow. Cognate with Ancient Greek σκότος (skótos) (whence English scoto-) and σκιά (skiá) (whence English scia-, and uncertainly via σκίουρος (skíouros) English squirrel).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 schade，來源為古英語 sċeadu，再溯自原始西日耳曼語 *skadu，再溯自原始德語 *skaduz，再溯自原始印歐語 *(s)ḱh₃tús，源自 *(s)ḱeh₃-。為 shadow 的同源詞。與古希臘語 σκότος (skótos)（由此衍生英文 scoto-）及 σκιά (skiá)（由此衍生英文 scia-，並可能經 σκίουρος (skíouros) 產生英文 squirrel）同源。

senses.definition: To shield (someone or something) from light.

examples.text: Line art emphasizes form and outline, over color, shading, and texture.
examples.translation: 線條藝術強調形式和輪廓，而不是顏色、陰影和紋理。

examples.text: The old oak tree shaded the lawn in the heat of the day.

senses.definition: A slight coloring.

senses.native: 任何顏色的淡色；特別是指加入白色後產生的顏色變化（對比色）

senses.definition: A color considered with reference to other very similar colors.

senses.definition: A shaded effect in engraving, produced by the juxtaposition of many fine parallel lines.
senses.native: 雕刻中由許多細密平行線並置產生的陰影效果

senses.definition: A vehicle window that has been darkened to conceal the occupant.
senses.native: 經過變色處理以遮蔽車內乘客的車窗

examples.text: The mountain glowed with the sunset tints.
examples.translation: 山巒在夕陽的餘暉中泛著光澤。

examples.text: Green tints prevail in the upholstery.
examples.translation: 沙發上呈現綠色調。

examples.text: Who in the rainbow can draw the line where the violet tint ends and the orange tint begins?
examples.translation: 誰能在彩虹中劃出線來，標示紫色色調結束與橘色色調開始的界線？

examples.text: A tint of glamour.

examples.text: The sunset gave the sky a delicate violet tint, softening the horizon's harshness.
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The old photograph possessed a sepia tint, hinting at memories from decades past.
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: Alteration of earlier tinct, influenced by French teinte (“tint”), from Latin tīnctus (“dyed”), past participle of verb tingō (“tinge”). Doublet of tent (“kind of red wine”). Cognate with Dutch tint, Estonian tint, French teinte, German Tinte, Hungarian tinta, Italian tinta, Luxembourgish Tintin, Portuguese tinta, and Spanish tinta.
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 tīnctus（染色的），是動詞 tingō（染色）的過去分詞，受法語 teinte 影響。與 tent（一種紅酒）同源，並與荷蘭語 tint、愛沙尼亞語 tint 等語言中的 tint 為同源詞。

senses.definition: The spectral composition of visible light.

Hue as opposed to achromatic colors (black, white and grays).
These hues as used in color television or films, color photographs, etc (as opposed to the shades of grey used in black-and-white television).
Any of the standard dark tinctures used in a coat of arms, including azure, gules, sable, and vert.
A paint.
Human skin tone, especially as an indicator of race or ethnicity.
Skin color, noted as normal, jaundiced, cyanotic, flush, mottled, pale, or ashen as part of the skin signs assessment.
A flushed appearance of blood in the face; redness of complexion.
Richness of expression; detail or flavour that is likely to generate interest or enjoyment.

senses.definition: The denotation, referent, or idea connected with a word, expression, or symbol.
The connotation associated with a word, expression, or symbol.
The purpose, value, or significance (of something) beyond the fact of that thing's existence.
Intention.

examples.text: There's another meaning behind his words.
examples.translation: 他的話裡有文章。

examples.text: What's the meaning of this sentence?
examples.translation: 這句話是什麼意思呀？

examples.text: Get the meaning of a word from its context.

examples.text: I don't understand the meaning of this phrase.

examples.translation: 湯姆的興趣是園藝、帆船、木工和騎腳踏車。

etymology.text: From Middle English gardyn, garden, from Anglo-Norman gardin, from Frankish *gardin-, oblique stem of *gardō (“enclosure, yard”), from Proto-Germanic *gardô (“enclosure, garden, house”), whence also inherited English yard. (compare Old French jart alongside jardin, Medieval Latin gardīnus). Doublet of jardin and of garth. Displaced Old English wyrttūn.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 gardyn，意為「花園」，來自盎格魯-諾曼語 gardin，再源自古法語 *gardin-，為 *gardō（「圍欄、院子」）的偏正形式，而 *gardō 又源自古德語 *gardô（「圍欄、花園、房屋」），此詞亦傳入英文 yard。可與古法文 jart 及中世紀拉丁文 gardīnus 相對照。為 jardin 與 garth 的同源詞，亦取代了古英語 wyrttūn。

senses.definition: Common, ordinary, domesticated.

examples.text: The ball bounded away into our neighbor's garden.
examples.translation: 球彈呀彈呀的彈進了鄰家的花園。

etymology.text: From Middle English gardyn, garden, from Anglo-Norman gardin, from Frankish *gardin-, oblique stem of *gardō (“enclosure, yard”), from Proto-Germanic *gardô (“enclosure, garden, house”), whence also inherited English yard. (compare Old French jart alongside jardin, Medieval Latin gardīnus). Doublet of jardin and of garth. Displaced Old English wyrttūn.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 gardyn，意為「花園」，來自盎格魯-諾曼語 gardin，再源自古法語 *gardin-，為 *gardō（「圍欄、院子」）的偏正形式，而 *gardō 又源自古德語 *gardô（「圍欄、花園、房屋」），此詞亦傳入英文 yard。可與古法文 jart 及中世紀拉丁文 gardīnus 相對照。為 jardin 與 garth 的同源詞，亦取代了古英語 wyrttūn。

senses.definition: A tract of ground kept in its natural state, about or adjacent to a residence, such as for the preservation of game, for walking, riding, or the like.
A piece of ground in or near a city or town, enclosed and kept for ornament and recreation.
An enclosed parcel of land stocked with animals for hunting, which one may have by prescription or royal grant.
A wide, flat-bottomed valley in a mountainous region.
An open space occupied by or reserved for vehicles, matériel or stores.
A partially enclosed basin in which oysters are grown.
An area zoned for a particular (industrial or commercial) purpose.
An area on which a sporting match is played; (soccer) a pitch.
An inventory of matériel.
A space in which to leave a car; a parking space.
The gear into which one shifts an automatic transmission when one is parking a car or truck. (Denoted with symbol P on a shifter's labeling.)

examples.text: The park is filled with children.
examples.translation: 公園裡都是孩子。

examples.text: Don't play baseball in the park.
examples.translation: 不要在公園玩壘球。

examples.text: He walked in the park yesterday.
examples.translation: 他昨天在公園裡散步。

examples.text: There are many parks in London.
examples.translation: 倫敦有很多公園。

examples.text: You can park behind the hotel.
examples.translation: 你們可以把車停到旅館背後。

examples.text: Don't just park along the road as you please.
examples.translation: 不要隨意在路邊停車。

etymology.text: From Middle English park, from Old French parc (“livestock pen”), from Medieval Latin parcus, parricus, from Frankish *parrik (“enclosure, pen, fence”). Cognate with Dutch perk (“enclosure; flowerbed”), Old High German pfarrih, pferrih (“enclosure, pen”), Old English pearroc (“enclosure”) (whence modern English paddock), Old Norse parrak, parak (“enclosure, pen; distress, anxiety”), Icelandic parraka (“to keep pent in under restraint and coercion”). More at parrock, paddock.
etymology.native: 「park」源自中世紀英語，來源為古法語「parc」，再源自中世紀拉丁語「parcus」或「parricus」，而這些詞又來自古弗蘭克語「*parrik」（意為圍欄或籠子）。與荷蘭語「perk」（意為圍欄或花壇）、古高地德語「pfarrih」或「pferrih」（意為圍欄或籠子）、古英語「pearroc」（意為圍欄，後演變為現代英語「paddock」）、古諾斯語「parrak」或「parak」（意為圍欄或籠子，亦可指困擾或焦慮）、冰島語「parraka」（意為拘束或壓制）同源。另見「parrock」與「paddock」。

senses.definition: Plants, taken collectively.
An abnormal mass on an endocardial surface, especially a heart valve, composed chiefly of fibrin and platelets and often containing microorganisms.
An excrescent, verrucous or fibrinous growth on a mucosal or epithelial surface.
The act or process of vegetating, or growing as a plant does; vegetable growth.

examples.text: He adores vegetation.
examples.translation: 他熱愛植物。

examples.text: Vegetation is green because of the chlorophyll.
examples.translation: 植物之所以呈綠色，是因為含有葉綠素。

examples.text: The slopes are devoid of vegetation of any kind.
examples.translation: 山坡上無任何植物。

examples.text: This city is very modern but it lacks vegetation.
examples.translation: 這座城市非常現代，但缺乏植物。

examples.text: Green vegetation is on the decrease on Earth.
examples.translation: 地球上綠色植物正逐年減少。

examples.text: Ziri's clothes got wet from the damp vegetation.
examples.translation: 茲里拉的衣服因潮濕的植物而濕透。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French végétation, from Medieval Latin vegetātiōnem.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀拉丁語 vegetātiōnem，來自法語 végétation。

senses.definition: A small forest.
A small forest with minimal undergrowth.
An orchard of fruit trees.
A place of worship.
A lodge of the Ancient Order of Druids.

examples.text: We walked through the bamboo grove.
examples.translation: 我們穿過竹林。

examples.text: Pandas live in bamboo groves.
examples.translation: 大熊貓生活在竹林中。

examples.text: There are many orange groves in Florida.
examples.translation: 佛羅里達州有許多橘樹園。

examples.text: In spring, the bamboo grove outside Hsinchu City is especially green.
examples.translation: 春天的時候，新竹城外的竹林特別翠綠。

examples.text: I lived near an orange grove when I was a kid.
examples.translation: 我小時候住在橘樹園附近。

examples.text: We must preserve the century-old grove.
examples.translation: 我們必須保護這片百年老樹林。

etymology.text: From Middle English grove, grave, from Old English grāf, grāfa (“grove; copse”), from Proto-West Germanic *graib, *graibō (“branch, group of branches, thicket”), from Proto-Germanic *graibaz, *graibô (“branch, fork”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 grove、grave，來自古英語 grāf、grāfa（小樹林；叢林），源於日耳曼語族 *graibaz、*graibô（枝條；分叉）

senses.definition: A gallery, platform, or balcony, usually roofed and often partly enclosed, extending along the outside of a building.

examples.text: They have a very nice veranda.
examples.translation: 他們有一個非常漂亮的暖房。

examples.text: Blimey, O'Reilly, who's got a veranda?
examples.translation: 喔天啊，奧萊利，你有陽台嗎？

examples.text: A cat entered through the veranda.
examples.translation: 一隻貓從陽台進來。

examples.text: Tom is having lunch with Mary on the veranda.
examples.translation: 湯姆正在陽台和瑪麗吃午餐。

examples.text: Tom and Mary often drink their morning coffee on the veranda.
examples.translation: 湯姆和瑪麗常在陽台喝早咖啡。

examples.text: I left some scallions out on the veranda for too long and they dried out.
examples.translation: 我把蔥放在陽台上太久，乾掉了。

etymology.text: An Indian English word of Indo-Portuguese origin, from Portuguese varanda (“balustrade; balcony”). Further etymology is unclear and disputed.
etymology.native: 印度英語詞，源自印度-葡萄牙語，來自葡萄牙語的 varanda（意為「護欄；陽台」）。其更詳細來源不明且有爭議。

senses.definition: A utensil or a tool designed for cutting, consisting of a flat piece of hard material, usually steel or other metal (the blade), usually sharpened on one edge, attached to a handle. The blade may be pointed for piercing.
A weapon designed with the aforementioned specifications intended for slashing or stabbing but too short to be called a sword; a dagger.
Any blade-like part in a tool or a machine designed for cutting, such as that of a chipper.

examples.text: This knife has served me well.
examples.translation: 這把刀對我很有用。

examples.text: Cut the cake with that knife.
examples.translation: 用那把刀把蛋糕切開。

examples.text: Tom handed the knife to Mary.
examples.translation: 湯姆把刀遞給了瑪麗。

examples.text: She has sharpened the knives.
examples.translation: 她磨了這些刀。

examples.text: This knife doesn't cut well.
examples.translation: 這把刀不好切東西。

examples.text: Here are the knives, the forks and the spoons.
examples.translation: 這裡有刀叉和湯匙。

etymology.text: From Middle English knyf, knif, from late Old English cnīf, from Old Norse knífr or Proto-West Germanic *knīb, from Proto-Germanic *knībaz, from *knīpaną (“to pinch”), Proto-Indo-European *gneybʰ- (compare Lithuanian gnýbti, žnýbti (“to pinch”), gnaibis (“pinching”)). Displaced native Middle English sax (“knife”), from Old English seax; and Middle English coutel, qwetyll (“knife”) from Old French coutel.
etymology.native: 「knife」源自中古英語 knyf、knif，來源為古英語 cnīf，再溯自古諾斯語 knífr 或古西德語 *knīb，源自古德語 *knībaz，而 *knīpaną（意為「捏」），再溯自印歐語系 *gneybʰ-（可比擬立陶宛語 gnýbti、žnýbti（意為「捏」）、gnaibis（意為「捏」））。此詞取代了中古英語原生詞 sax（刀），源自古英語 seax；以及中古英語 coutel、qwetyll（刀），源自法語 coutel。

senses.definition: To cut with a knife.
To use a knife to injure or kill by stabbing, slashing, or otherwise using the sharp edge of the knife as a weapon.
To cut through as if with a knife.
To betray, especially in the context of a political slate.
To positively ignore, especially in order to denigrate; compare cut.

examples.text: Tom was knifed to death.
examples.translation: 湯姆被人用刀捅死了。

etymology.text: From Middle English knyf, knif, from late Old English cnīf, from Old Norse knífr or Proto-West Germanic *knīb, from Proto-Germanic *knībaz, from *knīpaną (“to pinch”), Proto-Indo-European *gneybʰ- (compare Lithuanian gnýbti, žnýbti (“to pinch”), gnaibis (“pinching”)). Displaced native Middle English sax (“knife”), from Old English seax; and Middle English coutel, qwetyll (“knife”) from Old French coutel.
etymology.native: 「knife」源自中古英語 knyf、knif，來源為古英語 cnīf，再溯自古諾斯語 knífr 或古西德語 *knīb，源自古德語 *knībaz，而 *knīpaną（意為「捏」），再溯自印歐語系 *gneybʰ-（可比擬立陶宛語 gnýbti、žnýbti（意為「捏」）、gnaibis（意為「捏」））。此詞取代了中古英語原生詞 sax（刀），源自古英語 seax；以及中古英語 coutel、qwetyll（刀），源自法語 coutel。

senses.definition: To pierce or to wound (somebody) with a (usually pointed) tool or weapon, especially a knife or dagger.
To thrust in a stabbing motion.
To recklessly hit with the tip of a (usually pointed) object, such as a weapon or finger (often used with at).
To cause a sharp, painful sensation (often used with at).

examples.text: He doesn't know who stabbed him.
examples.translation: 他不知道誰捅了他。

examples.text: She stabbed him in the back.
examples.translation: 她在他的背上戳了一下。

examples.text: Tom tried to stab me.
examples.translation: 湯姆企圖刺我。

examples.text: Tom was stabbed to death.
examples.translation: 湯姆被人捅死了。

examples.text: I trusted him, and he stabbed me in the back.
Tom wasn't stabbed by Mary. John stabbed him.

etymology.text: First attested in Scottish English (compare Scots stob, stobbe, stabb (“a pointed stick or stake; a thrust with a pointed weapon”)), from Middle English stabbe (“a stab”), probably a variant of Middle English stob, stub, stubbe (“pointed stick, stake, thorn, stub, stump”), from Old Norse stobbi, stubbi, cognate with Old English stybb. Cognate with Middle Dutch stobbe.

senses.definition: An instrument of attack or defense in combat or hunting, e.g. most guns, missiles, or swords.
An instrument or other means of harming or exerting control over another.
senses.native: 傷害或控制他人的工具

senses.definition: A tool of any kind.
An idiot, an oaf, a fool, a tool; a contemptible or incompetent person.
A very skilled, competent, or capable person or thing worthy of awe.
The human genitals.

examples.text: Put down your weapons.
examples.translation: 放下你們的武器。

examples.text: Put your weapon down.
examples.translation: 把你的武器放下。

examples.text: Give me that weapon.
examples.translation: 把那件武器給我。

examples.text: It's a weapon.
examples.translation: 這是一種武器。

examples.text: It's against the law to carry weapons.
examples.translation: 攜帶武器是違法的。

examples.text: He used his umbrella as a weapon.
examples.translation: 他用他的雨傘當作武器。

etymology.text: From Middle English wepen, from Old English wǣpn, from Proto-West Germanic *wāpn, from Proto-Germanic *wēpną (“weapon”), of unknown origin, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *wēbnom.
etymology.native: 「weapon」源自古德語 *wāpn，再溯源自古德語 *wēpną，其來源不明，可能源自印歐語系 *wēbnom。

senses.definition: Something which projects, protrudes, juts out, sticks out, or stands out.
The action of projecting or throwing or propelling something.
The display of an image by devices such as movie projector, video projector, overhead projector or slide projector.
A forecast or prognosis obtained by extrapolation.
A belief or assumption that others have similar thoughts and experiences to one's own, including making accusations that would more fittingly apply to the accuser.
The image that a translucent object casts onto another object.
Any of several systems of intersecting lines that allow the curved surface of the earth to be represented on a flat surface. The set of mathematics used to calculate coordinate positions.
An image of an object on a surface of fewer dimensions.
An idempotent linear transformation which maps vectors from a vector space onto a subspace.
A transformation which extracts a fragment of a mathematical object.
A morphism from a categorical product to one of its (two) components.
The crisis or decisive point of any process, especially a culinary process.

examples.text: Is the soul a projection from somewhere else?

senses.definition: Any physical device meant to ease or do a task.
Any piece of equipment used in a profession, such as a craftsman's.
A piece of software used to develop software or hardware, or to perform low-level operations.
Anything that aids someone to perform an operation; an instrument; a means.
A person or group which is used or controlled, usually unwittingly, by another person or group, a pawn.
A particular skill pertaining to baseball (such as hitting, running, etc.).
A penis, notably with a sexual or erotic connotation.
An obnoxious or uptight person.
A handgun.

examples.text: I have a tool.
examples.translation: 我有一個工具。

examples.text: Lithic tools are studied by archaeologists.
Buffalo bones were made into tools.
I need a tool for pulling weeds in my garden.
examples.translation: 我需要工具來給花園除草。

examples.text: Give us the tools, and we'll finish the job.
examples.translation: 給我們工具，我們會完成工作。

examples.text: These tools are used for building a house.
examples.translation: 這些工具是用來造房子的。

etymology.text: From Middle English tool, tol, from Old English tōl (“tool, implement, instrument”, literally “that with which one prepares something”), perhaps borrowed from Old Norse tól, but at any rate ultimately from Proto-Germanic *tōlą (“that which is used in preparation, tool”), from Proto-Indo-European *dewh₂- (“to tie to, secure”), equivalent to taw (“to prepare”) + -le (agent suffix). Cognate with Scots tuil (“tool, implement, instrument, device”), Icelandic tól (“tool”), Faroese tól (“tool, instrume

senses.definition: A slightly curved but almost flat dish from which food is served or eaten.
Such dishes collectively.
The contents of such a dish.
A course at a meal.
An agenda of tasks, problems, or responsibilities
A flat object of uniform thickness.
Vehicle license plates, registration plates.
A taxi permit, especially of a metal disc.
Plate armor.
A layer of a material on the surface of something, usually qualified by the type of the material; plating
A material covered with such a layer.

examples.text: How many plates do we have?
examples.translation: 我們有多少個盤子？

examples.text: There are no clean plates.
examples.translation: 沒有任何干淨的盤子。

examples.text: Where are the plates?
examples.translation: 盤子在哪裡？

examples.text: The plate is dirty.
examples.translation: 盤子很髒。

examples.text: I want ten plates.
examples.translation: 我要十個盤子。

examples.text: When eating, the largest plate is always the table.
examples.translation: 吃飯的時候，最大的盤子永遠是桌子。

etymology.text: From Middle English plate, from Old French plate, from Medieval Latin plata, from Vulgar Latin *plat(t)us, from Ancient Greek πλατύς (platús, “broad, flat, wide”). Compare Spanish plato.
etymology.native: 「plate」源自中世紀英語，來源於古法語 plate，再源自中世紀拉丁語 plata，源自通俗拉丁語 *plat(t)us，最終來自古希臘語 πλατύς（platús），意為「寬廣、平坦」。可與西班牙語 plato 相比。

senses.definition: To cover the surface material of an object with a thin coat of another material, usually a metal.

examples.text: The chefs prepared the feast, plating dishes meticulously in the busy kitchen.
examples.translation: 廚師們在忙碌的廚房裡精心擺盤，準備盛宴。

etymology.text: From Middle English plate, from Old French plate, from Medieval Latin plata, from Vulgar Latin *plat(t)us, from Ancient Greek πλατύς (platús, “broad, flat, wide”). Compare Spanish plato.
etymology.native: 「plate」源自中世紀英語，來源於古法語 plate，再源自中世紀拉丁語 plata，源自通俗拉丁語 *plat(t)us，最終來自古希臘語 πλατύς（platús），意為「寬廣、平坦」。可與西班牙語 plato 相比。

senses.definition: An ordered, usually numerical sequence used for measurement; means of assigning a magnitude.
Size; scope.
The ratio of depicted distance to actual distance.
A series of notes spanning an octave, tritave, or pseudo-octave, used to make melodies.
A ladder; a series of steps; a means of ascending.
A line or bar associated with a drawing, used to indicate measurement when the image has been magnified or reduced.
A mathematical base for a numeral system; radix.
Gradation; succession of ascending and descending steps and degrees; progressive series; scheme of comparative rank or order.
A standard amount of money to be paid for a service, for example union-negotiated amounts received by a performer or writer; similar to wage scale or pay grade.

examples.text: Arrows can't pierce the dragon's scales.
examples.translation: 箭頭無法穿透龍的鱗片。

examples.text: The fish scales make good fertilizer.
examples.translation: 魚鱗很適合當肥料。

examples.text: They practiced their scales all day.
examples.translation: 他們整天練習鱗片。

examples.text: I weighed myself on the bathroom scales.
examples.translation: 我用浴室的體重計量了體重。

examples.text: Japanese comics have boomed on a large scale.
examples.translation: 日本漫畫在大規模上風靡一時。

examples.text: I want a map of Texas on a scale of 1 to 250000.
examples.translation: 我想要一張1比250000的得克薩斯州的地圖。

etymology.text: From Middle English scale, from Latin scāla, usually in plural scālae (“a flight of steps, stairs, staircase, ladder”), for *skand-slā, from scandō (“to climb”); see scan, ascend, descend, etc. Doublet of scala.
etymology.native: 來源於中世紀英文 scale，源自拉丁文 scāla，通常以複數形式 scālae 出現，意為「階梯、樓梯、梯子」，源自 *skand-slā，來自 scandō（意為「攀爬」）；見 scan、ascend、descend 等詞；為 scala 的同源詞。

senses.definition: The act of illustrating; the act of making clear and distinct.
The state of being illustrated, or of being made clear and distinct.
senses.native: 被說明或被闡述的狀態

senses.definition: Something which illustrates; a comparison or example intended to make clear or apprehensible, or to remove obscurity.
A picture designed to decorate a publication, or elucidate a literary work.
A calculated prevision of insurance premiums and returns (life insurance).
senses.native: 保險費與收益的計算預估（生命保險）

examples.text: The book has some interesting illustrations.
examples.translation: 這本書裡有一些有趣的插圖。

examples.text: This book has 252 pages, excluding illustrations.
examples.translation: 這本書共有 252 頁，不包括插圖。

examples.text: The book's illustrations are very good.
examples.translation: 這本書的插圖非常棒。

examples.text: This book has a lot of illustrations.
examples.translation: 這本書有很多插圖。

examples.text: Here's an illustration at the top of this page.
examples.translation: 這裡有一張位於本頁頂部的插圖。

examples.text: The illustration shows the depths of the earth.
examples.translation: 這幅插圖展示了地球的深層結構。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French illustration, from Latin illūstrātiō, from illūstrō (“to illustrate”). By surface analysis, illustrate + -ion.
etymology.native: 源自中古法語 illustration，來自拉丁語 illūstrātiō，源於動詞 illūstrō（「使明亮、闡明」）。按表層分析可拆分為 illustrate 加上 -ion。

senses.definition: A device used to dampen, muffle, restrain, or otherwise control the movement of a fluid, or waves travelling through a fluid such as light or sound; specifically, a surface positioned inside an open area to inhibit direct motion from one place to another without preventing motion altogether.
senses.native: 用於減弱、消音、抑制或以其他方式控制流體運動，或光波或聲波等穿過流體的波的裝置；具體而言，是設置在開放區域內以阻擋直接運動而不阻止任何運動的表面

senses.definition: A lever for operating the throttle valve of a winding engine.
senses.native: 用於操作捲軸引擎排氣閥的槓桿

senses.definition: A device to prevent the spreading of sound or light.
senses.native: 防止聲音或光線擴散的裝置

senses.definition: A barrier designed to obstruct and confuse enemies, rendering them vulnerable.
senses.native: 設計用於阻礙並混淆敵人，使其處於脆弱狀態的障礙物

examples.text: Tanker trucks use baffles to keep the liquids inside from sloshing around.
examples.translation: 油罐車裝有隔板，防止液體在車內晃動。

etymology.text: The origin of the verb is uncertain; it is possibly:
etymology.native: 此動詞的來源尚不確定，可能是：

senses.definition: A small colorless disk-shaped particle found in the blood of mammals, which plays an important role in the formation of blood clots.

examples.text: The young leaves are lush.

examples.text: The garden flourished with lush rosemary plants.

examples.text: The mountains are a lush green in summer.

senses.definition: Any member of the family Cactaceae, a family of flowering New World succulent plants suited to a hot, semi-desert climate.

senses.definition: Exceeding proper limits; excessive or unduly high; extravagant.

examples.text: She throws the most exorbitant parties.

examples.text: This year, the prices are simply exorbitant.
examples.translation: 今年，價格簡直是過高。

examples.text: He's selling his car at an exorbitant price.
examples.translation: 他以過高的價格出售他的汽車。

examples.text: The price of this camera is exorbitant.

examples.text: Some generous souls made exorbitant donations that helped save the orphanage.

etymology.text: From Middle English exorbitant, through Old French from Late Latin exorbitāns, present active participle of exorbitō (“to go out of the track”), from ex (“out”) + orbita (“wheel-track”); see orbit. Compare French exorbitant.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 exorbitant，經古法語來自晚拉丁語 exorbitāns，為 exorbitō（「脫離軌道」）的現在分詞，由 ex（外）加上 orbita（輪軌）組成；可比較法語 exorbitant。

senses.definition: Standing, pointing, or moving straight up or down; parallel to the local direction of gravity; along the direction of a plumb line; perpendicular to something horizontal.

etymology.text: From Middle English sclise, sklise, from Old French esclice, esclis (“a piece split off”), deverbal of esclicer, esclicier (“to splinter, split up”), from Frankish *slitjan (“to split up”), from Proto-Germanic *slitjaną, from Proto-Germanic *slītaną (“to split, tear apart”), from Proto-Indo-European *sleyd- (“to rend, injure, crumble”). Akin to Old High German sliz, gisliz (“a tear, rip”), Old High German slīȥan (“to tear”), Old English slītan (“to split up”), modern French éclisse. More at slit
etymology.native: 此詞源自中世英文 sclise, sklise，來自古法文 esclice, esclis（意為「分離出的一塊」），為動詞 esclicer, esclicier（意為「劈開、分開」）的來源，而該動詞又源自古弗蘭克語 *slitjan（意為「劈開」），再溯源自古日耳曼語 *slitjaną，再往上溯源自古日耳曼語 *slītaną（意為「劈開、撕裂」），最終源自印歐語系 *sleyd-（意為「撕裂、損傷、粉碎」）。與古高地德語 sliz, gisliz（意為「撕裂、裂口」）、古高地德語 slīȥan（意為「撕裂」）、古英語 slītan（意為「劈開」）、現代法文 éclisse 同源。詳見 slit

etymology.text: From Middle English slitten, from Old English slītan, from Proto-Germanic *slītaną (“to tear apart”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)leyd- (“to tear, rend (cut apart), split apart”). Possibly cognate with Latin laed- (“to strike, hurt, injure”). Doublet of slite; also related to slice through French borrowing. Apparently unrelated to English slot, whose etymology, however, is uncertain.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 slitten，再追溯至古英語的 slītan，來自日耳曼語族的 *slītaną（撕裂），最終源自印歐語系的 *(s)leyd-（撕裂、割開）。可能與拉丁語的 laed-（打擊、傷害）同源。它是 slite 的同源詞，也與從法語借來的 slice 有關。似乎與英語的 slot 無關，後者的詞源尚不確定。

Related also to Middle Low German rocke (“rock ledge”). One suggestion is that it derives from Vulg

Cognate with Icelandic gustur (“gust of wind”). Related also to Old Norse gusa (“to gush forth”), Old High German gussa (“flood”), Middle English guschen (> English gush).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語未記載的 *gust，來自古諾斯語 gustr（意為「風暴」），源自原始日耳曼語 *gustiz，再源自原始印歐語 *ǵʰew-。與冰島語 gustur（意為「風暴」）同源，亦與古諾斯語 gusa（意為「噴湧」）、古高地德語 gussa（意為「洪水」）、中古英語 guschen（演變為現代英語 gush）相關。

senses.definition: To blow in gusts.
To taste.
To have a relish for.

examples.text: Fatigued firefighters battled gusting winds fanning multiple blazes.
examples.translation: 疲憊的消防員在強勁風勢中奮力對抗多處火災。

etymology.text: Apparently from an unrecorded Middle English *gust, from Old Norse gustr (“a gust, blast”), from Proto-Germanic *gustiz, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰew-. Cognate with Icelandic gustur (“gust of wind”). Related also to Old Norse gusa (“to gush forth”), Old High German gussa (“flood”), Middle English guschen (> English gush).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語未記載的 *gust，來自古諾斯語 gustr（意為「風暴」），源自原始日耳曼語 *gustiz，再源自原始印歐語 *ǵʰew-。與冰島語 gustur（意為「風暴」）同源，亦與古諾斯語 gusa（意為「噴湧」）、古高地德語 gussa（意為「洪水」）、中古英語 guschen（演變為現代英語 gush）相關。

senses.definition: A violent gust of wind (in windy weather) or apparent wind (around a moving vehicle).
A forcible stream of gas or liquid from an orifice, for example from a bellows, the tuyeres of a blast furnace, a person's mouth, etc.
senses.native: 從孔口噴出的強迫性氣體或液體流，例如風箱、高爐的吹管、人的嘴等

senses.definition: A hit of a recreational drug from a pipe.
senses.native: 從煙囪吸食的可樂迷幻藥一次劑量

senses.definition: The continuous blowing to which one charge of ore or metal is subjected in a furnace.
senses.native: 高爐中對一爐礦石或金屬連續吹風的動作

senses.definition: The exhaust steam from an engine, driving a column of air out of a boiler chimney, and thus creating an intense draught through the fire; also, any draught produced by the blast.
senses.native: 引擎排出的蒸汽，將空氣柱從鍋爐煙囪推出，從而產生強烈的火風；也指由吹風產生的任何風流

senses.definition: An explosion, especially for the purpose of destroying a mass of rock, etc.
senses.native: 爆炸，特別是為了摧毀大塊岩石等物體而進行爆炸

senses.definition: A direct and fast swing of a bat; a home run.
senses.native: 球棒的一次直接且快速的揮擊；本壘打

senses.definition: A verbal attack or punishment; a severe criticism or reprimand.
senses.native: 言語上的攻擊或懲罰；嚴厲的批評或斥責

senses.definition: An explosive charge for blasting.
A loud, sudden sound.

examples.text: Yesterday, we had a blast!
examples.translation: 昨天我們玩得特別痛快!

examples.text: It was a blast.
examples.translation: 它超級好玩的

examples.text: News of the recent blast is all over the radio.
examples.translation: 收音機廣播充斥著有關最近爆炸的新聞。

examples.text: A series of blasts reduced the laboratory to ruins.
examples.translation: 一連串的爆炸使實驗室成為廢墟。

examples.text: An icy blast of wind chilled me to the bone.
examples.translation: 冰冷的疾風吹到我骨子裡去了。

examples.text: Tom was injured in the blast.
examples.translation: 湯姆在爆炸中受傷。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English blast, from Old English blǣst (“blowing, blast”), from Proto-West Germanic *blāstu, from Proto-Germanic *blēstuz (“blowing, blast”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 blast，來自古英語 blǣst（「吹拂、強風」），源自原始日耳曼語 *blēstuz。

senses.definition: simple past and past participle of mottle

etymology.text: 1670-80 mottle + -ed.
etymology.native: 1670-80 年由 mottle 派生出的過去分詞形式。

senses.definition: Discoloured by spots; stained.
Characterized by spots (used especially of animals and plants).

examples.text: Dan was spotted at a local car rental agency.
examples.translation: 丹在當地租車行被目擊到。

examples.text: The comet was first spotted by amateur astronomer Michael Mattiazzo.
examples.translation: 這顆彗星是由業餘天文愛好者邁克爾·馬蒂亞佐首次目擊發現的。

examples.text: A black-and-white spotted cow.
examples.translation: 黑白斑點的牛。

examples.text: The wine spotted the tablecloth.
examples.translation: 葡萄酒弄髒了桌布。

examples.text: The canvas was spotted with raindrops, each a tiny mirror reflecting the sky.
examples.translation: 畫布上佈滿雨滴，每一滴都像小鏡子，映照著天空。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Her dress, spotted with ink, looked like a map of forgotten thoughts.
examples.translation: 她穿的裙子沾滿墨水，彷彿是一張遺忘思緒的地圖。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

senses.definition: simple past and past participle of spot

pronunciations.value: S P AA1 T IH0 D

senses.definition: To draw up (a document etc.), to designate (a cheque).
To discern; to manage to see, hear etc.
To manage, get along; to do (well, badly etc.).
To represent; to make (something) appear to be true.
senses.native: 代表；使（某物）看起來是真的

senses.definition: To send out.
To get along with (someone).
To make an (often temporary) home.
To embrace and kiss passionately.
To engage in heavy petting or sexual intercourse.
senses.native: 親密接觸或發生性關係

examples.text: Tom couldn't make out their faces.
examples.translation: 湯姆看不清楚他們的臉。

examples.text: I can't make out these figures.
examples.translation: 我看不清這些數字。

examples.text: What can you make out?
examples.translation: 你能看出什麼來嗎？

examples.text: I couldn't make out what he meant by 'megafeps'.
examples.translation: 我不能明白他說的「megafeps」是甚麼意思。

examples.text: I can't make out what the man is saying.
examples.translation: 我聽不清那個男的在說些什麼。

examples.text: I can't make out what he wants.
examples.translation: 我不明白他想要什麼。

senses.definition: To see, find; to pick out, notice, locate, distinguish or identify.

examples.text: There's a little black spot on the sun today.

relations.native: 因灑漏或其他接觸液體或物質而變色

etymology.text: From Middle English spot, spotte, partially from Middle Dutch spotte (“spot, speck”), and partially merging with Middle English splot, from Old English splott (“spot, plot of land”), from Proto-West Germanic *splott, from Proto-Germanic *spluttaz (“segment”), from Proto-Indo-European *splt-no- (“an off-split, segment”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)pel- (“to split”).

senses.definition: To make distinctions.
To treat or affect differently, depending on differences in traits.
senses.native: 根據特質的差異而給予不同待遇或影響

senses.definition: To make decisions harmful to (a person or group) based on prejudice.
To infringe upon (a person's rights) in a prejudicial manner.
senses.native: 以偏見的方式侵害（某人的權利）

senses.definition: To set apart as being different; to mark as different; to separate from another by discerning differences; to distinguish.
senses.native: 將其標記為不同；將其與另一者分開，透過辨識差異

examples.text: I don't discriminate.
examples.translation: 我不歧視人。

examples.text: Most of women are discriminated.
examples.translation: 大多數女性受到歧視。

examples.text: Tom doesn't discriminate.
examples.translation: 湯姆不會進行區分。

examples.text: I was discriminated against in my home country.
examples.translation: 我在原籍國曾受到歧視。

examples.text: Discriminating against people because of their race is a mistake.
examples.translation: 因為人的種族而歧視他們是一種錯誤。

examples.text: We must be able to discriminate between objects and situations.
examples.translation: 我們必須能夠分辨物件與情境的差異。

etymology.text: First attested in 1615; borrowed from Latin discrīminātus, perfect passive participle of discrīminō (“to divide, separate, distinguish”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix) and -ate (adjective-forming suffix)), from discrīmen (“a space between, division, separation, distinction”), from discernō (“to divide, separate, distinguish, discern”). By surface analysis, dis- + criminate.
etymology.native: 最早見於 1615 年；借自拉丁語 discrīminātus，動詞 discrīminō（「分開、分離、區分」）的完成被動分詞。

senses.definition: To oxidize or discolor due to oxidation.
To compromise, damage, soil, or sully.
To lose its lustre or attraction; to become dull.
senses.native: 失去光澤或吸引力；變得暗淡無光

senses.definition: To use a sign, image, expression, etc. sufficiently close to a trademarked one that it brings disrepute to it.
senses.native: 使用與商標極其相似的符號、圖像或表達方式，使其招致不美譽

examples.text: Old love does not tarnish.
examples.translation: 古老的愛情不會褪色。

examples.text: Mary's reputation was tarnished by gossip.
examples.translation: 瑪麗的聲譽因閒言碎語而受損。

examples.text: They tarnished the village's reputation.
examples.translation: 他們損害了村莊的聲譽。

examples.text: A person's reputation can be greatly burnished or tarnished depending on how the media chooses to cover them.
examples.translation: 人們的聲譽取決於媒體如何報導，可能會受到極大損害或提升。

examples.text: Those photos—which experts say could have been created as early as 1850—were tarnished so badly they were unrecognizable.
examples.translation: 那些照片據專家稱可能早在 1850 年就已拍攝，因受損嚴重而無法辨認。

examples.text: People on the website engage in a disgraceful behavior of bullying Antonio, tarnishing the online community's reputation.
examples.translation: 網站上的人對安東尼進行霸凌行為，損害了網路社群的聲譽。

relations.native: 因灑漏或其他接觸液體或物質而變色

etymology.text: From Middle English ternysshen, from Old French terniss-, stem of ternir (“to make dim, make wan”), borrowed from Old High German *ternen, tarnen, from Proto-West Germanic *darnijan (“to conceal”). Doublet of dern and darn.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 ternysshen，來自舊法語 terniss-，源自 ternir（使變暗、使蒼白），借自舊高地德語 *ternen 及 tarnen。

senses.definition: To mark with speckles.

examples.text: I have a black and white speckled dog.
examples.translation: 我有一隻黑白斑點狗。

examples.text: This is a large speckled brown egg.
examples.translation: 這是一顆帶有斑紋的大褐色雞蛋。

examples.text: The black-and-white speckled cover of the classic school notebook is timeless.
examples.translation: 經典校用筆記本黑白相間的斑點封面永恆經典。

examples.text: Her complexion bears a subtle, almost imperceptible speckling characteristic of her heritage.
examples.translation: 她的膚色帶有微妙的、幾乎難以察覺的斑點特徵，這是其血統的特徵。

examples.text: Nature's artistry is revealed in the microscopic speckling that defines every living cell.
examples.translation: 大自然的神奇工藝在於定義每個活細胞的微細斑點紋理。

etymology.text: The noun is from Middle Dutch spekkel; the verb was later coined from the noun, in the late 16th century.
etymology.native: 此詞源自中世紀荷蘭語的 spekkel；動詞則於 16 世紀末由該名詞衍生而成。

senses.definition: A flat fold; a doubling, as of cloth; a pleat.
A braid, as of hair or straw; a plat.

examples.text: She wore her hair in plaits.
examples.translation: 她扎著辮子。

examples.text: Mary plaits her hair into a pigtail.
examples.translation: 瑪莉把頭髮編成雙馬尾。

examples.text: Mary decided to cut off her plaits.
examples.translation: 瑪麗決定剪掉她的髮辮。

examples.text: Swazi women traditionally plait grass to make thatch roofs for their homes.
examples.translation: 斯瓦濟人女性傳統上會編草製成屋頂茅草。

etymology.text: From Middle English pleit, from Anglo-Norman pleit (compare Old French ploit), from Latin plectō, which is akin to Old Norse flétta (Danish flette), Russian плести́ (plestí) and also to Old English fleohtan, which it displaced. Doublet of plight (“plait, fold”) and pleat.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 pleit，來自盎格魯-諾曼語 pleit（對照古法語 ploit），源自拉丁語 plectō，與古挪威語 flétta（丹麥語 flette）、俄語 плести́（plestí）相近，亦與古英語 fleohtan 相似，此詞已取代它。是 plight（「編織、摺疊」）的同源詞。

senses.definition: To fold; to double in narrow folds; to pleat
To interweave the strands or locks of; to braid

examples.text: He plaited her hair for her.
examples.translation: 他為她編髮。

examples.text: Mary is plaiting her hair into a pigtail.
examples.translation: 瑪莉正在把頭髮編成辮子。

examples.text: This made Cinderella's lot still harder, for it was she who ironed her sisters' linen and plaited their ruffles.
examples.translation: 這讓灰姑娘的困境更為艱難，因為是她鐵了姐妹的襯衫，並編了姐妹的花邊。

etymology.text: From Middle English pleit, from Anglo-Norman pleit (compare Old French ploit), from Latin plectō, which is akin to Old Norse flétta (Danish flette), Russian плести́ (plestí) and also to Old English fleohtan, which it displaced. Doublet of plight (“plait, fold”) and pleat.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 pleit，來自盎格魯-諾曼語 pleit（對照古法語 ploit），源自拉丁語 plectō，與古挪威語 flétta（丹麥語 flette）、俄語 плести́（plestí）相近，亦與古英語 fleohtan 相似，此詞已取代它。是 plight（「編織、摺疊」）的同源詞。

senses.definition: A twisting force.
Anything twisted, or the act of twisting.
The form given in twisting.
The degree of stress or strain when twisted.
A type of thread made from two filaments twisted together.
A sliver of lemon peel added to a cocktail, etc.
A sudden bend (or short series of bends) in a road, path, etc.
A distortion to the meaning of a passage or word.
An unexpected turn in a story, tale, etc.
A modern dance popular in Western culture in the late 1950s and 1960s, based on rotating the hips repeatedly from side to side. See Twist (dance) on Wikipedia for more details.
A rotation of the body when diving.

examples.text: Don't twist my words around.
examples.translation: 不要扭曲我說的話。

examples.text: Don't twist your words with me.
Dickens was the author of 'Oliver Twist'.
You need to twist the faucet to open it.
I like it when you twist my conkers.
Did he twist the facts to suit his narrative?

etymology.text: From Middle English twist, from Old English *twist, in compounds (e.g. mæsttwist (“a rope; stay”), candeltwist (“a wick”)), from Proto-Germanic *twistaz, a derivative of *twi- (“two-”) (compare also twine, between, betwixt).

senses.definition: An act of folding.

examples.text: Fold the quilt.
examples.translation: 折被子。

examples.text: If you don't fold your clothes or hang them, they will be wrinkled.
examples.translation: 若沒有將衣服摺起來或是掛在衣架上，會起皺紋。

examples.text: Fold the towel and place it on the towel rack.
examples.translation: 將毛巾摺疊後放在毛巾架上。

examples.text: Could you please help me fold the laundry?
examples.translation: 能請您幫我摺洗好的衣物嗎？

examples.text: After two reraises in quick succession, John realised his best option for this poker hand was probably a fold.
examples.translation: 在連續兩次重注後，約翰意識到這張撲克牌的最佳選擇可能是棄牌。

etymology.text: The verb is from Middle English folden, from Old English fealdan, from Proto-West Germanic *falþan, from Proto-Germanic *falþaną (“to fold”), from Proto-Indo-European *pel- (“to fold”).
etymology.native: 此詞源於中古英語的 folden，來自古英語 fealdan，再源自原始日耳曼語 *falþaną（「摺疊」），最終追溯至原始印歐語 *pel-（「摺疊」）。

senses.definition: To form something by passing lengths or strands of material over and under one another.
To spin a cocoon or a web.
To unite by close connection or intermixture.
senses.native: 透過緊密連結或混合而結合

senses.definition: To compose creatively and intricately; to fabricate.
senses.native: 創意且複雜地編織；製造

senses.definition: To move by turning and twisting.
To make (a path or way) by winding in and out or from side to side.
senses.native: 透過蜿蜒進出或左右穿梭而開闢道路

senses.definition: To move the head back and forth in a stereotyped pattern, typically as a symptom of stress.
senses.native: 以特定模式前後搖動頭部，通常為壓力症狀

examples.text: Basket weaving isn't all that complicated.
examples.translation: 編織籃子並不算太複雜。

examples.text: The caterpillar of the weaving moth spins a silk thread to form a cocoon.
examples.translation: 編織蛾類的幼蟲會紡出一條絲線形成蛹室。

examples.text: This loom weaves yarn into cloth.
The boxer weaved out the way to avoid getting hit.
examples.translation: 拳手編織出路以避開被擊中。

examples.text: A tangled web they weaved, as they practiced to deceive.
examples.translation: 他們編織了一張糾結的網，正如他們練習欺騙一樣。

examples.text: Spiders weave beautiful but deadly webs.

etymology.text: From Middle English weven (“to weave”), from Old English wefan (“to weave”), from Proto-West Germanic *weban, from Proto-Germanic *webaną, from Proto-Indo-European *webʰ- (“to weave, braid”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 weven（「編織」），來自古英語 wefan（「編織」），源自西日耳曼語族 *weban，源自日耳曼語族 *webaną，源自印歐語系 *webʰ-（「編織、編髮」）。

senses.definition: A fully sufficient or abundant quantity of; enough or more than enough.
A quantity (of something) that is fully sufficient; plenty.

examples.text: We have ample time to finish the task.
examples.translation: 我們有足夠的時間完成這項任務。

examples.text: It is a large house with ample space for all of us.
examples.translation: 這是一棟大房子，為我們所有人提供了足夠的空間。

examples.text: We don't need any more. We already have ample.
examples.translation: 我們不需要更多了，我們已經夠了。

etymology.text: From late Middle English ample, from Middle French ample, from Latin amplus (“large”).

senses.definition: Large; great in size, extent, capacity, or bulk; for example spacious, roomy or widely extended.
Very adequate.
Not contracted or brief; not concise; extended; diffusive

examples.text: There's ample room in the attic.
examples.translation: 閣樓空間充足。

examples.text: We have ample funds in hand.
examples.translation: 我們手頭資金充裕。

examples.text: She's got ample frontage.
examples.translation: 她前額寬闊。

examples.text: We have ample time to catch our train.
examples.translation: 我們有充裕的時間趕上火車。

examples.text: He has ample experience.
examples.translation: 他經驗豐富。

examples.text: Both Tom and Mary's personalities are ample.
examples.translation: 湯姆與瑪麗的個性都十分豐沛。

etymology.text: From late Middle English ample, from Middle French ample, from Latin amplus (“large”).

senses.definition: Having little flesh; lean; thin.
Poor, deficient or inferior in amount, quality or extent
Of a set: such that, considered as a subset of a (usually larger) topological space, it is in a precise sense small or negligible.
senses.native: 指集合中，視為較大拓撲空間的子集時，在精確意義上微小或可忽略

senses.definition: Dry and harsh to the touch (e.g., as chalk).
senses.native: 觸感乾燥粗糙（例如像石灰）

examples.text: My German is very meager.
examples.translation: 我的德國語非常貧乏。

examples.text: The pay was meager.
examples.translation: 薪水微薄。

examples.text: The pay is meager.
examples.translation: 薪水微薄。

examples.text: He fleeced three old ladies of their meager pensions.
examples.translation: 他從三位老婦人那裡剝削了微薄的養老金。

examples.text: You have a meager vocabulary.
examples.translation: 你的詞彙量很貧乏。

examples.text: Fadil wasn't satisfied with meager wages.
examples.translation: 法迪爾對微薄的薪資並不滿意。

etymology.text: From Middle English megre, from Anglo-Norman megre, Old French maigre, from Latin macer, from Proto-Indo-European *mh₂ḱrós. Akin, through the Indo-European root, to Old English mæġer (“meager, lean”), West Frisian meager (“meager”), Dutch mager (“meager”), German mager, Old Norse magr whence the Icelandic magur,
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 megre，來自盎格魯諾曼語 megre，古法語 maigre，拉丁語 macer，印歐語系 *mh₂ḱrós。與古英語 mæġer（貧瘠、瘦）、西弗里斯蘭語 meager（貧瘠）、荷蘭語 mager（貧瘠）、德語 mager 及古諾斯語 magr 同源，由此衍生出冰島語 magur。

senses.definition: To lay or place; to put (one thing to another)
To put to use; to use or employ for a particular purpose, or in a particular case
To submit oneself as a candidate (with the adposition "to" or "at" designating the recipient of the submission, and the adposition "for" designating the position).
To make use of, declare, or pronounce, as suitable, fitting, or relevant.
To put closely; to join; to engage and employ diligently or with attention.
To work diligently and attentively.
To address oneself; to refer.
To pertain or be relevant.
To busy; to keep at work; to ply.
To visit.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: I applied for a summer internship.
examples.translation: 我應徵了一個暑期實習。

examples.text: This still applies to him.
examples.translation: 那對他依然奏效。

examples.text: Tom applied for the job.
examples.translation: 湯姆申請了這份工作。

examples.text: In order to apply, you have to go in person.
examples.translation: 要申請的話，你得親自去。

examples.text: What Tom said doesn't apply in this situation.
examples.translation: 湯姆所言不符時局。

examples.text: I haven't decided which job to apply for.
examples.translation: 我還沒確定找哪份工作。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English aplien, borrowed from Old French applier, from Latin applicō, from ad- + plicō (“fold; arrive”). See applicant, ply.

senses.definition: Alternative spelling of appley.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: You can't apply this rule to every case.
examples.translation: 你不能把這規則應用在所有事上。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English aplien, borrowed from Old French applier, from Latin applicō, from ad- + plicō (“fold; arrive”). See applicant, ply.

senses.definition: To grasp or grip.
To contain or store.
To have and keep possession of something.
To reserve.
To cause to wait or delay.
To halt or delay (medication) temporarily.
To detain.
To be or remain valid; to apply (usually in the third person).
To keep oneself in a particular state.
To impose restraint upon; to limit in motion or action; to bind legally or morally; to confine; to restrain.

examples.text: Brian is holding Kate's hands.
examples.translation: 布萊恩正握著凱特的手。

examples.text: She was holding a small parasol in her hand.
examples.translation: 她手裡握著一把小陽傘。

examples.text: The moment I see dessert, I can't hold back.
examples.translation: 一看到甜點，我就無法自拔。

examples.text: You're holding the book upside-down. This is upside-down and this is right-side up.
examples.translation: 你把書拿反了，這是反面，這才是正面。

examples.text: Holding a conversation with her feels like walking across a minefield.
examples.translation: 跟她談話就像穿過雷區。

examples.text: The proposition holds.
examples.translation: 這個提案成立。

etymology.text: Derived from Middle English holden, derived from Old English healdan, derived from Proto-West Germanic *haldan, derived from Proto-Germanic *haldaną (“to tend, herd”), maybe derived from Proto-Indo-European *kel- (“to drive”). Doublet of halt.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 holden，來自古英語 healdan，源自古西日耳曼語 *haldan，源自古德語 *haldaną（意為「放牧、照料」），可能源自印歐語系 *kel-（意為「驅馭」）。為 halt 的同源詞。

senses.definition: The act of surveying; a general view.
A particular view; an examination, especially an official examination, of a particular group of items, in order to ascertain the condition, quantity, or quality.
The operation of finding the contour, dimensions, position, or other particulars of any part of the Earth's surface.
An examination of the opinions and/or information of a group of people.
A measured plan and description of any portion of country.
A questionnaire or similar instrument used for examining the opinions and/or information of a group of people.
An auction at which a farm is let for a lease for lives.
A district for the collection of customs under a particular officer.

examples.text: She interprets the survey results.
examples.translation: 她解讀調查結果。

examples.text: He drew his conclusions based on that survey.
examples.translation: 他根據這份調查得出了結論。

examples.text: A recent survey shows that the number of smokers is decreasing.
examples.translation: 最近的一項調查顯示吸菸的人數減少了。

examples.text: According to the latest survey, 99% of employees want a free iPad.
examples.translation: 根據最新的調查，99%的員工想要一個免費的iPad。

examples.text: A survey shows that many businessmen skip lunch.
examples.translation: 調查顯示，許多商人忽略午餐。

examples.text: He surveys the population for data.
examples.translation: 他為收集資料而調查人口。

etymology.text: From Middle English surveyen, from Old French sourveoir, surveer (“to oversee”), from sour-, sur- (“over”) + veoir, veeir (“to see”), from Latin videre. See sur- and vision. Related to supervision.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 surveyen，來自古法文 sourveoir、surveer（意為「監督」），由 sour-、sur-（意為「超越」）+ veoir、veeir（意為「看見」）構成，源自拉丁文 videre。見 sur- 與 vision。與 supervision 相關。

senses.definition: The act of seeing or looking at something.
The range of vision.
Something to look at, such as scenery.
An individual viewing of a web page or a video etc. by a user.
A picture, drawn or painted; a sketch.
A mental image.
A way of understanding something, an opinion, a theory.
A point of view.
An intention or prospect.
A virtual or logical table composed of the result set of a query in relational databases.
Appearance; show; aspect.

examples.text: Do you have a table with a view of the ocean?

senses.definition: The sense or faculty by which objects are perceived through the agency of light; the sense by which we see.
Something seen.
Something worth seeing; a spectacle, either good or bad.
A device used in aiming a projectile, through which the person aiming looks at the intended target; see also in one's sights.
An act, instance, opportunity or possibility of seeing; the perception of objects by the eye; view (see also idiomatic expressions such as in sight, out of sight, catch sight of, etc.)
senses.native: 看見、視察；眼睛感知物體的能力；景象

senses.definition: A small aperture through which objects are to be seen, and by which their direction is settled or ascertained.
senses.native: 用於觀察物體並確定其方向的狹小孔洞

senses.definition: a great deal, a lot; frequently used to intensify a comparative.
senses.native: 很多、許多；常用於加強比較級語氣

senses.definition: In a drawing, picture, etc., that part of the surface, as of paper or canvas, which is within the frame or the border or margin. In a frame, the open space, the opening.
senses.native: 畫作或紙張上位於邊框內的部分；相框中的開口

senses.definition: The instrument of seeing; the eye.
Mental view; opinion; judgment.

examples.text: The bird disappeared from my sight.
examples.translation: 鳥兒從我的視線中消失了。

examples.text: She attracted me at first sight.
examples.translation: 我對她一見鐘情。

examples.text: Switzerland boasts many sights.
examples.translation: 瑞士有很多景點。

examples.text: There's still no end in sight.
examples.translation: 還是看不見盡頭。

examples.text: There's not a cloud in sight.
examples.translation: 連一個雲朵都沒有。

examples.text: Did you fall in love with her at first sight?
examples.translation: 你對她是不是一見鍾情？

etymology.text: From Middle English sighte, from Old English sihþ (“something seen; vision”), from Proto-West Germanic *sihti (“seeing, sight”), equivalent to see + -t.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 sighte，來自古英語 sihþ（「所見之物；視覺」），等同於 see 加上 -t 詞綴。

senses.definition: A rapidly executed freehand drawing that is not intended as a finished work, often consisting of a multitude of overlapping lines.
A brief musical composition or theme, especially for the piano.
A rough design, plan, or draft, as a rough draft of a book.
senses.native: 粗略的草圖、計畫或草稿，例如書稿的初稿

senses.definition: A brief description of a person or account of an incident; a general presentation or outline.
senses.native: 對人物的簡短描述或事件經過的敘述；一般性的介紹或大綱

senses.definition: A brief, light, or informal literary composition, such as an essay or short story.
senses.native: 一篇輕盈、隨意或非正式的文學作品，例如散文或短篇小說

senses.definition: An amusing person.
A lookout; vigilant watch for something.
senses.native: 警戒者；對某事的警惕監視

senses.definition: A humorous newspaper article summarizing political events, making heavy use of metaphor, paraphrase and caricature.
senses.native: 一篇幽默的新聞文章，總結政治事件，大量運用比喻、改寫和漫畫風格

senses.definition: A formal specification of a mathematical structure or a data type described in terms of a graph and diagrams (and cones (and cocones)) on it. It can be implemented by means of “models”, which are functors which are graph homomorphisms from the formal specification to categories such that the diagrams become commutative, the cones become limiting (i.e., products), the cocones become colimiting (i.e., sums).
senses.native: 一種數學結構或資料類型的正式規格，以圖形和圖表（以及錐體與反錐體）描述之；可透過函子實現，使圖形成為可交換、錐體成為極限積、反錐體成為極限餘

examples.text: Jiro made a sketch of Mt. Fuji.
examples.translation: 次郎畫了一幅富士山的素描。

examples.text: This sketch is representative of Tom's style.
Tom ripped a page out of his sketch book.
examples.translation: 湯姆從他的繪畫本上撕下了一頁。

examples.text: I have to write a character sketch for a novel study.

etymology.text: From Dutch schets or German Skizze, from Italian schizzo, from Latin schedium, from Ancient Greek σχέδιος (skhédios, “made suddenly, off-hand”), from σχεδόν (skhedón, “near, nearby”), from ἔχω (ékhō, “to hold”). Compare scheme.

senses.definition: The action of looking; an attempt to see.

examples.text: Judging from the look of the sky, it is likely to rain.
examples.translation: 看看天的樣子，要下雨了。

senses.definition: To notice or view, especially carefully or with attention to detail.
To follow or obey the custom, practice, or rules (especially of a religion).
To take note of and celebrate (a holiday or similar occurrence), to keep; to follow (a type of time or calendar reckoning).
To comment on something; to make an observation.

examples.text: They will observe it.
examples.translation: 他們會觀察它。

senses.definition: To deliberately not listen or pay attention to.
To pretend to not notice someone or something.
Fail to notice.
Not to know.

pronunciations.attribution: Self, recorded using the program Shtooka.

examples.text: He ignored our repeated warnings.
examples.translation: 他不顧我們的一再勸告。

examples.text: He ignored all of our warnings.
examples.translation: 他不顧我們的一再勸告。

examples.text: She ignored all my warnings.
examples.translation: 她忽視了我所有的警告。

examples.text: The warnings were ignored.
examples.translation: 警告被忽視。

examples.text: Why are you ignoring me?
examples.translation: 為什麼你不理我？

examples.text: I have a feeling I'm being ignored.
examples.translation: 我有一種我被忽略了的感覺。

etymology.text: From French ignorer, from Latin ignōrō (“to have no knowledge of, mistake, take no notice of, ignore”), from ignārus (“not knowing”), from in- (“not”) + gnārus (“knowing”), from gnōscō, nōscō; see know.

senses.definition: To discharge; to end the employment or service of.
To order to leave.
To dispel; to rid one’s mind of.
To reject; to refuse to accept.
To invalidate; to treat as unworthy of serious consideration.
senses.native: 駁回；視為不值得認真考慮

senses.definition: To send or put away, to discard with disregard, contempt or disdain. (sometimes followed by as).
To get a batsman out.
To give someone a red card; to send off.

examples.text: Lucy dismissed what Mary was saying.
examples.translation: 露西不理會瑪麗所說的話。

examples.text: They were dismissed from their jobs.
examples.translation: 他們被從工作中解僱了。

examples.text: He was dismissed by the boss of the factory.
examples.translation: 他被工廠的老闆解僱。

examples.text: The secretary was dismissed.
examples.translation: 秘書被炒了。

examples.text: Henry was dismissed by reason of his old age.
examples.translation: 亨利因年事已高而被解僱。

examples.text: The possibility of a lack of connection between the events can be dismissed immediately.
examples.translation: 可以立即排除事件之間缺乏關聯的可能性

relations.native: 點燃（某物，通常是建築物）

etymology.text: Middle English, from Latin dimissus (“sent away, dismissed, banished”), perfect passive participle of dīmittō (“send away, dismiss”), from dis- + mittere (“to send”).
etymology.native: 源於拉丁語，意為「被遣送」，由前綴 dis- 與動詞 mittere（發送）組成。

senses.definition: To ignore; to pay no attention to.

examples.text: Donald disregarded Jessica's recommendations.
examples.translation: 唐納德忽略賈絲貝拉的建議。

examples.text: He disregarded his father's advice.
examples.translation: 他不顧他父親的忠告。

examples.text: He disregarded my advice.
examples.translation: 他不顧我的忠告。

examples.text: Disregarding the "No Entry" sign, she pushed open the door and walked inside.
examples.translation: 無視於「 禁止進入」 的牌子，她推開了門走進去。

etymology.text: From dis- + regard. Compare misregard.
etymology.native: 由 dis- 與 regard 組成。可與 misregard 相比。

senses.definition: To look at, see, or view for a period of time.
To observe over a period of time; to notice or pay attention.

examples.text: My little brother is watching television.
examples.translation: 我弟弟在看電視。

examples.text: We enjoyed watching the baseball game.
examples.translation: 我們喜歡看棒球比賽。

examples.text: Because they're watching television.
examples.translation: 因為他們正在看電視。

examples.text: Have you watched television tonight?
examples.translation: 你今晚看電視了嗎？

examples.text: I feel like everybody's watching me.
examples.translation: 我感覺大家都在關注我。

examples.text: Tom told me not to waste my time watching TV.
examples.translation: 湯姆叫我不要浪費時間看電視。

etymology.text: As a noun, from Middle English wacche, from Old English wæċċe. See below for verb form.

senses.definition: The quality or degree of being useful.

pronunciations.attribution: YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/embed/ei3C8P0XBWk – View/save archived versions on archive.org

examples.text: Usefulness must be combined with pleasantness.
examples.translation: 實用性必須與愉悅感結合。

examples.text: He's sceptical about astrology's usefulness.
examples.translation: 他對占星術的實用性持懷疑態度。

examples.text: People don't understand the usefulness of uselessness.
examples.translation: 人們不理解無用之物的實用性。

examples.text: The usefulness of a pot is in its emptiness.
examples.translation: 鍋的實用性在於它的空虛。

examples.text: He has doubts regarding astrology's usefulness.
examples.translation: 他對占星術的實用性存疑。

examples.text: Friendship is sometimes just a synonym of usefulness.
examples.translation: 友情有時只是實用性的同義詞。

etymology.text: From useful + -ness.

senses.definition: Facts or observations presented in support of an assertion.
Anything admitted by a court to prove or disprove alleged matters of fact in a trial.
One who bears witness.
A body of objectively verifiable facts that are positively indicative of, and/or exclusively concordant with, that one conclusion over any other.

examples.text: I destroyed all the evidence.
examples.translation: 我摧毀了所有的證據。

examples.text: I need evidence.
examples.translation: 我需要證據。

examples.text: The prosecutor withheld exculpatory evidence.
examples.translation: 檢方隱匿了有利於被告的證據。

examples.text: Do you have any evidence that really happened?
examples.translation: 你有證據證明那真的發生了嗎？

examples.text: The police assembled a lot of evidence against him.
examples.translation: 警察收集了很多對他不利的證據。

examples.text: The evidence was in his favor.
examples.translation: 證據對他有利。

etymology.text: From Middle English evidence, from Old French [Term?], from Latin evidentia (“clearness, in Late Latin a proof”), from evidens (“clear, evident”); see evident.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 evidence，來自古法文 [Term?]，源自拉丁文 evidentia（「清晰」，晚期拉丁文意為「證據」），來自 evidens（「清晰、明顯」）；見 evident。

senses.definition: To provide evidence for, or suggest the truth of.

examples.text: She was furious, as evidenced by her slamming the door.
examples.translation: 她非常氣憤，從她砰然關門的動作可見一斑。

etymology.text: From Middle English evidence, from Old French [Term?], from Latin evidentia (“clearness, in Late Latin a proof”), from evidens (“clear, evident”); see evident.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 evidence，來自古法文 [Term?]，源自拉丁文 evidentia（「清晰」，晚期拉丁文意為「證據」），來自 evidens（「清晰、明顯」）；見 evident。

senses.definition: A visible fact that shows that something exists or may happen.
A mark or another symbol used to represent something.
A clearly visible object, generally flat, bearing a short message in words or pictures.
Positive or negative polarity, as denoted by the + or - sign.
A specific gesture or motion used to communicate by those with speaking or hearing difficulties; now specifically, a linguistic unit in sign language equivalent to word in spoken languages.
An omen.
A property of the body that indicates a disease and, unlike a symptom, can be detected objectively by someone other than the patient.
Physical evidence left by an animal.
A wonder; miracle; prodigy.
An astrological sign.

examples.text: Don't forget to sign your name.
examples.translation: 不要忘記簽上你的名字。

examples.text: Could you sign here, please?
examples.translation: 請你在這裡簽名好嗎？

examples.text: Tom forgot to sign his name.
examples.translation: 湯姆忘記簽名了。

examples.text: Do you think it's a sign?
examples.translation: 你認為這是箇預兆嗎？

examples.text: All the signs are that she is getting better.
examples.translation: 一切的跡象都表示她的狀況有所改善。

examples.text: Red, as opposed to green, is a sign of danger.
examples.translation: 紅色是危險的標誌，與綠色相對。

etymology.text: From Middle English signe, sygne, syng, seine, sine, syne, from Old English seġn (“sign; mark; token”) and Old French signe, seing (“sign; mark; signature”); both from Latin signum (“a mark; sign; token”); root uncertain. Doublet of signum and signal. Partially displaced native token.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 signe, sygne, syng, seine, sine, syne，來自古英語 seġn（「標記；符號」）及古法語 signe, seing（「標記；簽名」）；皆源自拉丁文 signum（「標記；符號」）；詞源不明。為 signum 與 signal 的同源詞，部分取代原生詞「token」。

senses.definition: present participle and gerund of mean

etymology.text: From Middle English mening, menyng, equivalent to mean + -ing. Cognate with Scots mening (“intent, purpose, sense, meaning”), West Frisian miening (“opinion, mind”), Dutch mening (“view, opinion, judgement”), German Meinung (“opinion, view, mind, idea”), Danish and Swedish mening (“meaning, sense, sentence, opinion”), Icelandic meining (“meaning”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 mening、menyng，意為 mean + -ing。與蘇格蘭語 mening（意為「意圖、目的、意義」）、西弗里斯蘭語 miening（意為「意見、心思」）、荷蘭語 mening（意為「觀點、意見、判斷」）、德語 Meinung（意為「意見、觀點、心思、想法」）、丹麥語與瑞典語 mening（意為「意義、語意、句子、意見」）、冰島語 meining（意為「意義」）同源。

senses.definition: Having a (specified) intention.
Expressing some intention or significance; meaningful.

examples.text: I can't understand this sign's meaning.

etymology.text: From Middle English mening, menyng, equivalent to mean + -ing. Cognate with Scots mening (“intent, purpose, sense, meaning”), West Frisian miening (“opinion, mind”), Dutch mening (“view, opinion, judgement”), German Meinung (“opinion, view, mind, idea”), Danish and Swedish mening (“meaning, sense, sentence, opinion”), Icelandic meining (“meaning”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 mening、menyng，意為 mean + -ing。與蘇格蘭語 mening（意為「意圖、目的、意義」）、西弗里斯蘭語 miening（意為「意見、心思」）、荷蘭語 mening（意為「觀點、意見、判斷」）、德語 Meinung（意為「意見、觀點、心思、想法」）、丹麥語與瑞典語 mening（意為「意義、語意、句子、意見」）、冰島語 meining（意為「意義」）同源。

senses.definition: To form into the shape of a cup, particularly of the hands.

examples.text: Would you care for another cup of coffee?
examples.translation: 再來一杯咖啡怎麼樣？

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English cuppe, coppe, from the merger of Old English cuppe (“cup”) and Old English copp (“cup, vessel”).

senses.definition: A hollow place or cavity; an excavation; a pit; a dent; a depression; a fissure.
An opening that goes all the way through a solid body, a fabric, etc.; a perforation; a rent.
senses.native: 貫穿實體、布料等的開口；穿孔；裂口

senses.definition: A subsurface standard-size hole, also called cup, hitting the ball into which is the object of play. Each hole, of which there are usually eighteen as the standard on a full course, is located on a prepared surface, called the green, of a particular type grass.
senses.native: 標準尺寸的地下孔洞，俗稱果壘，目標是將球打入其中。通常一輪標準球場有十八個這樣的孔洞，位於特定草皮稱為果嶺的準備表面上

senses.definition: The part of a game in which a player attempts to hit the ball into one of the holes.
senses.native: 遊戲中玩家嘗試將球打入其中一個孔洞的部分

senses.definition: The rear portion of the defensive team between the shortstop and the third baseman.
senses.native: 防守隊後方短外野手與三壘手之間的區域

senses.definition: A square on the board, with some positional significance, that a player does not, and cannot in the future, control with a friendly pawn.
senses.native: 棋盤上的一個方格，具有位置意義，玩家目前無法控制且未來也不能用己方兵控制的方格

senses.definition: A card (also called a hole card) dealt face down thus unknown to all but its holder; the status in which such a card is.
senses.native: 背面朝下發給玩家的紙牌（亦稱暗牌），僅持有者所知；此類紙牌的狀態

senses.definition: In the game of fives, part of the floor of the court between the step and the pepperbox.
senses.native: 五人遊戲中，位於階梯與胡椒盒之間的場地部分

senses.definition: An excavation pit or trench.
A weakness; a flaw or ambiguity.

examples.text: The mouse ran into the hole.
examples.translation: 這隻老鼠跑進洞裡。

examples.text: They are digging a hole.
examples.translation: 他們正在挖一個洞。

examples.text: They're digging a hole.
examples.translation: 他們正在挖一個洞。

examples.text: The runner jumped over the hole in the ground.
examples.translation: 那個賽跑運動員躍過了地面上的洞。

examples.text: Time ticks by more slowly around a black hole.
examples.translation: 黑洞周圍的時間要流逝得慢得多。

examples.text: Time passes more slowly around a black hole.

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English hole, hol, from Old English hol (“orifice, hollow place, cavity”), from Proto-West Germanic *hol (“hole”), from Proto-Germanic *hulą (“hollow space, cavity”), noun derivative of Proto-Germanic *hulaz (“hollow”), which is of uncertain ultimate origin. Related to hollow.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 hole、hol，來自古英語 hol（「開口、空洞處」），源自西日耳曼語族 *hol（「孔」），源自原始日耳曼語 *hulą（「空洞空間」），為原始日耳曼語 *hulaz（「空洞」）的名詞派生詞，其最終來源不明。與 hollow 相關。

senses.definition: An item of furniture used to sit on or in, comprising a seat, legs or wheels, back, and sometimes arm rests, for use by one person.
The post or position of chairperson.
The seating position of a particular musician in an orchestra.
A cast-iron component used on railways to support bullhead rails and secure them to the sleepers.
One of two possible conformers of cyclohexane rings (the other being boat), shaped roughly like a chair.
A distinguished professorship at a university.
A vehicle for one person; either a sedan borne upon poles, or a two-wheeled carriage drawn by one horse; a gig.
The seat or office of a person in authority, such as a judge or bishop.
An assigned position in a beauty salon or barbershop.

etymology.text: From Middle English chayere, chayer, chayre, from Old French chaiere, chaere, from Latin cathedra (“seat”), from Ancient Greek καθέδρα (kathédra), from κατά (katá, “down”) + ἕδρα (hédra, “seat”). Partially displaced native stool and settle, which now have more specialised senses. Doublet of cathedra and chaise.

senses.definition: To act as chairperson at; to preside over.
To carry in a seated position upon one's shoulders, especially in celebration or victory.
To award a chair to (a winning poet) at a Welsh eisteddfod.
