etymology.text: From Middle English chayere, chayer, chayre, from Old French chaiere, chaere, from Latin cathedra (“seat”), from Ancient Greek καθέδρα (kathédra), from κατά (katá, “down”) + ἕδρα (hédra, “seat”). Partially displaced native stool and settle, which now have more specialised senses. Doublet of cathedra and chaise.

senses.definition: A place or location.
A post of employment; a job.
A status or rank.
An opinion, stand, or stance.
A posture.
A situation suitable to perform some action.
A place on the playing field, together with a set of duties, assigned to a player.
An amount of securities, commodities, or other financial instruments held by a person, firm, or institution.
A commitment, or a group of commitments, such as options or futures, to buy or sell a given amount of financial instruments, such as securities, currencies or commodities, for a given price.
A method of solving a problem by one or two suppositions; also called the rule of trial and error.
The full state of a chess game at any given turn.

examples.text: Competition for the position is very intense.

senses.definition: Something to be sat upon.
A place in which to sit.
The horizontal portion of a chair or other furniture designed for sitting.
A piece of furniture made for sitting, such as a chair, stool, or bench; any improvised place for sitting.
The part of an object or individual (usually the buttocks) directly involved in sitting.
The part of a piece of clothing (usually pants or trousers) covering the buttocks.
A part or surface on which another part or surface rests.
A membership in an organization, particularly a representative body.
The location of a governing body.
An electoral district, especially for a national legislature.
An ejection seat.

examples.text: Please have a seat.

senses.definition: An upholstered seat with a raised back and one or two raised ends, long enough to comfortably accommodate two or more people.
A raised area of a building's floor, usually covered with carpeting, used for sitting.
A slave soldier who served in the army of the Mali Empire.

examples.text: It's just there on the sofa.

examples.text: I'm sitting on the sofa.
examples.translation: 我坐在沙發上。

etymology.text: Borrowed from French sofa, ultimately from Arabic صُفَّة (ṣuffa, “a long seat made of stone or brick, covered with rich carpets and cushions and used for sitting”). Cognate with Aramaic צפא/Classical Syriac ܨܦܬܐ (ṣipā’, ṣeppəṯā, “mat, matting”). The word may have entered European languages via Muslim Iberia or through Turkish.
etymology.native: 「sofa」源自法語，最終來自阿拉伯語 صُفَّة (ṣuffa)，意為「用石或磚製成的長椅，鋪有絨毯與靠墊」。此詞亦與阿拉姆語 צפא 及古典敘利亞語 ܨܦܬܐ (ṣipā’, ṣeppəṯā) 同源，意為「墊子」。此詞可能經穆斯林伊比里亞半島或土耳其傳入歐洲語言。

senses.definition: A seat for one person without a back or armrests.
A footstool.
A seat with a back; a chair.
A throne.
A royal seat; a chief's throne.
A plant that has been cut down until its main stem is close to the ground, resembling a stool, to promote new growth.
A close-stool; a seat used for urination and defecation: a chamber pot, commode, outhouse seat, or toilet.
Feces; excrement.
A production of feces or excrement; an act of defecation, stooling.
A small channel on the side of a vessel, for the deadeyes of the backstays.
Material, such as oyster shells, spread on the sea bottom for oyster spat to adhere to.

examples.text: This stool needs to be repaired.

etymology.text: From Middle English stool, from Old English stōl (“chair, seat”), from Proto-West Germanic *stōl, from Proto-Germanic *stōlaz (“chair”), from Proto-Indo-European *stoh₂los (“frame, rack, stand”), from *steh₂- (“to stand”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 stool，來自古英語 stōl（意為「椅子、座位」），源自原始西日耳曼語 *stōl，再溯源自原始日耳曼語 *stōlaz（意為「椅子」），更上溯源自原始印歐語 *stoh₂los（意為「框架、支架」），來自 *steh₂-（意為「站立」）

senses.definition: A chair with supports for the arms or elbows.
An upholstered chair without armrests intended for the living room
A position from which a casual and inexpert perspective looks out on the world.

senses.definition: To divide (a thing) into separate parts.
To disunite from a group or mass; to disconnect.
To cause (things or people) to be separate.
To divide itself into separate pieces or substances.
To set apart; to select from among others, as for a special use or service.

examples.text: Separate the remaining pieces by color.
Separate the articles from the headings.
If the kids get too noisy, separate them for a few minutes.
The sauce will separate if you don't keep stirring.
He separated the fighting children.

etymology.text: From Middle English separaten (“to separate”), from separat (“separated”) + -en, from Latin sēparātus, perfect passive participle of sēparō (“to separate”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from sē- (“apart”) + parō (“prepare”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *per- (“produce, procure, bring forward, bring forth”). Displaced Middle English scheden, from Old English scēadan (whence English shed).

senses.definition: To furnish with one or more sofas.
To seat or lay down on a sofa.

etymology.text: Borrowed from French sofa, ultimately from Arabic صُفَّة (ṣuffa, “a long seat made of stone or brick, covered with rich carpets and cushions and used for sitting”). Cognate with Aramaic צפא/Classical Syriac ܨܦܬܐ (ṣipā’, ṣeppəṯā, “mat, matting”). The word may have entered European languages via Muslim Iberia or through Turkish.
etymology.native: 「sofa」源自法語，最終來自阿拉伯語 صُفَّة (ṣuffa)，意為「用石或磚製成的長椅，鋪有絨毯與靠墊」。此詞亦與阿拉姆語 צפא 及古典敘利亞語 ܨܦܬܐ (ṣipā’, ṣeppəṯā) 同源，意為「墊子」。此詞可能經穆斯林伊比里亞半島或土耳其傳入歐洲語言。

A piece of furniture holding one or more electric light sockets.
An eye.

etymology.text: From Middle English laumpe, lampe, from Old French lampe (“lamp, light”), from Latin lampas (“torch, lamp, light”), from Ancient Greek λαμπάς (lampás, “torch, lamp, beacon, light, meteor”), from Proto-Indo-European *leh₂p- (“to shine”). senses.definition: A collection of sheets of paper bound together to hinge at one edge, containing printed or written material, pictures, etc.

A long work fit for publication, typically prose, such as a novel or textbook, and typically published as such a bound collection of sheets, but now sometimes electronically as an e-book.
A major division of a long work.
A bookmaker (a person who takes bets on sporting events and similar); bookie; turf accountant.
A convenient collection, in a form resembling a book, of small paper items for individual use.
The script of a musical or opera.
Records of the accounts of a business.
A book award, a recognition for receiving the highest grade in a class (traditionally an actual book, but recently more likely a letter or certificate acknowledging the achievement).
Six tricks taken by one side.
Four of a kind.

etymology.text: From Middle English bok, book, from Old English bōc, from Proto-West Germanic *bōk, from Proto-Germanic *bōks. Bookmaker sense by clipping.
etymology.native: 「book」源自中世英文 bok，來自古英文 bōc，再溯源自原始西日耳曼語 *bōk，更上溯至原始日耳曼語 *bōks。其「賭博」義項則由剪切形成。

senses.definition: A set of items or amount of material procured, gathered or presented together.

senses.definition: A playing card.
Any game using playing cards; a card game.
A resource or argument, used to achieve a purpose. (See play the something card.)
Any flat, normally rectangular piece of stiff paper, plastic, etc.
A bank card.
Any electronic payment (rather than a cash payment using notes, bills or coins).

etymology.native: 此詞源自荷蘭語 landschap 的變體，而 landschap 又來自中世紀荷蘭語 landscap、lantscap，源自古荷蘭語 *landskepi、*landskapi，意為「地區、區域」；亦可追溯至古英語 landsċipe、landsċeap，意為「地區、區域」；在部分語義上亦與蘇格蘭語 landskape、landskep、landskip、弗里斯蘭語 lânskip、低德語 landschop 相關。

senses.definition: A telecommunication device which converts data or sounds (usually speech) into electrical signals which are then transmitted to enable two or more people to communicate with each other over a distance; now usually a device having a dial or keypad with numerals for entering a number, etc., to connect with a person, and means (such as a sound or vibration) for alerting one to an incoming call or transmission; also, the handset or receiver of such a device.
A means of communicating information from one person to another or others.
Now chiefly preceded by a descriptive word: a simple communication device which converts sounds (usually speech) into mechanical vibrations along a string, wire, etc.
A type of foghorn used for sending signals in the form of loud tones or musical notes, especially one invented in the 19th century by John Taylor, a captain in the British Royal Navy.

A communication device consisting of two aligned gutta-percha speaking tubes connected to parabolic reflectors which allows speech spoken into one tube to be sent through the air to the other one, invented in the 19th century by the British engineer Francis Whishaw (1804–1856); also, a speaking tube of such a device.
A system of communication using musical notes, also known as Solresol, invented in 1828 by the French composer Jean-François Sudre (1787–1862).

Synonym of Chinese whispers (“a game for several players in which a phrase, whispered by each person in turn to their neighbour, is often unwittingly misunderstood as it is transferred, to humorous effect by the time it reaches the last person and is compared with the original phrase; (figurative) a situation where something is changed or misunderstood as a result of passing through successive people or processes”).

etymology.text: The noun is derived from tele- (prefix meaning ‘from a distance’) + -phone (suffix denoting a device which makes a sound), modelled after German Telephon (“early apparatus converting sound into electrical signals”) (dated) (now German Telefon). The word was first used to refer to the modern device in 1876 by the Scottish-born Canadian-American engineer Alexander Graham Bell (1847–1922).
etymology.native: 這個名詞源自 tele-（表示「從遠處」的前綴）＋ -phone（表示「發出聲音的裝置」的後綴），仿照德語 Telephon（「早期將聲音轉換為電信號的裝置」）（舊用語）（現為德語 Telefon）。1876年，蘇格蘭出生的加拿大裔美國工程師亞歷山大·格雷厄姆·貝爾（1847–1922）首次用此詞指稱現代裝置。

An image used in whole or in part as a trademark or service mark.
An image or logo denoting official or proprietary authority or provenience.
Any specific class of wordplay element in a cryptic crossword.
Power of devising; invention; contrivance.
A spectacle or show.
Opinion; decision.

The only sure cognates are Saterland Frisian Koai (“key”), West Frisian kaai (“key”), and North Frisian kai, koie (“key”). senses.definition: (uncountable) A heavy yellow elemental metal of great value, with atomic number 79.
A coin or coinage made of this material, or supposedly so.
A deep yellow colour, resembling the metal gold.
A gold medal.
The bullseye of an archery target.
Anything or anyone that is very valuable.
A grill (jewellery worn on front teeth) made of gold.

examples.text: Who do you think will win the gold medal?
examples.translation: 你們覺得誰會贏金牌？

examples.text: The color of gold is very similar to brass.
examples.translation: 金的顏色和黃銅很相似。

examples.text: That food mixer you gave me is absolute gold, mate!
examples.translation: 你給我那個食物攪拌機真是絕了，夥計！

etymology.text: From Middle English gold, from Old English gold (“gold”), from Proto-West Germanic *golþ, from Proto-Germanic *gulþą (“gold”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰl̥h₃tóm (“gold”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰelh₃- (“green, yellow”). Related to yellow; see there for more. Germanic cognates include Scots gowd, Dutch goud, German Gold, Faroese, Icelandic, Norwegian Bokmål, and Norwegian Nynorsk gull, Danish and Swedish guld, and cognates from other Indo-European languages include Latvian zelts, Russian зо
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 gold，來自古英語 gold（「金」），源自日耳曼語族原初 *golþ，來自日耳曼語族原初 *gulþą（「金」），源自印歐語系原初 *ǵʰl̥h₃tóm（「金」），源自印歐語系原初 *ǵʰelh₃-（「綠、黃」）。與黃色相關；詳見該詞。日耳曼語族同源詞包括蘇格蘭語 gowd、荷蘭語 goud、德語 Gold、法羅語、冰島語、挪威書面語和挪威新挪威語 gull、丹麥語和瑞典語 guld，以及來自其他印歐語言的同源詞包括拉脫維亞語 zelts、俄語 зо

senses.definition: A hard, generally yellow to brown translucent or transparent fossil resin from extinct coniferous trees of the pine genus, used for jewellery, decoration and later dissolved as a binder in varnishes. One variety, blue amber, appears blue rather than yellow under direct sunlight.
A yellow-orange colour.
The intermediate light in a set of three traffic lights, which when illuminated indicates that drivers should stop when safe to do so. See also yellow light.
The stop codon (nucleotide triplet) "UAG", or a mutant which has this stop codon at a premature place in its DNA sequence.
Hesitance to proceed, or limited approval to proceed; an amber light.
Ambergris, the waxy product of the sperm whale.
Formerly thought to be the product of a plant.

examples.text: The traffic lights were amber, so we stopped.
Amber preserves insects that get trapped in it.
Maple syrup is an amber liquid.
Amber Heard fought back against her abuser; this is a good thing.
Johnny Depp is on tape admitting to physically abusing Amber Heard.
Look what I've found! A piece of amber!

relations.native: 監獄長；看守人；守護者或巡邏員

etymology.text: From Middle English ambre, aumbre, from Old French aumbre, ambre, from Arabic عَنْبَر (ʕanbar, “ambergris”), from Middle Persian 𐭠𐭭𐭡𐭫 (ʾnbl /⁠ambar⁠/, “ambergris”). Compare English lamber, ambergris. Displaced Middle English smulting (from Old English smelting (“amber”)), Old English eolhsand (“amber”), Old English glær (“amber”), and Old English sāp (“amber, resin, pomade”).

senses.definition: A large and often winding stream which drains a land mass, carrying water down from higher areas to a lower point, oftentimes ending in another body of water, such as an ocean or in an inland sea.
A visually undesirable effect of white space running down a page, caused by spaces between words on consecutive lines happening to coincide.
Any large flow of a liquid in a single body.
senses.native: 單一整體中的液體大規模流動

senses.definition: The last card dealt in a hand.
senses.native: 一手牌中最後發出的牌

senses.definition: One who rives or splits.

examples.text: Children can't swim in this river.
examples.translation: 小孩兒不能在這條河裡游泳。

examples.text: Don't throw stones into the river.
examples.translation: 不要扔石頭到河裡。

examples.text: That river is 300 kilometers long.
examples.translation: 那條河長300公里。

examples.text: We enjoyed swimming in the river.
examples.translation: 我們喜歡在河裡游泳。

examples.text: This river is dangerous to swim in, in July.
examples.translation: 七月份，這條河不適合游泳。

examples.text: It is very important for us to love a river.
examples.translation: 對於我們來說愛惜河川是很重要的。

etymology.text: From Middle English ryver, from Anglo-Norman rivere, from Early Medieval Latin rīpāria (“littoral, riverbank”), from Latin rīpārius (“of a riverbank”), from Latin rīpa (“river bank”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁reyp- (“to scratch, tear, cut”). Unrelated to Latin rīvus (“stream”) (whence rival, derive). Doublet of riviera and rivière. Displaced native Old English ēa.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 ryver，來自盎格魯 - 諾曼語 rivere，再源自早期中世紀拉丁語 rīpāria。

senses.definition: Any of several shrubs or trees of the genus Citrus in the family Rutaceae.

The fruit of such plants, generally spherical, oblate, or prolate, consisting of an outer glandular skin (called zest), an inner white skin (called pith or albedo), and generally between 8 and 16 sectors filled with pulp consisting of cells with one end attached to the inner skin. Citrus fruits include orange, grapefruit, lemon, lime, and citron.
senses.native: 一般呈球形、扁圓形或長圓形的植物果實，由外層腺狀果皮（稱作柑橘皮）、內層白色果皮（稱作中果皮或白肉）以及通常包含 8 至 16 個填充有果肉（細胞一端連接著內層果皮）的扇區組成。柑橘類水果包括橘、葡萄柚、檸檬、青檸和佛手柑

examples.text: We're paying too much for citrus.
examples.translation: 我們為柑橘類水果付了太多錢。

examples.text: Citrus adds a nice tang to a salad dressing.
examples.translation: 柑橘類水果能讓沙拉醬增添一點酸味。

examples.text: Every single citrus tree entering the country is inspected for signs of canker lesions on its leaves and stems.
examples.translation: 進入國境的每一棵柑橘樹都會被檢查其葉片和莖上是否有乾枯病的跡象。

examples.text: Lemons and oranges are types of citrus fruits that grow on trees.
examples.translation: 檸檬和橘是生長在樹上的柑橘類水果類型。

etymology.text: From Latin citrus (“a citron tree, thuja”), probably via Etruscan from Ancient Greek κέδρος (kédros); compare Middle English citurtre, cytyr tre. Thus a possible doublet of cedar.
etymology.native: 源於拉丁語 citrus（指佛手柑樹或雪松），可能經伊特魯西亞語來自古希臘語 κέδρος；與中古英語 citurtre、cytyr tre 相比。因此可能是雪松的雙胞胎詞。

senses.definition: Any color in plant or animal cells.

Wine flavoured with spices and honey.
senses.native: 香料與蜂蜜調味的葡萄酒

examples.text: Adrenochrome is a pigment.
examples.translation: 腺色素是一種顏料。

examples.text: This pigment is the best.
examples.translation: 這種顏料是最好的。

examples.text: Make up has often used carmine as a pigment to achieve bright red shades.
examples.translation: 化妝品常使用胭脂紅作為顏料，以達到鮮豔的紅色調。

examples.text: Yellow is a primary colour of pigments, but not of light; those are only red, green, and blue.
examples.translation: 黃色是顏料的基礎色之一，但並非光的基礎色；光的基礎色僅有紅、綠、藍三色。

examples.text: It is said that Lycopene, a pigment found in tomatoes, makes your skin beautiful and helps you lose weight.
examples.translation: 據說番茄中的葉黃素是一種色素，能使皮膚美麗並幫助減重。

examples.text: Chlorophyll is the pigment responsible for most plants' green colouring.
examples.translation: 葉綠素是負責植物綠色外觀的主要色素。

etymology.text: From Middle English pigment, from Latin pigmentum (“pigment”), itself from pingō (“to paint”) + -mentum; variants of this word may have been known in Old English (e.g. 12th century pyhmentum). Doublet of pimiento, pimento, and piment.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語的 pigment，來自拉丁語 pigmentum（「顏料」），本身由 pingō（「塗抹」）加上 -mentum 構成；此詞的變體可能早在古英語時就已存在（例如 12 世紀的 pyhmentum）。它是 pimiento、pimento 和 piment 的同源詞。

senses.definition: The color of snow or milk; the color of light containing equal amounts of all visible wavelengths.

examples.text: The black telephone costs more than the white.
examples.translation: 黑的電話比白的花錢多。

senses.definition: The colour of the setting sun, blood, and strawberries; the colour which is evoked by the longest visible wavelengths (between about 625–740 nm), and a primary additive colour.

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English red, from Old English rēad, from Proto-West Germanic *raud, from Proto-Germanic *raudaz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rowdʰós, from *h₁rewdʰ- + *-ós.

senses.definition: The color of grass and leaves; a primary additive color midway between yellow and blue which is evoked by light between roughly 495–570 nm.

A putting green, the part of a golf course near the hole.
The surface upon which bowls is played.
One of the color balls used in snooker, with a value of 3 points.
A public patch of land in the middle of a settlement.
A grassy plain; a piece of ground covered with verdant herbage.
Fresh leaves or branches of trees or other plants; wreaths.
Any substance or pigment of a green color.

examples.text: He painted all the walls green.

examples.text: These green leaves turn red or yellow in fall.

examples.text: Is it true Tom wants to paint his house green?

examples.text: A green carpet will not go with this blue curtain.
examples.translation: 綠色的毯子和這條藍色的簾子不配。

examples.text: I hear the grass in England is green even in the winter.

examples.text: The blackbird found a little red worm in the green grass.

senses.definition: The color of sunflower petals and lemons; the color obtained by mixing green and red light, or by subtracting blue from white light; the color evoked by light of wavelength around 580 nm; one of the three primary colors in subtractive color systems.
The middle light in a set of three traffic lights, the lighting of which indicates that drivers should stop short of the intersection if it is safe to do so.
senses.native: 三盞交通燈中的中間一盞，若安全則指示駕駛者在路口前停車

senses.definition: One of the color balls used in snooker, with a value of 2 points.

senses.definition: One of two groups of object balls, or a ball from that group, as used in the principally British version of pool that makes use of unnumbered balls (the yellow(s) and red(s)); contrast stripes and solids in the originally American version with numbered balls).
senses.native: 八球或九球中未編號球組（黃球與紅球）中的一個球；對比美式八球中的彩條球與固體球

senses.definition: A yellow card.
A yellow dye or pigment.
A pen, pencil, crayon, etc., made of yellow pigment.
senses.native: 一種由黃色顏料製成的筆、鉛筆或蠟筆等

senses.definition: Something, or a part of a thing, which is yellow.
senses.native: 任何呈黃色的事物或其一部分

senses.native: 各種科氏蝶屬的其中一種，特別是黃色品種；與硫磺蝶相對比

examples.text: Red, yellow, and blue are colors.
examples.translation: 紅色和黃色和藍色是顏色。

examples.text: These green leaves turn red or yellow in fall.
examples.translation: 這些綠葉到秋天變成紅色或黃色。

examples.translation: 湯姆穿著一件黃色襯衫，繫著一條藍色領帶。

examples.text: I have a lot of flowers. Some are red and some are yellow.
examples.translation: 我種了很多花，有些是紅色的，有些是黃色的。

examples.text: At the end of April, the water of the Yellow River had darkened.
examples.translation: 四月底，黃河的水發黑了。

examples.text: A rainbow consists of red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.

etymology.text: From Middle English yelwe, yelou, from Old English ġeolwe, oblique form of Old English ġeolu, from Proto-West Germanic *gelu, from Proto-Germanic *gelwaz, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰelh₃wós, from *ǵʰelh₃- (“green, yellow”).

senses.definition: An approximately spherical or ellipsoidal body produced by birds, insects, reptiles, and other animals, often housing an embryo within a membrane or shell during its development.
The (usually) non-developing, edible egg (sense 1.1) of a domestic fowl such as a duck, goose, or, especially, chicken; (uncountable) the contents of such an egg or eggs used as food.
A food item shaped to resemble an egg (sense 1.1.1), such as a chocolate egg.
Synonym of ovum (“the female gamete of an animal”); an egg cell.
A thing which looks like or is shaped like an egg (sense 1.1).
A swelling on one's head, usually large or noticeable, resulting from an injury.
Chiefly in egg and dart: an ornamental oval moulding alternating in a row with dart or triangular shapes.
A score of zero; specifically (cricket), a batter's failure to score; a duck egg or duck's egg.
A bomb or mine.
A would-be spark, especially one created by an overweight spaceship and that leads to a pattern's destruction.
A golf ball.

examples.text: Excuse me, where are the eggs?
examples.translation: 請問雞蛋在哪裡？

examples.text: Where did you buy these eggs?
examples.translation: 你從哪兒買的這些蛋？

examples.text: A chicken hatches an egg and a chick emerges.
examples.translation: 母雞孵蛋，孵出小雞。

examples.text: To make a cake, you need egg, butter and sugar.
examples.translation: 要做蛋糕，你要用到雞蛋，奶油和糖。

examples.text: We need flour, sugar and eggs to make this cake.
examples.translation: 我們需要麵粉、砂糖和雞蛋來做這個蛋糕。

examples.text: I can't eat raw eggs; they must be cooked.
examples.translation: 我不能吃生雞蛋。它們必須是熟的。

etymology.text: The noun is derived from Middle English eg, egg, egge (“egg of a domestic or wild fowl; egg of a snake”) [and other forms] (originally Northern England and Northeast Midlands), from Old Norse egg (“egg”), from Proto-Germanic *ajją (“egg”) (by Holtzmann’s law), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ōwyóm (“egg”), probably from *h₂éwis (“bird”), from *h₂ew- (“to consume”). Doublet of huevo, oeuf, and ovum.
etymology.native: 這個名詞源自中古英語 eg, egg, egge（意為「家禽或野鳥的蛋；蛇的蛋」），來自古諾斯語 egg，再溯源自原始日耳曼語 *ajją（意為「蛋」），由原始印歐語 *h₂ōwyóm 來，可能源自 *h₂éwis（意為「鳥」），而 *h₂ew-（意為「食用」）。是 huevo、oeuf 與 ovum 的同源詞。

senses.definition: To throw (especially rotten) eggs (noun sense 1.1.1) at (someone or something).

examples.text: I cannot fry these eggs. They are rotten.
examples.translation: 這些雞蛋壞掉了，不能拿來煎。

etymology.text: The noun is derived from Middle English eg, egg, egge (“egg of a domestic or wild fowl; egg of a snake”) [and other forms] (originally Northern England and Northeast Midlands), from Old Norse egg (“egg”), from Proto-Germanic *ajją (“egg”) (by Holtzmann’s law), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ōwyóm (“egg”), probably from *h₂éwis (“bird”), from *h₂ew- (“to consume”). Doublet of huevo, oeuf, and ovum.
etymology.native: 這個名詞源自中古英語 eg, egg, egge（意為「家禽或野鳥的蛋；蛇的蛋」），來自古諾斯語 egg，再溯源自原始日耳曼語 *ajją（意為「蛋」），由原始印歐語 *h₂ōwyóm 來，可能源自 *h₂éwis（意為「鳥」），而 *h₂ew-（意為「食用」）。是 huevo、oeuf 與 ovum 的同源詞。

senses.definition: To stare intently or earnestly.
To stare at.

examples.text: We gazed at the beautiful scenery.
examples.translation: 我們望著這美麗的風景。

examples.text: The girl was gazing at the doll.
examples.translation: 女孩凝視著洋娃娃。

examples.text: At night, she gazed at the moon.
examples.translation: 她在夜晚望著月亮。

etymology.text: First appears c. 1655, in the English translation Álvaro Semedo’s writings. From Dutch thee, from Hokkien 茶 (tê) (Amoy dialect), from Old Chinese, ultimately from Proto-Sino-Tibetan *s-la (「leaf, tea」). Introduced to English and other Western European languages by the Dutch East India Company, who sourced their tea in Amoy; compare Malay teh along the same trade route. Doublet of chai and cha (and, distantly, the first element of lahpet), from same Proto-Sino-Tibetan root; see discussion of cogn
etymology.native: 最早出現於1655年左右，源自荷蘭人譯本Álvaro Semedo的著作。來自荷蘭語thee，源自 Hokkien 茶（tê）（同安腔），源自古漢語，最終源自原始漢藏語 *s-la（「葉，茶」）。由荷蘭東印度公司引入英文及其他西歐語言，他們從同安供應茶葉；可與馬來語teh 比較，沿同一貿易路線。與chai及cha為同源詞（且遠源與lahpet之首字同源），詳見相關詞源討論。

senses.definition: A conical peg or pin used to close and open the hole or vent in a container.
An object with a tapering conical form like a tap (etymology 1, noun sense 1); specifically, ellipsis of taproot (“long, tapering root of a plant”).
senses.native: 像水龍頭般收縮成錐形的物體（詞源 1，名詞義項 1）；特指主根之省略（「長而細長的植物根部」）

senses.definition: A hollow device used to control the flow of a fluid, such as an alcoholic beverage from a cask, or a gas or liquid in a pipe.
senses.native: 用於控制液體流動的空心裝置，例如從桶中取酒，或管道中的氣體或液體

senses.definition: A procedure that removes fluid from a body cavity; paracentesis.
senses.native: 一種從身體腔體內抽取液體的程序；腹腔穿刺術

senses.definition: Liquor drawn through a tap (etymology 1, noun sense 2.2); hence, a certain kind or quality of liquor; also (figurative, informal), a certain kind or quality of any thing.
senses.native: 透過水龍頭取得的酒（詞源 1，名詞義項 2.2）；因此指某種類型的酒；亦為（比喻、口語）任何事物的某種類型或品質

senses.definition: A device used to listen in secretly on telephone calls or other communications.
senses.native: 用於秘密監聽電話通話或其他通訊的裝置

senses.definition: A secret interception of telephone calls or other communications using such a device; also, a recording of such a communication.
senses.native: 使用該裝置對電話通話或其他通訊進行秘密截獲；亦指該類通訊的錄音

senses.definition: A situation where a borrowing government authority issues bonds over a period of time, usually at a fixed price, with volumes sold on a particular day dependent on market conditions.
senses.native: 一種情況，即借入政府當局在一段時間內發行債券，通常以固定價格出售，每日銷售量取決於市場狀況

senses.definition: A cylindrical tool used to cut an internal screw thread in a hole, with cutting edges around the lower end and an upper end to which a handle is fitted to turn the tool.
senses.native: 用於在孔洞中切割內部螺紋的圓柱形工具，其下端有切削邊緣，上端配有手柄以旋轉該工具

senses.definition: A connection made to an electrical or fluid conductor without breaking it; a tapping.
senses.native: 在不斷開的情況下連接至電氣或液體導體；接駁點

examples.text: The tap is dripping.
examples.translation: 水龍頭在滴水。

examples.text: Mend the tap in the kitchen.
examples.translation: 修理廚房的水龍頭。

examples.text: I’d tap that.
examples.translation: 我會點那個。

examples.text: There's a chance that tap water may contain harmful substances like chlorine and lead.
examples.translation: 自來水有可能含有氯、鉛等有害物質。

examples.text: We don’t have bottled water; you’ll have to get it from the tap.
examples.translation: 我們沒有瓶裝水；你得從水龍頭那裡去拿。

examples.text: Is the tap water here safe to drink?
examples.translation: 這裡的水龍頭水安全嗎？

etymology.text: The noun is derived from Middle English tappe (“hollow device for controlling the flow of liquid from a hole, cock, faucet, spigot; hole through which the liquid flows; the liquid which thus flows”), from Old English tæppa, from Proto-West Germanic *tappō, from Proto-Germanic *tappô (“a plug, tap; peg; tapering stick”), from Proto-Indo-European *deh₂p- (“to lose; to sacrifice”). Doublet of tapa.
etymology.native: 此名詞源於中古英語 tappe（「控制液體從孔洞、龍頭流出的空心裝置；液體流動的孔道；由此流動的液體」），來自古英語 tæppa，源自原始西日耳曼語 *tappō，源自原始日耳曼語 *tappô（「塞子、水龍頭；栓；錐形棍棒」），源自原始印歐語 *deh₂p-（「失去；犧牲」）。與 tapa 為雙胞胎詞。

senses.definition: To fool or trick (someone).
To engage in frivolous behavior; to fool around or waste time.
To hum or sing (a tune) at a low pitch or volume.
To play (a musical instrument or passage of music) or to sing (a passage of music) in an improvisatory or lighthearted manner; also, to play (a series of ornamental notes) on an instrument.

examples.text: Tom has been sitting in the other room noodling on his guitar all afternoon.

etymology.text: Borrowed from Dutch noedel (“noodle”), or from its etymon German Nudel (“piece of pasta, noodle”); further etymology uncertain, probably a variant of Knödel (“dumpling”), from Middle High German knödel (“dumpling; small knot”), and then either:
etymology.native: 源自荷蘭語 noedel（意為「麵條」），或源自其語源德語 Nudel（意為「意麵或麵條」）；更早的來源尚不確定，可能為德語 Knödel（意為「餛飩」），源自中古高地德語 knödel（意為「小結節」），之後可能源自：

senses.definition: A structural element resembling the hollow upper half of a sphere.
Anything shaped like an upset bowl, often used as a cover.
Any erection resembling the dome or cupola of a building, such as the upper part of a furnace, the vertical steam chamber on the top of a boiler, etc.
A prism formed by planes parallel to a lateral axis which meet above in a horizontal edge, like the roof of a house; also, one of the planes of such a form.
A geological feature consisting of symmetrical anticlines that intersect where each one reaches its apex.
A press stud or snap fastener.
A person's head.
head, oral sex
A building; a house; an edifice.

examples.text: She was trapped inside the dome.

senses.definition: To swindle, deceive, or trick.
To duplicate.

examples.text: You were duped by him.
examples.translation: 他讓你上當。

examples.text: You have been duped.
examples.translation: 您被騙了。

examples.text: We've been duped.
examples.translation: 我們被騙了。

examples.text: He was duped by being fed false information.
examples.translation: 他被灌輸錯誤資訊而遭騙了。

examples.text: I was duped into thinking he was trustworthy.
examples.translation: 我被他騙信以為真，認為他很值得信任。

examples.text: Duping Mary should be as easy as a piece of cake.
examples.translation: 欺騙瑪麗應該易如反掌。

etymology.text: From French duper, from Middle French duppe, alteration of huppe (“hoopoe”), from Latin, onomatopoeic.
etymology.native: 源自法語 duper，中法語 duppe，huppe（鴝鵙）的變體，來自拉丁語擬聲詞。

senses.definition: Any of various dishes commonly made by combining liquids, such as water or stock, with other ingredients, such as meat and vegetables, that contribute the food value, flavor, and texture.
A serving of such a dish, typically in a bowl.
The liquid part of such a dish; the broth.
Any mixture or substance suggestive of soup consistency.
Thick fog or cloud (also pea soup).
Nitroglycerine or gelignite, especially when used for safe-cracking.
Dope or cocaine.
Processing chemicals into which film is dipped, such as developer.
A liquid or gelatinous substrate, especially the mixture of organic compounds that is believed to have played a role in the origin of life on Earth.
An unfortunate situation; trouble, problems (a fix, a mess); chaos.
The foamy portion of a wave.

examples.text: She cooked vegetable soup for us.
examples.translation: 她為我們煮了蔬菜湯。

examples.text: I'm eating soup in the kitchen.
examples.translation: 我在廚房裡喝湯。

examples.text: How did you make this soup?
examples.translation: 這湯怎麼做的？

examples.text: There's a hair in my soup.
examples.translation: 我的湯裡有一根頭髮。

examples.text: A good cook doesn't throw out yesterday's soup.
examples.translation: 一個好的廚師不會丟掉昨天的湯。

examples.text: Peas and carrots are common ingredients in soups.
examples.translation: 豌豆和胡蘿蔔是做湯的常見配料。

relations.native: 一次迅速、聰明且極具成功性的行動

etymology.text: The noun is from Middle English soupe, sowpe, from Old French soupe, souppe, sope, from Late Latin suppa (“sopped bread”), from Proto-Germanic *supô (compare Middle Dutch sope (“broth”)). Doublet of sop and zuppa. See also sup and supper.
etymology.native: 這個名詞來自中古英語 soupe、sowpe，源自古法語 soupe、souppe、sope，來源為拉丁語 suppa（意為「泡過的麵包」），再溯自古德語 *supô（可與中世荷蘭語 sope（意為「湯」）相比較）。是 sop 與 zuppa 的同源詞。另見 sup 與 supper。

senses.definition: To feed: to provide with soup or a meal.

etymology.text: The noun is from Middle English soupe, sowpe, from Old French soupe, souppe, sope, from Late Latin suppa (“sopped bread”), from Proto-Germanic *supô (compare Middle Dutch sope (“broth”)). Doublet of sop and zuppa. See also sup and supper.
etymology.native: 這個名詞來自中古英語 soupe、sowpe，源自古法語 soupe、souppe、sope，來源為拉丁語 suppa（意為「泡過的麵包」），再溯自古德語 *supô（可與中世荷蘭語 sope（意為「湯」）相比較）。是 sop 與 zuppa 的同源詞。另見 sup 與 supper。

senses.definition: To affect with drugs.

examples.text: Who are the world doping champions?
examples.translation: 誰是世界的興奮劑冠軍？

examples.text: EPO can be used as a blood doping agent.
examples.translation: EPO 可用作血液興奮劑。

examples.text: I can't compete with somebody who's doping.
examples.translation: 我無法與那些使用興奮劑的人競爭。

examples.text: Doping modifies the electrical characteristics of silicon.
examples.translation: 興奮劑會改變矽電子的特性。

examples.text: An investigation established that the racehorse had been doped.
examples.translation: 調查證實這匹賽馬曾被注射興奮劑。

examples.text: Doping is not compatible with my ideological views on the sport.
examples.translation: 我認為你的碩士論文與我在體育方面的理念不符，因為涉及興奮劑。

morphemes.native: 用於處理表面的潤滑液或糊狀物

etymology.text: From Dutch doop (“thick dipping sauce”), from Dutch dopen (“to dip”), from Middle Dutch dopen, from Old Dutch *dōpen, from Frankish *daupijan, from Proto-Germanic *daupijaną.
etymology.native: 源於荷蘭語 doop（厚醬汁），來自 dopen（浸泡），再追溯至古日耳曼語。

senses.definition: An optional light meal consumed shortly before going to bed.
Any meal eaten in the evening; dinner eaten in the evening, rather than at noon.
A meal from a chip shop consisting of a deep-fried food with chips.
A drinker, especially one who drinks slowly (i.e., one who sups).

examples.text: Whoever gets home first starts cooking the supper.

senses.definition: A wide, flat receptacle used around the house, especially for cooking.
The contents of such a receptacle.
A cylindrical receptacle about as tall as it is wide, with one long handle, usually made of metal, used for cooking in the home.
A deep plastic receptacle, used for washing or food preparation; a basin.
A wide receptacle in which gold grains are separated from gravel by washing the contents with water.
A pond or lake, considered as the expanse of land upon which the water sits.
A dry lake or playa, especially a salt flat.
Synonym of playa lake: a temporary pond or lake in a playa.
Strong adverse criticism.
Synonym of pipe: a channel for lava within a volcano; the cylindrical remains of such channels.

examples.text: He fell out of the frying pan into the fire.
examples.translation: 他真是剛出狼窩又入虎穴。

examples.text: Hopefully things will pan out nicely.
examples.translation: 希望事情能順利解決。

examples.translation: 用紙巾把那口鍋擦乾。

examples.translation: 你蔑視了目睹你罪行的仙女們，也蔑視了我を這位強大的潘神。

examples.translation: 露營時，湯姆沒有徹底清洗鍋碗瓢盆，導致瑪莉得了痢疾。

examples.text: Induction cookers use magnets to directly heat pots and pans.
examples.translation: 電磁爐利用磁力直接加熱鍋與平底鍋。

relations.native: 平坦地區（有時覆蓋淺水或潮汐水）

etymology.text: From Middle English panne, from Old English panne, from Proto-West Germanic *pannā, from Proto-Germanic *pannǭ. Further origin uncertain.

senses.definition: To wash in a pan (of earth, sand etc. when searching for gold).

examples.translation: 相機掃過房間。

examples.text: The critics panned the performance.
examples.translation: 評論家對這場演出給予負面評價。

senses.definition: To portray; to draw.

etymology.text: From Middle French portraict, pourtraict, nominal use of the past participle of portraire (“portray”), from Latin prōtrahō (< prō- + trahō).
etymology.native: 源於中法語 portraict，由描繪動詞 portraire 的過去分詞派生，該動詞來自拉丁語 prōtrahō。

senses.definition: A flat-bottomed vessel (usually metal) used for cooking food, possibly excluding saucepans (see usage notes).
The nominal household cooking vessel, metaphorically standing for the supply of food for a meal, or for the home.
A vessel (usually earthenware) used with a seal for storing food, such as a honeypot.
A vessel used for brewing or serving drinks: a coffee pot or teapot.
A vessel used to hold soil for growing plants, particularly flowers: a flowerpot.
A vessel used for urination and defecation: a chamber pot; (figuratively, slang) a toilet; the lavatory.
A crucible: a melting pot.
A pot-shaped trap used for catching lobsters or other seafood: a lobster pot.
A pot-shaped metal or earthenware extension of a flue above the top of a chimney: a chimney pot.
A perforated cask for draining sugar.
An earthen or pewter cup or mug used for drinking liquor.

examples.text: Bob filled the pot with water.
examples.translation: 鮑伯把這個壺裝滿了水。

examples.text: Small pots have long handles.
examples.translation: 小鍋柄長。

examples.text: Put the carrots in the pot.
examples.translation: 把胡蘿蔔放在鍋裡。

examples.text: A watched pot never boils.
examples.translation: 心急吃不了熱豆腐。

examples.text: The flower pot is broken.
examples.translation: 花盆碎了。

examples.text: Claudio had long hair and smoked pot.
examples.translation: 克勞迪奧留著長髮，而且抽大麻。

etymology.text: From Middle English pot, potte, from Old English pott (“pot”) and Old French pot (“pot”) (probably from Frankish *pott); both Old English and Frankish from Proto-Germanic *puttaz (“pot”), from Proto-Indo-European *budnós (“a type of vessel”).

senses.definition: An elevation of land of considerable dimensions rising more or less abruptly, forming a conspicuous figure in the landscape, usually having a small extent of surface at its summit.
Something very large in size or quantity; a huge amount; a great heap.
A difficult task or challenge.
Wine from Malaga made from grapes that grow on a mountain.
A woman's large breast.
The twenty-first Lenormand card.
A steam locomotive of the 4-8-2 wheel arrangement.

examples.text: His airplane crashed in the mountains.
examples.translation: 他的飛機在山上墜毀。

examples.text: He makes mountains out of molehills.
examples.translation: 他小題大作。

examples.text: Mountains are not necessarily green.
examples.translation: 山不一定是綠色的。

examples.text: Have you ever seen a snow leopard hunt in the mountains?
examples.translation: 你見過雪豹在山上狩獵嗎？

examples.text: The hikers traced a convoluted route through the mountains.
examples.translation: 徒步者們穿過山巒，走了一條蜿蜒曲折的路徑。

examples.text: I am thankful for standing on the tops of mountains.
examples.translation: 我感謝自己能站在山巔之上。

etymology.text: From Middle English mountayne, mountain, montaigne, from Anglo-Norman muntaine, muntaigne, from Early Medieval Latin montānia, a collective based on Latin montem (“mountain”), from Proto-Indo-European *monti (compare Welsh mynydd (“mountain”), Albanian mat (“bank, shore”), Avestan 𐬨𐬀𐬙𐬌 (mati, “promontory”)), from *men- (“to project, stick out”). Displaced native English barrow (from Old English beorg) and down (from Old English dūn), and partially displaced non-native Old English munt, from Lati
etymology.native: 「山」一詞源於中古英語的 mountayne，再追溯至盎格魯 - 諾曼語 muntaine 與早期中世紀拉丁語 montānia。

senses.definition: A piece of wood or other material, usually long and slender, pointed at one end so as to be easily driven into the ground as a marker or a support or stay.
A piece of wood driven in the ground, placed in the middle of the court, that is used as the finishing point after scoring 12 hoops in croquet.
senses.native: 槓球中計分十二圈後作為終點的木釘

senses.definition: A stick or similar object (e.g., steel channel or angle stock) inserted upright in a lop, eye, or mortise, at the side or end of a cart, flat car, flatbed trailer, or the like, to prevent goods from falling off; often connected in a grid forming a stakebody.
senses.native: 防止貨物掉落而插入車廂側邊或末端的直立木棍，常與其他木棍組成網狀結構

senses.definition: The piece of timber to which a person condemned to death was affixed to be burned.
senses.native: 將死刑犯綁縛並焚燒時所使用的木架

senses.definition: A share or interest in a business or a given situation.
senses.native: 對某項事業或局勢所擁有的份額或利益

senses.definition: That which is laid down as a wager; that which is staked or hazarded; a pledge.
senses.native: 作為賭注的籌碼；押上的東西；保證

senses.definition: A small anvil usually furnished with a tang to enter a hole in a bench top, as used by tinsmiths, blacksmiths, etc., for light work, punching hole in or cutting a work piece, or for specific forming techniques etc.
senses.native: 供錫匠、鐵匠等輕工作用的小型砧座，通常帶有插入工作台孔洞的鉸口

senses.definition: A territorial division comprising all the Mormons (typically several thousand) in a geographical area.
senses.native: 包含所有摩門教徒（通常數千人）的地區行政單位

examples.text: Better than anyone, he understood the stakes.
examples.translation: 他比任何人都更清楚其中的利害關係。

examples.text: I'll stake my reputation on it.
examples.translation: 我賭上我的名聲。

examples.text: The question of IT security has high stakes.
examples.translation: 資訊安全的風險極高。

examples.text: She has a ten percent stake in this company.
examples.translation: 她持有該公司百分之十的股權。

examples.text: We have a substantial stake in the venture.
examples.translation: 我們對這項投資有重大利益。

examples.text: That one is a stake for my plot of land.
examples.translation: 那根木釘標示著我土地的地界。

etymology.text: From Middle English stake, from Old English staca (“pin, tack, stake”), from Proto-West Germanic *stakō, from Proto-Germanic *stakô (“stake”), from Proto-Indo-European *stog-, *steg- (“stake”).
etymology.native: 此詞源於中古英語的 stake，來自古英語 staca（「釘子、楔子」），再追溯至原始日耳曼語及印歐語系詞根。

senses.definition: An overflow of a large amount of water (usually disastrous) from a lake or other body of water due to excessive rainfall or other input of water.
A large number or quantity of anything appearing more rapidly than can easily be dealt with.
The flowing in of the tide, opposed to the ebb.
A floodlight.
Menstrual discharge; menses.
Water as opposed to land.

examples.text: Thirty people perished in the flood.
The flood washed away the bridge.
Our streets flood when it rains.
A lot of houses were washed away by the flood.
examples.translation: 許多房屋被洪水沖走了。

examples.text: The people were evacuated because of the flood.
examples.translation: 人們因為洪水被疏散了。

examples.text: Many homes were washed away by the flood.
examples.translation: 很多家園被洪水沖走了。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English flod, from Old English flōd, from Proto-West Germanic *flōdu, from Proto-Germanic *flōduz, from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₃(w)-. Cognate with Scots flude, fluid, Saterland Frisian Floud, Dutch vloed, German Flut, Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk, and Swedish flod, Icelandic flóð, and Gothic 𐍆𐌻𐍉𐌳𐌿𐍃 (flōdus).

senses.definition: A vessel for boiling a liquid or cooking food, usually metal and equipped with a lid.
The quantity held by a kettle.
A vessel or appliance used to boil water for the preparation of hot beverages and other foodstuffs.
A kettle hole, sometimes any pothole.
A group of raptors swirling and spiraling upward as they ride a thermal, especially when migrating.
A steam locomotive.
A kettledrum.
An instance of kettling; a group of protesters or rioters confined in a limited area.
A watch (timepiece).
A bucket for holding a quantity of paint during the painting process.
A type of encirclement.

examples.text: Why doesn't the kettle work anything?
examples.translation: 為何電水壺什麼都不做？

examples.text: The pot's calling the kettle black.
examples.translation: 鍋子在叫電水壺黑了。

examples.text: I'll put the kettle on and we'll have some tea.
examples.translation: 我點火開水壺，我們來泡杯茶。

examples.text: Flora Jane, go out and put the kettle on.
examples.translation: 弗洛拉·瓊，出去把電水壺開起來。

examples.text: The pot calls the kettle black.
examples.translation: 五十步笑百步。

examples.text: That's like the pot calling the kettle black.
examples.translation: 這就像鍋在說水壺是黑的。

One of the items in a hierarchy.
