One of the seven network switch pieces in the Open Systems Interconnection model: application, presentation, session, transport, network, data link, and physical.
An alternative keymap accessed through a modifier key or toggle.
A person who lays anything, such as tiles or a wager.
A mature female bird, insect, etc. that is able to lay eggs.
A hen kept to lay eggs; a breed of chicken bred to maximize laying output.

examples.text: I layer cheese in lasagna.
The layer of ice was thick enough to walk on.
Beer isn't beer without a nice layer of foam.
Storms have abraded the outer layer of paint.
This morning there was a thick layer of frost.
I added a layer of strawberry jam to the cake.

etymology.text: Appears at first glance to be from Middle English leyer, leyare (“a layer of stones or bricks”), equivalent to lay + -er. In which case, ultimately identical to etymology 2 below. For the pronunciation compare prayer.

senses.definition: To connect or assemble pieces using a screw.
senses.native: 使用螺絲將零件連接或組裝

examples.text: You are screwed.
examples.translation: 你死定了。

examples.text: That could have screwed everything up.
examples.translation: 那可能把一切都搞砸了。

examples.text: Your maid is not the first one to get screwed.
examples.translation: 你的女傭不是第一個被坑的人。

etymology.text: From Middle English screw, scrue (“screw”); apparently, despite the difference in meaning, from Old French escroue (“nut, cylindrical socket, screwhole”), from Latin scrōfa (“female pig”) through comparison with the corkscrew shape of a pig's penis. There is also the Old French escruve (“screw”), from Old Dutch *scrūva ("screw"; whence Middle Dutch schruyve (“screw”)), which probably influenced or conflated with the aforementioned, resulting in the Middle English word.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 screw，scrue（「螺絲」）；儘管意義不同，可能來自舊法語 escroue（「螺母、圓柱形插座、螺紋孔」），再經拉丁語 scrōfa（「母豬」）與豬陰莖螺旋槳形狀的比較。另有舊法語 escruve（「螺絲」），源自舊荷蘭語 *scrūva（「螺絲」；由此衍生中古荷蘭語 schruyve（「螺絲」）」），可能影響或與前述詞彙合併，形成中古英語此詞。

senses.definition: A folded-back and stitched piece of fabric; especially, the stitching that joins two or more pieces of fabric.
A suture.
A thin stratum, especially of an economically viable material such as coal or mineral.
senses.native: 煤礦層或礦物層等具有經濟價值的薄層

senses.definition: The stitched equatorial seam of a cricket ball; the sideways movement of a ball when it bounces on the seam.
senses.native: 板球賽中縫合的赤道線；球在該線上反彈時產生的橫向移動

senses.definition: A joint formed by mating two separate sections of materials.
senses.native: 兩段材料接合處形成的接縫

senses.definition: A line or depression left by a cut or wound; a scar; a cicatrix.
senses.native: 切割或傷口留下的痕跡；傷疤；癒合組織

senses.definition: A line of junction; a joint.

examples.text: The blanket's seam has unraveled.
examples.translation: 毯子的縫線已經鬆開了。

examples.text: My jeans ripped at the seams.
examples.translation: 我的牛仔褲在縫線處破裂了。

examples.text: Please take in the seams of the jacket a little.
examples.translation: 請將外套的縫線收緊一些。

examples.text: His clothes were bursting at the seams.
examples.translation: 他的衣服快要從縫線處爆開了。

examples.text: Reality is ripping apart at the seams.
examples.translation: 現實正在從內部崩解。

examples.text: In order to fix this mistake we'll have to tear out this seam.
examples.translation: 要修正這個錯誤，我們必須拆掉這條縫線。

etymology.text: From Middle English seem, seme, from Old English sēam (“seam”), from Proto-West Germanic *saum, from Proto-Germanic *saumaz (“that which is sewn”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 seem、seme，來自古英語 sēam（縫合處），源自原始日耳曼語 *saumaz（被縫合之物）。

senses.definition: To kill; to murder.
To eradicate or stamp out.
To defeat; to overcome (in a competition or contest).
senses.native: 擊敗；在比賽或競賽中克服

senses.definition: To delight or overwhelm, especially with laughter.
senses.native: 使欣喜若狂，尤其是因大笑而不知所措

senses.definition: To amaze, stun, or otherwise incapacitate by excellence; to excel at something.
senses.native: 以卓越表現令人驚嘆、癱瘓或超越某事

senses.definition: To have sex with.

examples.text: His jokes really slay me.
examples.translation: 他的笑話把我樂翻了。

examples.text: Slay it like a Capricorn.
examples.translation: 像摩羯座一樣去征服它吧。

examples.text: He slayed the dragon and saved the princess.
examples.translation: 他屠龍救公主。

examples.text: Nobody slays it as best as Capricorn does.
examples.translation: 沒有人能比摩羯座更出色地征服它。

examples.text: 'Twas Thomas who did slay the dragon.
examples.translation: 正是湯瑪斯殺死了那條龍。

examples.text: Stefan must slay the one-eyed monster.
examples.translation: 史丹芬必須屠殺那只獨眼怪物。

etymology.text: From Middle English sleen, slen, from Old English slēan (“to hit, punch, strike; to kill”), from Proto-West Germanic *slahan, from Proto-Germanic *slahaną (“to hit, strike; to kill”), from Proto-Indo-European *slak- (“to hit, strike, throw”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 sleen 或 slen，來自古英語的 slēan（「擊打、拳擊、打擊；殺死」），源自西日耳曼語族的 *slahan，再源自日耳曼語族的 *slahaną（「擊打、打擊；殺死」），最終源自印歐語系的 *slak-（「擊打、打擊、投擲」）。

senses.definition: One of several parallel horizontal layers of material arranged one on top of another.
A layer of sedimentary rock having approximately the same composition throughout.
senses.native: 成分大致相同的沉積岩層

senses.definition: Any of the regions of the atmosphere, such as the stratosphere, that occur as layers.
senses.native: 大氣中如平流層等以層狀出現的區域

senses.definition: A layer of tissue.
A class of society composed of people with similar social, cultural, or economic status.
senses.native: 由具有相似社會、文化或經濟地位的人所組成之階級

senses.definition: A layer of vegetation, usually of similar height.
senses.native: 通常高度相似的植被層

senses.definition: The level of accuracy of a computer's clock, relative to others on the network.
senses.native: 電腦時鐘相對於網路上其他裝置的準確度等級

senses.definition: A historical layer of a language.

examples.text: This stratum goes right across the lake.
examples.translation: 這層岩層橫跨整個湖泊。

examples.text: The color of this stratum stands out from the rest of the cliff face.
examples.translation: 這層岩石的顏色與崖壁其餘部分截然不同。

examples.text: This stratum is waterproof.
examples.translation: 這層岩層具有防水特性。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin strātum (“a spread for a bed, coverlet, quilt, blanket; a pillow, bolster; a bed”), neuter singular of strātus, perfect passive participle of sternō (“spread”). Doublet of estrade and street.
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 strātum，意為床墊或毯子，是 sternō 的過去分詞。與 estrade 及 street 同源。

senses.definition: Constituting or relating to the average.
Neither very good nor very bad; rated somewhere in the middle of all others in the same category.
Typical.
Not outstanding, not good, banal; bad or poor.

examples.text: My school grades were average.

senses.definition: In accordance with, or established by, custom or common usage.
Holding or held by custom.

examples.text: He forgot the customary “thank you.”
examples.translation: 他忘了慣例的「謝謝。」

examples.text: It's customary over here to tip waiting staff.
examples.translation: 這裡慣例是給服務人員小費。

examples.text: It's customary to take calls outside the library.
examples.translation: 在圖書館外接電話是慣例。

examples.text: On Purim it is customary to drink wine.
examples.translation: 在普珥節，慣例是喝葡萄酒。

examples.text: He did the work with his customary efficiency.
examples.translation: 他以慣常的效率完成這項工作。

examples.text: In Japan it is not customary to tip for good service.
examples.translation: 在日本，對優良服務不慣例給小費。

etymology.text: From Middle English custumary, from Medieval Latin custumarius. By surface analysis, custom + -ary.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 custumary，來源為中世紀拉丁文 custumarius。由表面分析可得 custom + -ary。

senses.definition: An instance of plucking or pulling sharply.
The lungs, heart with trachea and often oesophagus removed from slaughtered animals.
senses.native: 宰殺動物後取出的肺、心臟及氣管（有時含食道）

senses.definition: Guts, nerve, fortitude or persistence.

examples.text: Those tiny birds are hardly worth the tedious pluck.

relations.native: 滾動的行為、結果或狀態

etymology.text: From Middle English plucken, plukken, plockien, from Old English pluccian, ploccian (“to pluck, pull away, tear”), also Old English plyċċan ("to pluck, pull, snatch; pluck with desire"), from Proto-West Germanic *plukkōn, from Proto-Germanic *plukkōną, *plukkijaną (“to pluck”), of uncertain and disputed origin.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 plucken、plukken 或 plockien，來自古英語 pluccian 與 ploccian（「拔取、拉扯、撕扯」），亦見古英語 plyċċan（「拔取、拉扯；渴望地拔取」），源自日耳曼語族原初 *plukkōn，其起源不明且存在爭議。

senses.definition: To have luster, to gleam, to shine.

etymology.text: From Middle French lustre, from Old Italian lustro, from Old Italian lustrare (“brighten”), from Latin lūstrō (“to purify, to brighten”), from Latin lūstrum (“purification ritual”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀法語的 lustre，來自古義大利語的 lustro，再來自古義大利語的 lustrare（「使明亮」），源於拉丁語 lūstrō（「淨化、使明亮」），最終來自拉丁語 lūstrum（「淨化儀式」）。

senses.definition: Movement in people or things characterized with a continuous motion, involving either a non solid mass or a multitude.
senses.native: 人或物持續運動的特徵，涉及非固體物質或眾多事物

senses.definition: The movement of a real or figurative fluid.
A formalization of the idea of the motion of particles in a fluid, as a group action of the real numbers on a set.
senses.native: 粒子在流體中運動概念的正式化，即實數對集合的群體作用

senses.definition: The rising movement of the tide.
Smoothness or continuity.
The amount of a fluid that moves or the rate of fluid movement.
senses.native: 流體的移動量或流動速率

senses.definition: A flow pipe, carrying liquid away from a boiler or other central plant (compare with return pipe which returns fluid to central plant).
senses.native: 輸送液體遠離鍋爐或其他中央設施的管道（與將液體送回中央設施的回流管相對）

senses.definition: A mental state characterized by concentration, focus, and enjoyment of a given task.
senses.native: 專注、專注力並享受特定任務的心理狀態

senses.definition: The emission of blood during menstruation.
The ability to skillfully rap along to a beat.
senses.native: 有技巧地隨節奏說唱的能力

senses.definition: The sequence of steps taken in a piece of software to perform some action.
senses.native: 軟體執行某項動作所採取的步驟序列

examples.text: The river flows under the bridge.
examples.translation: 河從橋下流過。

examples.text: The Seine flows through Paris.
examples.translation: 塞納河穿越了巴黎。

examples.text: This river flows quickly.
examples.translation: 這條河水流湍急。

examples.text: The Rhine flows between France and Germany.
examples.translation: 萊茵河流經法國和德國國界。

examples.text: The river that flows through London is the Thames.
examples.translation: 流經倫敦的河是泰晤士河。

examples.text: That river flows into the Pacific.
examples.translation: 這條河匯入太平洋。

relations.native: 工作進程中的步驟序列
流體中持續運動的特徵，涉及非固體物質或眾多事物

etymology.text: From Middle English flowe, from the verb (see below). The psychology sense “state of focus” was coined by Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi in 1975.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 flowe，來自動詞（見下文）。心理學意義「專注狀態」由米哈里·契克森米哈賴於 1975 年提出。

senses.definition: To criticise harshly; to reprove.

examples.text: Don't rebuke him for that.
examples.translation: 不要因為那件事責備他。

examples.text: Mary is rebuking Tom.
examples.translation: 瑪麗正在責備湯姆。

examples.text: He who rebukes the world is rebuked by the world.
examples.translation: 責備世界的人，會被世界責備。

examples.text: Even Satan rebukes you.
examples.translation: 連撒旦也在責備你。

examples.text: He was rebuked for writing such a rough report.
examples.translation: 他因寫了一份如此粗糙的報告而被責備。

examples.text: The minister was rebuked in public.
examples.translation: 該部長在公眾面前受到了斥責。

etymology.text: From Middle English rebuken, from Anglo-Norman rebuker (“to beat back, repel”), from re- + Old French *buker, buchier, buschier (“to strike, hack down, chop”), from busche (“wood”), from Vulgar Latin *busca (“wood, grove”), from Frankish *busk (“grove”), from Proto-Germanic *buskaz (“bush”); equivalent to re- + bush.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 rebuken，來自盎格魯 - 諾曼語 rebuker（「擊退、抵禦」），由前綴 re- 加上古法語 *buker, buchier, buschier（「打擊、砍伐」）組成，後者源於 busche（「樹木」），再源自通俗拉丁語 *busca（「樹木、叢林」），最終來自弗蘭克語 *busk（「叢林」），與原始日耳曼語 *buskaz（「灌木叢」）相當。

senses.definition: Of, or relating to glaciers.
Having the appearance of ice.
Very slow.
Cold and icy.
Cool and unfriendly.

examples.text: Glacial water gets its colour from rock flour.
examples.translation: 冰川水因其顏色來自岩石粉塵而呈現色澤。

examples.text: There are three glacial fjords in Ireland.
examples.translation: 愛爾蘭有三個冰川峽灣。

examples.text: Glacial meltwater is not purer than other types of water.
examples.translation: 冰川融水不如其他類型的水純淨。

examples.text: The melted snowpack seeps down to fill mountainside indentations to form glacial lakes.
examples.translation: 融化的積雪滲透下去，填滿山邊的凹陷處，形成冰川湖。

examples.text: This project runs at a glacial pace.
examples.translation: 這個專案進展緩慢如冰川。

examples.text: In front of the fireplace, they shared stories to forget the glacial winter nights.
examples.translation: 壁爐前，他們分享故事以忘卻那寒冷無情的冬夜。

relations.native: 與礦床或開採地有關的

etymology.text: Borrowed from French glacial, from Latin glaciālis, from glaciēs (“ice”). The sense "slow" refers to the speed of actual glaciers, typically around 1 meter per day.
etymology.native: 借自法語 glacial，源於拉丁語 glaciālis，來自 glaciēs（冰）。「緩慢」之意指實際冰川的速度，通常每天約一米。

senses.definition: A hard growth of keratin that protrudes from the top of the head of certain animals, usually paired.

Any similar real or imaginary growth or projection such as the elongated tusk of a narwhal, the eyestalk of a snail, the pointed growth on the nose of a rhinoceros, or the hornlike projection on the head of a demon or similar.
An antler.
The hard substance from which animals' horns are made, sometimes used by man as a material for making various objects.
A vessel made from a horn, to contain drink, ink, gunpowder, etc.
One of the two corners of a crescent, particularly of the crescent moon
The high pommel of a saddle; also, either of the projections on a lady's saddle for supporting the leg.
The Ionic volute.
The outer end of a crosstree; also, one of the projections forming the jaws of a gaff, boom, etc.
A curved projection on the fore part of a plane.
One of the projections at the four corners of the Jewish altar of burnt offering.

examples.text: Cows have horns.
examples.translation: 牛有角。

examples.text: Angry drivers were blowing their horns.
examples.translation: 氣惱的駕駛員都在按喇叭。

examples.text: This may sound like blowing my own horn, but ...
examples.translation: 這聽起來可能像是我在自吹自擂, 但是...

examples.text: Viking helmets with horns aren't in style in Scandinavia anymore.
examples.translation: 斯堪的納維亞現在已經不流行戴維京人那種有角的頭盔了。

examples.text: The train slowed and blared its horn as it approached the railway crossing.
examples.translation: 火車在快到交叉路口的時候減速、按喇叭。

examples.text: The older the billy goat, the harder the horn.
examples.translation: 越老的公山羊，角就越硬。

etymology.text: From Middle English horn, horne, from Old English horn, from Proto-West Germanic *horn, from Proto-Germanic *hurną. Compare West Frisian hoarn, Dutch hoorn, Low German Hoorn, horn, German Horn, Danish and Swedish horn, Gothic 𐌷𐌰𐌿𐍂𐌽 (haurn).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 horn、horne，來自古英語 horn，源自原始西日耳曼語 *horn，再源自原始德語 *hurną。可參照西弗里斯蘭語 hoarn、荷蘭語 hoorn、低德語 Hoorn、德語 Horn、丹麥語與瑞典語 horn、古高地德語 𐌷𐌰𐌿𐍂𐌽 (haurn)。

senses.definition: Alternative spelling of doughnut.

examples.text: I've got some donuts.
examples.translation: 我有幾個甜甜圈。

examples.text: Could I have three cinnamon donuts?
examples.translation: 請問我要三個肉桂甜甜圈嗎？

examples.text: The baklava is better than donuts.
examples.translation: 巴克拉瓦比甜甜圈好吃。

examples.text: Can you save one of those donuts for me?
examples.translation: 你可以幫我留一個甜甜圈嗎？

examples.text: I don't want you eating donuts every morning.
examples.translation: 我不希望你每天早上都吃甜甜圈。

examples.text: I want to buy a dozen donuts.
examples.translation: 我想買十二個甜甜圈。

etymology.text: Alteration of doughnut, from dough + nut. Attested 1900.
etymology.native: 甜甜圈是麵團與堅果的變化，始見於一九零零年。

senses.definition: A lightweight woven container, generally round, open at the top, and tapering toward the bottom.
A bed for a cat.
A wire or plastic container similar in shape to a basket, used for carrying articles for purchase in a shop.
In an online shop, a listing of a customer's chosen items before they are ordered.
A set or collection of intangible things.
A circular hoop, from which a net is suspended, which is the goal through which the players try to throw the ball.
The act of putting the ball through the basket, thereby scoring points.
The game of basketball.

A dance movement in some line dances, where men put their arms round the women's lower backs, and the women put their arms over the men's shoulders, and the group (usually of four, any more is difficult) spins round, which should result in the women's feet leaving the ground.
The penis and region surrounding it.
The bulge of the penis seen through clothing.

examples.text: The basket was filled with strawberries.
examples.translation: 籃子裡裝滿了草莓。

examples.text: The basket was full of strawberries.
examples.translation: 籃子裡裝滿了草莓。

examples.text: There's a basket under the table.
examples.translation: 桌子底下有一個籃子。

examples.text: The eggs are in the basket.
examples.translation: 雞蛋在籃子裡。

examples.text: She was carrying a basket full of flowers.
examples.translation: 她提著一籃鮮花。

examples.text: There are a lot of eggs in the basket.
examples.translation: 籃子裡有很多雞蛋。

etymology.text: From Middle English basket, from Anglo-Norman baschet, basket, bascat, from latin

senses.definition: To clean thoroughly; to rid of impurities; to cleanse; to clear of (something unwanted).
To remove by cleansing; to wash away.
To free from sin, guilt, or burden.
To evacuate (the bowels or the stomach); to defecate or vomit.
To cause someone to purge; to operate (on somebody) using a cathartic or emetic, or in a similar manner.
To forcibly remove, for example, from political activity.
To forcibly remove people by an organization.
To clear of a charge, suspicion, or imputation.
To clarify; to clear the dregs from (liquor).
To become pure, as by clarification.
To have or produce frequent evacuations from the intestines, as by means of a cathartic.

examples.text: Does Algeria need a major political purge?
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞是否需要大規模的政治清洗？

examples.text: There was a post-coup purge in Turkey.
examples.translation: 土耳其在政變後曾進行過清洗。

examples.text: Purge your head of morals and prejudice.
examples.translation: 清除你心中的道德與偏見。

examples.text: Joe purged himself of the suspicion.
examples.translation: 喬伊已清除自己心中的懷疑。

examples.text: What's the first thing you'd do if The Purge was real?
examples.translation: 如果《清洗》真的發生，你第一件事會做什麼？

examples.text: Algeria needs to be purged of corruption.
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞必須清除腐敗。

etymology.text: From Middle English purgen, from Old French purgier, from Latin pūrgō (“to make pure, to cleanse”), from pūrus (“clean, pure”) + agō (“to make, to do”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 purgen，來自古法文 purgier，源自拉丁文 pūrgō（意為「使純淨、清潔」），由 pūrus（意為「清潔、純淨」）與 agō（意為「使、做」）組成。

senses.definition: To eject forcibly and in a stream.
To be forcibly ejected.
To speak or write quickly and voluminously, especially words that are not worth listening to or reading.
senses.native: 快速且大量地說話或寫作，特別是那些不值得聽或讀的詞語

senses.definition: To be written or spoken voluminously.
To vomit.
To ejaculate.
To develop a white powder or dark crystals on the surface of finished leather, as a result from improper tanning.
senses.native: 因鞣製不當，在成品皮革表面形成白色粉末或深色晶體

examples.text: Please stop spewing lies.
examples.translation: 請停止撒謊。

examples.text: You spew out lies!
examples.translation: 你竟然在說謊！

examples.text: Black smoke spewed out of the third-story windows.
examples.translation: 黑煙從三樓的窗戶噴出。

examples.text: He effortlessly spews the funniest non sequiturs I've ever heard.
examples.translation: 他毫不費力地說出我聽過最荒謬的笑話。

examples.text: Tom keeps spewing out high-end terms, but I know it's all fluff.
examples.translation: 湯姆一直在吐高端術語，但我知道都是虛的。

examples.text: Puyehue Volcano keeps on spewing lava.
examples.translation: 普耶湖火山持續噴發熔岩。

etymology.text: From Middle English spewen, from Old English spīwan, from Proto-West Germanic *spīwan, from Proto-Germanic *spīwaną, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ptyēw- (“to spit, vomit”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 spewen，再追溯至古英語、日耳曼語族及印歐語系詞根，意為「吐口水」或「嘔吐」。

senses.definition: A large pile of hay, grain, straw, or the like, larger at the bottom than the top, sometimes covered with thatch.
A pile of similar objects, each directly on top of the last.
A linear data structure in which items inserted are removed in reverse order (the last item inserted is the first one to be removed).
A pile of poles or wood, indefinite in quantity.
A pile of wood containing 108 cubic feet. (~3 m³)
An extensive collection
A smokestack.
A stack data structure stored in main memory that is manipulated during machine language procedure call related instructions.
An implementation of a protocol suite (set of protocols forming a layered architecture).
A combination of interdependent, yet individually replaceable, software components or technologies used together on a system.
A generalization of schemes in algebraic geometry and of sheaves.

examples.text: Tom put a stack of letters on Mary's desk.
examples.translation: 湯姆把一疊信放在瑪麗桌上。

examples.text: There's a stack of comic books on Tom's desk.
Hey, could you send over a stack of manuscripts straight away?
examples.translation: 喂，請問現在能給我馬上送一疊稿子嗎？

examples.text: She's a professor whose works you could stack up to head height.
examples.translation: 那位是一個著作等身的教授。

examples.text: Tom is clambering about on the roof, repairing the chimney stack.
examples.translation: 湯姆在屋頂一邊爬一邊修理煙囪。

examples.text: Don't stack too many items on the counter; it can lead to clutter.

etymology.text: From Middle English stack, stacke, stakke, stak, from Old Norse stakkr (“a barn; haystack; heap; pile”), from Proto-Germanic *stakkaz (“a barn; rick; haystack”).
etymology.native: 來自中世紀英文 stack、stacke、stakke、stak，源自古諾斯語 stakkr（意為「穀草堆；堆積物」），來自原始日耳曼語 *stakkaz（意為「穀草堆；堆積物」）。

senses.definition: The act, or process of slewing.
A device used for slewing.
A change of position.

examples.text: The prince slew the dragon.
examples.translation: 王子殺死了龍。

examples.text: Tom slew the dragon.
examples.translation: 湯姆殺死了龍。

examples.text: Rama slew Ravana.
examples.translation: 拉瑪殺死了羅波那。

examples.text: He slew his children, his wife, his concubines, and his servants.
examples.translation: 他殺死了他的孩子、妻子、妾室和僕人。

examples.text: Tom slew the monster.
examples.translation: 湯姆殺死了怪物。

examples.text: A slew of corporate logos adorned the entrance to the soccer match.
examples.translation: 一群企業標誌裝飾著足球賽的入口。

etymology.text: In all senses, a mostly British spelling of slue.
etymology.native: 在所有用法中，slue 的大多為英國拼寫。

senses.definition: Consisting of two or more threads, strands or the like intertwined; formed by twisting or twining.
Mentally or emotionally distorted or unsound; perverted.
Having the intended meaning altered or misrepresented; misunderstood.
Distorted or contorted by tensing the facial muscles.
Under heavy influence of intoxicants, usually alcohol and marijuana; very intoxicated.
Having a spiral ornament inside.
Intimately associated or connected; united; combined.

examples.text: Tom's haters have twisted his words.
examples.translation: 湯姆的敵人曲解了他的話。

examples.text: Tom and Mary twisted their ankles.
examples.translation: 湯姆和瑪麗扭傷了腳踝。

examples.text: The creature's limbs were twisted.
examples.translation: 那生物的四肢扭曲了。

examples.text: She twisted her ankle while she was doing exercise.
examples.translation: 她鍛鍊時扭傷了腳踝。

examples.text: Nobody twisted Yanni's arm to become a Muslim.
examples.translation: 沒有人強迫雅尼皈依伊斯蘭。

examples.text: Tom and Mary have both twisted their ankles.
examples.translation: 湯姆和瑪麗都扭傷了腳踝。

etymology.text: The sense "intertwined" comes from twist (verb) by the late 15th century. The sense "mentally disturbed, perverted" is probably from twist (“mental peculiarity, perversion”, noun), which is attested by 1811.
etymology.native: 「交織」的意思來自於15世紀晚期的動詞「扭」；「精神異常、扭曲」的意思則可能來自於1811年出現的名詞「扭」，意指「精神特異、扭曲」。

senses.definition: Susceptible to death by aging, sickness, injury, or wound; not immortal.
Causing death; deadly, fatal, killing, lethal (now only of wounds, injuries etc.).
Punishable by death.
Fatally vulnerable.
Of or relating to the time of death.
Affecting as if with power to kill; deathly; related to a life-and-death struggle.
senses.native: 具有殺死力量的；致命的；與生死搏鬥相關

senses.definition: Human; belonging or pertaining to people who are mortal.
senses.native: 人類；屬於會死亡的人類

senses.definition: Very painful or tedious; wearisome.
senses.native: 極度痛苦或枯燥的；令人疲乏的

senses.definition: Very drunk.
Causing spiritual death (the destruction of charity in the soul) and thus, a disruption of one's relationship with God.
senses.native: 造成靈魂死亡（慈善心的毀滅），從而破壞與上帝的關係

examples.text: Mortal enemies are immortal friends.
examples.translation: 不共戴天的敵人是不朽的朋友。

examples.text: The body is mortal, but the soul is immortal.
examples.translation: 身體是會死的，但靈魂是不朽的。

examples.text: Man is mortal.
examples.translation: 人固有一死。

examples.text: Tatoeba: Let the 'mortal translation' begin!
examples.translation: Tatoeba：讓「致命翻譯」開始吧！

examples.text: We know that all men are mortal.
examples.translation: 我們知道人皆難免一死。

examples.text: How can you, a mere mortal, dare criticise Tom?
examples.translation: 你如何敢於，身為一個凡夫俗子，批評 Tom？

etymology.text: From Middle English mortal, mortel, from Old French mortal, and their source Latin mortālis, from mors (“death”). In this sense, displaced native deadly, from Old English dēadlīċ.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 mortal 或 mortel，來自舊法語的 mortal，其根源為拉丁語 mortālis，源自 mors（死亡）。在此意義上，取代了本土的 deadly，來自古英語 dēadlīċ。

senses.definition: A large or dense piece of something.
An attractive man, especially one who is muscular.
senses.native: 一位有魅力的男子，特別是指肌肉結實者

senses.definition: A record of differences between almost contiguous portions of two files (or other sources of information). Differences that are widely separated by areas which are identical in both files would not be part of a single hunk. Differences that are separated by small regions which are identical in both files may comprise a single hunk. Patches are made up of hunks.
senses.native: 兩個幾乎相鄰的文件（或其他資訊來源）之間差異的記錄。若兩文件間存在大量相同區域，則相隔甚遠的差異不會屬於同一塊；若相隔區域較小且內容相同，則可能構成單一區塊。修補檔由多個區塊組成

senses.definition: A honyock.
A material object considered purely as extended stuff without identity criteria.
senses.native: 僅視為具有延展性的物質，而不考慮其身份標準的實體物件

senses.definition: A goal or base in children's games.
senses.native: 兒童遊戲中的目標或基地

examples.text: The teacher gave us a large hunk of bread to share.
examples.translation: 老師給我們一大片麵包分享。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: That dense hunk of fog obscured the distant mountain peaks.
examples.translation: 那團濃密的霧氣遮擋了遠處的山巒。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: You're a hunk.
examples.translation: 你真是個帥哥。

examples.text: Tom is a hunk.
examples.translation: 湯姆是個帥哥。

examples.text: He's a hunk.
examples.translation: 他真帥氣。

examples.text: We won't get very far with this hunk of junk.
examples.translation: 我們拿這堆破東西是辦不到什麼大事的。

etymology.text: Probably borrowed from West Flemish hunke (“hunk; chunk”), of obscure origin. Probably from an earlier *humke, *humpke, a diminutive related to Dutch homp (“hunk; lump”), English hump, equivalent to hump + -kin. The sense of an attractive man is recorded in Australian slang in 1941, in jive talk in 1945.
etymology.native: 可能源自西弗蘭芒語的 hunke（意為「塊狀物；碎塊」），其起源不明確。可能來自更早的 *humke 或 *humpke，這是與荷蘭語 homp（意為「塊狀物；疙瘩」）、英語 hump 相關的貶稱詞，相當於 hump + -kin。形容有魅力的男子一義始見於 1941 年的澳洲俚語，至 1945 年才出現在 jive talk 中。

senses.definition: To fall away gradually; to subside.
To fall into error or heresy.
To slip into a bad habit that one is trying to avoid.
senses.native: 滑入試圖避免的不良習慣

senses.definition: To become void.

examples.text: Tom lapsed into silence.
examples.translation: 湯姆陷入了沉默。

examples.text: He lapsed into despair after that accident.
examples.translation: 那場事故後，他陷入了絕望。

examples.text: Tom lapsed into a coma and didn't regain consciousness.
examples.translation: 湯姆陷入了昏迷，未能恢復意識。

examples.text: The correspondence lapsed.
examples.translation: 通訊中斷了。

etymology.text: From Middle French laps, from Latin lāpsus, from lābī (“to slip”). Doublet of lapsus.
etymology.native: 源於中古法語 laps，來自拉丁語 lāpsus，意為「滑動」。與 lapsus 同源詞。

senses.definition: A hollow or pit into which liquid drains, such as a cesspool, cesspit or sink.
The lowest part of a mineshaft into which water drains.
senses.native: 礦坑的最低處，水會在此匯集

senses.definition: A completely flooded cave passage, sometimes passable by diving.
senses.native: 完全被水淹沒的洞穴通道，有時可潛水通行

senses.definition: The crankcase or oil reservoir of an internal combustion engine.
senses.native: 內燃機的曲軸箱或油槽

senses.definition: The pit at the lowest point in a circulating or drainage system (FM 55-501).
senses.native: 循環或排水系統中最低點的坑洞（FM 55-501）

senses.definition: An intentional depression around a drain or scupper that promotes drainage.
senses.native: 排水口或溢流口周圍有意設計的凹陷，促進排水

senses.definition: A sudden or heavy fall of rain; a deluge.
senses.native: 突發性或強烈的降雨；傾盆大雨

examples.text: We need to clean the sump before it overflows again.
examples.translation: 我們需要在它再次溢流之前清理水坑。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: This sump is deep and filled with murky liquid inside.
examples.translation: 這個水坑很深，裡面充滿了渾濁的液體。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The boat's bilge sump collects rainwater that enters during storms.
examples.translation: 船隻的艙底水坑會收集颱風期間進入的雨滴。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The antiquated sump, lined with rusted iron, still serves its purpose.
examples.translation: 這座陳舊的水坑內襯鏽鐵，仍發揮其功能。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Architects designed a complex sump network to handle peak storm runoff.
examples.translation: 建築師設計了複雜的水坑網路，以處理高峰期的暴雨徑流。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The derelict sump, long abandoned by civilization, now serves as a breeding ground for mold.
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

relations.native: 廢棄物堆放處；焚化灰場；垃圾填埋場
撞擊或撞上，伴隨突然的衝擊

etymology.text: From Middle English sompe, either from Middle Dutch somp, sump or Middle Low German sump from Old Saxon *sump, from Proto-West Germanic *sump, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *sumpaz. Doublet of swamp.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 sompe，可能來自中古荷蘭語 somp 或中低地德語 sump，最終源自原始日耳曼語 *sumpaz，與 swamp 同源。

senses.definition: A part broken off; a small, detached portion; an imperfect part, either physically or not.
A sentence not containing a subject or a predicate; a sentence fragment.
senses.native: 主詞或謂語皆缺失的句子；句子片段

senses.definition: An incomplete portion of code.
senses.native: 程式碼中不完整的一段

senses.definition: A portion of a URL referring to a subordinate resource or anchor (such as a specific point on a web page), introduced by the # sign.
senses.native: 網址中指向從屬資源或錨點（如網頁特定位置）的部分，以「#」符號引入

senses.definition: A split piece of an organism that has undergone the asexual reproduction process where the organism splits into one or more pieces, then those pieces become new individuals.
senses.native: 生物體經過無性繁殖分裂成一個或多個部分，這些部分再變成新個體的片段

examples.text: The vase broke into fragments.
I can only remember fragments.
Donald went to clean up the mirror fragments.
examples.translation: 唐納德去清理鏡子碎片。

examples.text: It's hard to splice the two fragments together.
Fragments of the mirror were scattered on the floor.
A few fragments of dead leaves floated on the pond.
examples.translation: 池塘裡漂浮著零星的幾片落葉。

relations.native: 由碎片組成；斷裂的；散亂的

etymology.text: From Late Middle English fragment, from Latin fragmentum (“a fragment, remnant”), from frangō (“to break”) + -mentum.

senses.definition: A loose filmy mass or a thin chiplike layer of anything
A scale of a fish or similar animal
A prehistoric tool chipped out of stone.
A person who is impractical, flighty, unreliable, or inconsistent; especially with maintaining a living.
A carnation with only two colours in the flower, the petals having large stripes.
A flat turn or tier of rope.
A corrupt arrest, e.g. to extort money for release or merely to fulfil a quota.
A wire rack for drying fish.

examples.text: It's a flake covered in chocolate!
examples.translation: 這是一塊沾滿巧克力的脆片！

examples.text: Tom likes corn chips, but hates corn flakes.
examples.translation: 湯姆喜歡玉米片，卻討厭玉米脆片。

examples.text: Corn flakes and milk certainly go well together.
examples.translation: 玉米脆片配牛奶，搭配得非常完美。

examples.text: Dandruff is made of small flakes of dead skin.
examples.translation: 頭皮屑是由脫落的死皮細小碎片組成。

examples.text: He can finish ten boxes of corn flakes in one sitting.
examples.translation: 他一次能吃完十盒玉米脆片。

examples.text: He likes to sprinkle coconut flakes on top of his cupcakes.
examples.translation: 他喜歡在紙杯蛋糕上撒椰子脆片。

etymology.text: From Middle English flake (“a flake of snow”), from Old English flacca and/or Old Norse flak (“loose or torn piece”) (compare Old Norse flakna (“to flake or chip”)), from Proto-Germanic *flaką (“something flat”), from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat, broad, plain”). Cognate with Norwegian flak (“slice, sliver”, literally “piece torn off”), Swedish flak (“a thin slice”), Danish flage (“flake”), German Flocke (“flake”), Dutch vlak (“smooth surface, plain”) and vlok (“flake”), as well as with La
etymology.native: 「flake」源自中世英文 flake（雪片），來自古英語 flacca 和／或古諾斯語 flak（鬆散或撕裂的碎片），又源自原始日耳曼語 *flaką（扁平之物），再溯源自原始印歐語 *pleh₂-（平坦、寬廣）。與挪威語 flak（切片、薄片，字面為「撕下的碎片」）、瑞典語 flak（薄片）、丹麥語 flage（碎屑）、德語 Flocke（碎屑）、荷蘭語 vlak（平滑表面）及 vlok（碎屑）同源，亦與拉丁語相關。

senses.definition: A small part of something, such as a song or fabric; sample.
A text file containing a relatively small amount of code, useless by itself, along with instructions for inserting that code into a larger codebase.
senses.native: 一段包含少量程式碼的檔案，本身無用，但附有將該程式碼插入較大程式碼庫的說明

examples.text: She gave me a snippet of information which is top secret.
examples.translation: 她給我一段機密至極的資訊片段。

examples.text: I collect snippets of information from a variety of sources.
examples.translation: 我從各種來源收集資訊片段。

examples.text: And miraculously, he lifted his own violin and started playing, by ear, certain snippets of violin concertos.
examples.translation: 神蹟般地，他拿起自己的小提琴開始演奏，憑耳聽，彈奏某些小提琴協奏曲的片段。

examples.text: From the snippet I heard of their rehearsal, they sound pretty good.
examples.translation: 從我聽到的他們彩排片段來看，他們的聲音還不錯。

examples.text: This is just a tiny snippet of the whole song.
examples.translation: 這只是整首歌的一小段片段。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: She cut a small snippet from the old fabric.
examples.translation: 她從舊布料上剪下一小塊。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

relations.native: 浸在肉汁裡的一小塊烤麵包

etymology.text: From snip + -et. Compare snippock.
etymology.native: 由「剪」加上後綴「-et」組成。可與「snippock」相比。

senses.definition: A taste, liking, or inclination for (something).
A card game resembling bezique.
senses.native: 類似貝齊克的紙牌遊戲

senses.definition: In the game of penchant, any queen and jack of different suits held at the same time.
senses.native: 在筆欽遊戲中，同時持有的不同花色的王后與傑克

examples.text: He has a penchant for fine wine.
examples.translation: 他非常喜愛優質葡萄酒。

examples.text: Women have a natural penchant for the mysterious.
examples.translation: 女性天生對神秘事物有著天然的興趣。

examples.text: He plays a wily detective with a penchant for disguises.
examples.translation: 他扮演一位擅長變裝的狡猾偵探。

examples.text: He has a penchant for whistling at pretty ladies he sees on the street.
examples.translation: 他喜歡在街上對漂亮女士吹口哨。

examples.text: The Irish have a penchant for blarney.
examples.translation: 愛爾蘭人擅長說花言巧語。

examples.text: I have a real penchant for collecting old stamps.
examples.translation: 我真的很喜歡收集舊郵票。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

relations.native: 易受影響的狀態；脆弱性

etymology.text: Unadapted borrowing from French penchant, present participle of pencher (“to tilt, to lean”), from Middle French, from Old French pengier (“to tilt, be out of line”), from Vulgar Latin *pendicāre, a derivative of Latin pendere (“to hang”).
etymology.native: 此詞源自法語筆欽，意為傾斜或倚靠，其源頭可追溯至古法語及拉丁語的「懸掛」之意。

senses.definition: To label (something).

examples.text: Claudio tagged Isabella in a picture.
examples.translation: 克勞迪奧在照片中標記了伊莎貝拉。

examples.text: Are you sure you don't mind me tagging along?
examples.translation: 你確定不介意我跟著一起嗎？

examples.text: The snail tagged along with the turtle.
examples.translation: 田螺跟著烏龜一起前行。

examples.text: In the first paragraph, she describes the labels she was tagged with, which have a negative connotation.
examples.translation: 在第一段中，她描述了被她標記的標籤，這些標籤帶有負面含義。

etymology.text: From Middle English tagge (“small piece hanging from a garment”), probably of North Germanic origin. Compare Norwegian tagg (“point; prong; barb; tag”), Swedish tagg (“thorn; prickle; tine”), Icelandic tág (“a willow-twig”). Compare also tack.
etymology.native: 此詞源於中古英語的 tagge，意指掛在衣服上的小塊物體。

senses.definition: To hold by the end; said of a timber when it rests upon a wall or other support; with in or into

examples.text: I can't make head or tail of those directions.

etymology.text: From Middle English tail, taile, taille, tayil, tayl, tayle, tayll, teil, tæȝel, from Old English tæġel, tæġl (“tail”), from Proto-West Germanic *tagl, from Proto-Germanic *taglą (“hair, fiber; hair of a tail”), from Proto-Indo-European *doḱ- (“hair of the tail”), from Proto-Indo-European *deḱ- (“to tear, fray, shred”).

senses.definition: To detect with the senses, especially with the eyes.
To perceive, recognize, or comprehend with the mind; to descry.
senses.native: 心智感知、辨識或理解；詳察

senses.definition: To distinguish something as being different from something else; to differentiate or discriminate.
senses.native: 辨別某物與他物之不同；區分或鑑別

senses.definition: To perceive differences.

examples.text: He just talks; he doesn't discern.
examples.translation: 他只會說話，無法辨別。

etymology.text: Shortened from gooney, from obsolete gony (“simpleton”), used circa 1580, of unknown origin. The term goon first carried the meaning "stupid person" (circa 1921). Compare Scots goni, guni (“a bogey, bugbear, hobgoblin”), dialectal Swedish gonnar (“elves, goblins”, plural).
etymology.native: 「gooney」源自已廢棄的「gony」（意為「傻瓜」），約在1580年使用，起源不明。可能源自中古英格蘭的「gone」，為「gome」（意為「人」）的變體。 sailors 約在1839年用「gony」形容鴨嘴鳥等笨重的大鳥。直到1921年，「goon」才開始指「愚蠢的人」。可與蘇格蘭語「goni」、「guni」（意為「惡魔、妖怪」）及瑞典方言「gonnar」（意為「精靈、小妖」）相對照。
