examples.text: The Japanese are an industrious people.
examples.translation: 日本人是勤奮的國民。

examples.text: He liberated the people from bondage.
examples.translation: 他讓人們擺脫了奴役。

examples.text: People who will lie for you, will lie to you.
examples.translation: 會為你說謊的人，就會對你說謊。

examples.text: Two hundred people died of cholera last year.
examples.translation: 去年有兩百人因霍亂死亡。

etymology.text: From Middle English puple, peple, peeple, from Anglo-Norman people, from Old French pueple, peuple, pople, from Latin populus (“a people, nation”), from Old Latin populus, from earlier poplus, from even earlier poplos, from Proto-Italic *poplos (“army”) of unknown origin. Doublet of pueblo. Gradually ousted native English lede and, partially, folk.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 puple、peple 或 peeple，來自盎格魯 - 諾曼人的 people，再源自舊法語的 pueple、peuple 等，最終來自拉丁語 populus（「人民、民族」），其詞源可追溯至更早的拉丁語 poplus 及原始義大利語 *poplos（意為「軍隊」），具體起源不明。它與 pueblo 同源，逐漸取代了本土英語中的 lede 和 folk。

senses.definition: The part of the forelimb below the forearm or wrist in humans and other primates, and the corresponding part in many other animals.
An index or pointer on a dial; such as the hour and minute hands on the face of an analog clock, which are used to indicate the time of day.
A side; part, camp; direction, either right or left.
A limb of certain animals, such as the foot of a hawk, or any one of the four extremities of a monkey.
The set of cards held by a player.
A round of a card game.
A bundle of tobacco leaves tied together.
A bunch of bananas, a typical retail amount, where individual fruits are fingers.
Four inches, a hand's breadth.
Three inches.
Power of performance; means of execution; ability; skill; dexterity.

examples.text: All the students clapped their hands.
examples.translation: 所有的學生都拍手。

examples.text: Wash your hands before each meal.
examples.translation: 飯前洗手

examples.text: She greeted him waving her hand.
examples.translation: 她揮著手向他打招呼。

examples.text: You haven't washed your hands yet, have you?
examples.translation: 你還沒洗手，不是嗎？

examples.text: I entered the room and shook hands with him.
examples.translation: 我走進了房間與他握手。

examples.text: My right hand is Uighur, and my left is Han.
examples.translation: 我的右手是維族的，左手是漢族的。

etymology.text: From Middle English hond, hand, from Old English hand, from Proto-West Germanic *handu, from Proto-Germanic *handuz.
etymology.native: 「hand」源自中世紀英文 hond，來自古英文 hand，再溯源自原始西日耳曼語 *handu，更上溯至原始日耳曼語 *handuz。

senses.definition: To give, pass or transmit with the hand, literally or figuratively.

examples.text: Have you handed in your homework?
examples.translation: 你交功課了嗎？

examples.text: Tom handed the envelope full of cash to Mary.
examples.translation: 湯姆把裝滿現金的信封遞給瑪麗。

etymology.text: From Middle English hond, hand, from Old English hand, from Proto-West Germanic *handu, from Proto-Germanic *handuz.
etymology.native: 「hand」源自中世紀英文 hond，來自古英文 hand，再溯源自原始西日耳曼語 *handu，更上溯至原始日耳曼語 *handuz。

senses.definition: The act or process of writing done with the hand, rather than typed or word-processed.
The characteristic writing of a particular person.
Text that was written by hand.
A characteristic trait or hallmark by which somebody may be recognised.

examples.text: She has very nice-looking handwriting.
examples.translation: 她的筆跡很美。

examples.text: Your handwriting is really good!
examples.translation: 你的字寫得真漂亮！

examples.text: My mother has good handwriting.
examples.translation: 我母親的筆跡很好看。

examples.text: She's got terrible handwriting.
examples.translation: 她寫的字很難看。

examples.text: She has beautiful handwriting.
examples.translation: 她的筆跡很美。

examples.text: Do you know whose handwriting this is?
examples.translation: 你知道這是誰的字嗎？

etymology.text: From hand + writing, equal to handwrite + -ing.
etymology.native: 由「手」與「寫」組成，意即手寫加上動名詞尾。

senses.definition: The soft foot of a mammal or other animal, generally a quadruped, that has claws or nails; comparable to a human hand or foot.
A hand.

examples.text: The cat was licking its paws.
examples.translation: 貓正在舔它的爪子。

examples.text: David bandaged the dog's paw.
examples.translation: 戴維給小狗的爪子包紮了。

examples.text: Get your dirty paws off me.
examples.translation: 別用你那髒手碰我。

examples.text: Cookie, sit! Paw! Down! Roll over! Good girl!
examples.translation: 坐好！趴下！滾過來！乖女孩！

examples.text: Boris noticed the paw prints around the camp.
examples.translation: 鮑里斯注意到營地周圍的爪印。

examples.text: The cat was touching the mouse with its paw.
examples.translation: 貓用爪子觸碰著老鼠。

etymology.text: From Middle English pawe, from Old French poue, poe, from Vulgar Latin *pauta. Further origin unknown, perhaps from Frankish *pōta, from Frankish *pōtōn (“to put, stick, plant”), from Proto-Germanic *putōną, whence also Old English potian (“to push”), pȳtan (“to put out, poke out”). See more at put. Doublet of pote, put, and putt.
etymology.native: 詞源不明，可能來自日耳曼語族 *pōta，意為「放置、插入、種植」。

senses.definition: The atmosphere above a given point, especially as visible from the surface of the Earth as the place where the sun, moon, stars, and clouds are seen.
With a descriptive word: the part of the sky which can be seen from a specific place or at a specific time; its climate, condition, etc.
Usually preceded by the: the abode of God or the gods, angels, the souls of deceased people, etc.; heaven; also, powers emanating from heaven.
The set of all lightlike lines (or directions) passing through a given point in space-time.
In an art gallery: the upper rows of pictures that cannot easily be seen; also, the place where such pictures are hung.
A cloud.

examples.text: The sky was filled with aeroplanes.
examples.translation: 天上滿是飛機。

examples.text: The sky was ablaze with fireworks.
examples.translation: 天空被焰火點亮。

examples.text: The sky became darker and darker.
examples.translation: 天空變得越來越暗了。

examples.text: The clouds floating in the sky are beautiful.
examples.translation: 天空飄的雲很美。

examples.text: Not a single cloud could be seen in the sky.
examples.translation: 天上萬里無雲。

examples.text: Do you know the reason why the sky looks blue?
examples.translation: 你知道為什麼天看起來這麼藍嗎？

etymology.text: The noun is derived from Middle English sky (“sky; cloud; mist”), also spelled ski, skie, [and other forms], from Old Norse ský (“cloud”), from Proto-Germanic *skiwją (“cloud; sky”), from *skiwô (“cloud; cloud cover, haze; sky”) (whence Old English sċēo (“cloud”) and Middle English skew (“air; sky; (rare) cloud”)), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kewH- (“to cover; to conceal, hide”).
etymology.native: 這個名詞源自中古英語 sky（天空、雲霧），也寫作 ski、skie 等，來自古諾斯語 ský（雲），再溯源自原始日耳曼語 *skiwją（雲、天空），來自 *skiwô（雲、霧氣、天空），進而影響古英語 sċēo 與中古英語 skew（空氣、天空、罕見的雲）；而這些詞根又來自原始印歐語 *(s)kewH-（覆蓋、隱藏）

senses.definition: The gases surrounding the Earth or any astronomical body.
The air in a particular place.
The conditions (such as music, illumination, etc.) that can influence the mood felt in an environment.
A unit of measurement for pressure equal to 101325 Pa (symbol: atm), approximately the atmospheric pressure at sea level.
The apparent mood felt in an environment.
senses.native: 環境中感受到的明顯情緒氛圍

senses.definition: Extras in a scene who have no spoken lines.
senses.native: 場景中沒有對白線的配角

examples.text: Over 95% of Titan's atmosphere is nitrogen.
examples.translation: 泰坦大氣層超過百分之九十五是氮氣。

examples.text: The atmosphere protects us from meteors.
examples.translation: 大氣層保護我們免受流星撞擊。

examples.text: Can we make Mars' atmosphere breathable?
examples.translation: 我們能讓火星大氣層變得可呼吸嗎？

examples.text: This place has a mysterious atmosphere to it.
examples.translation: 這個地方的氣氛很神秘。

examples.text: The atmosphere in the room was hot and smoky.
examples.translation: 房間裡的大氣層又熱又多煙。

examples.text: The atmosphere is always extremely lively when eating hot pot.
examples.translation: 吃火鍋的時候 ,氣氛往往是非常熱鬧的.

etymology.text: Borrowed from French atmosphère, from New Latin atmosphaera, from Ancient Greek ἀτμός (atmós, “steam”) + σφαῖρα (sphaîra, “sphere”); corresponding to atmo- + -sphere.
etymology.native: 源自法語 atmosphère，來自新拉丁語 atmosphaera，源自古希臘語 ἀτμός（蒸汽）與 σφαῖρα（球體），對應於 atmo- 加上 -sphere。

senses.definition: A rampart of earth, stones etc. built up for defensive purposes.
A structure built for defense surrounding a city, castle etc.
Each of the substantial structures acting either as the exterior of or divisions within a structure.
A point of desperation.
A point of defeat or extinction.
An impediment to free movement.
The butterfly Lasiommata megera.
A barrier.
Something with the apparent solidity, opacity, or dimensions of a building wall.
A means of defence or security.

examples.text: She decorated the wall with pictures.
examples.translation: 她用繪畫來裝飾牆。

examples.text: They are breaking down the wall.
examples.translation: 他們正在拆這面牆。

examples.text: He painted all the walls green.
examples.translation: 他把所有的牆壁漆成了綠色。

examples.text: The wall is thirty yards long.
examples.translation: 這堵牆長三十碼。

examples.text: We're going to paint the wall.
examples.translation: 我們準備刷牆。

examples.text: He painted the picture which is on the wall.
examples.translation: 他畫了牆上的那幅畫。

etymology.text: From Middle English wal, from Old English weall (“wall, dike, earthwork, rampart, dam, rocky shore, cliff”), from Proto-West Germanic *wall (“wall, rampart, entrenchment”), from Latin vallum (“wall, rampart, entrenchment, palisade”), from Proto-Indo-European *welH- (“to turn, wind, roll”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 wal，來自古英語 weall（意為「牆、堤壩、土壩、防禦工事、水壩、岩岸、峭壁」），源自古西日耳曼語 *wall（意為「牆、防禦工事、壕溝」），源自拉丁語 vallum（意為「牆、防禦工蹟、木柵欄」），源自印歐語系原始詞 *welH-（意為「轉動、旋轉、滾動」）

senses.definition: To enclose with, or as if with, a wall or walls.

examples.text: Put these pictures up us for wall, please.

etymology.text: From Middle English wal, from Old English weall (“wall, dike, earthwork, rampart, dam, rocky shore, cliff”), from Proto-West Germanic *wall (“wall, rampart, entrenchment”), from Latin vallum (“wall, rampart, entrenchment, palisade”), from Proto-Indo-European *welH- (“to turn, wind, roll”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 wal，來自古英語 weall（意為「牆、堤壩、土壩、防禦工事、水壩、岩岸、峭壁」），源自古西日耳曼語 *wall（意為「牆、防禦工事、壕溝」），源自拉丁語 vallum（意為「牆、防禦工蹟、木柵欄」），源自印歐語系原始詞 *welH-（意為「轉動、旋轉、滾動」）

senses.definition: Pronunciation spelling of well.

etymology.text: From Middle English wal, from Old English weall (“wall, dike, earthwork, rampart, dam, rocky shore, cliff”), from Proto-West Germanic *wall (“wall, rampart, entrenchment”), from Latin vallum (“wall, rampart, entrenchment, palisade”), from Proto-Indo-European *welH- (“to turn, wind, roll”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 wal，來自古英語 weall（意為「牆、堤壩、土壩、防禦工事、水壩、岩岸、峭壁」），源自古西日耳曼語 *wall（意為「牆、防禦工事、壕溝」），源自拉丁語 vallum（意為「牆、防禦工蹟、木柵欄」），源自印歐語系原始詞 *welH-（意為「轉動、旋轉、滾動」）

senses.definition: Decorative paper-like material used to cover the inner walls of buildings.
An image or tiled pattern used as the background of a computer desktop.
senses.native: 電腦桌布、電腦壁紙、桌面背景

senses.definition: A roll of such paper.
A style or design of such material.
senses.native: 這種材料的樣式或設計

senses.definition: Anything that serves as a background or part of the surroundings.
senses.native: 任何可作為背景或環境一部分的東西

senses.definition: Generic footage of a building or location that may be used in the background of a related news report.
senses.native: 建築或地點的通用影像，可用於相關新聞報導的背景中

senses.definition: Gaudy mass-produced stamps, typically of little or no value and only produced for sale to collectors.
senses.native: 花哨的大批量生產郵票，通常價值極低，僅為賣給收藏家而製造

senses.definition: A radio operator's collection of awards and QSL cards.
senses.native: 無線電操作員的獎盃與 QSL 卡片收藏

examples.text: The walls were covered with wallpaper.
examples.translation: 牆壁被貼上了牆紙。

examples.text: Why are you using that wallpaper?
examples.translation: 為什麼你要用那種牆紙？

examples.text: The wallpaper had to be reglued.
examples.translation: 牆紙必須重新黏合。

examples.text: I'm not sure I like the damask wallpaper, Tom.
examples.translation: 我不確定我喜歡那款達馬斯克紋路的牆紙，湯姆。

examples.text: I still need to buy linoleum and wallpaper.
examples.translation: 我仍然需要購買塑膠地板革和牆紙。

examples.text: Claudio set the picture as his desktop wallpaper.

etymology.text: From wall + paper.
etymology.native: 由「牆」與「紙」組合而成。

senses.definition: The feel or shape of a surface or substance; the smoothness, roughness, softness, etc. of something.
The quality given to a work of art by the composition and interaction of its parts.
An image applied to a polygon to create the appearance of a surface.
The act or art of weaving.
Something woven; a woven fabric; a web.
A tissue.

examples.text: Avocados have a buttery texture.
examples.translation: 酪梨口感柔滑。

examples.text: Sea urchin has a slimy texture.
examples.translation: 海膽口感黏滑。

examples.text: I really like the crisp texture of gizzards.
examples.translation: 我真的很喜歡鴨脷的脆口感。

examples.text: The bletted medlars had an apple sauce texture.
examples.translation: 那顆壞掉的梅子口感像蘋果醬。

examples.text: Line art emphasizes form and outline, over color, shading, and texture.
examples.translation: 線條藝術強調形式和輪廓，而不是顏色、陰影和紋理。

examples.text: The taste is fine, but the texture is awful.
examples.translation: 味道還算不錯，但口感很糟糕。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French texture, borrowed from Latin textūra (“a weaving, web, texture, structure”), from textus, past participle of texere (“to weave”). See text. Doublet of tessitura.

senses.definition: To create or apply a texture.

examples.text: Drag the trowel through the plaster to texture the wall.
examples.translation: 用鏟子在灰泥上拖曳，以製造牆面紋理。

examples.text: The floor here is invisible because the game's devs forgot to texture it.
examples.translation: 這裡的地板因為遊戲開發者忘記貼圖，所以看不見。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French texture, borrowed from Latin textūra (“a weaving, web, texture, structure”), from textus, past participle of texere (“to weave”). See text. Doublet of tessitura.

senses.definition: Having an intense texture; with a texture that causes a strong (often positive) reaction.

etymology.text: Borrowed from Middle French texture, borrowed from Latin textūra (“a weaving, web, texture, structure”), from textus, past participle of texere (“to weave”). See text. Doublet of tessitura.

senses.definition: Flowing freely like water; fluid; not solid and not gaseous; composed of particles that move freely among each other on the slightest pressure.
Easily sold or disposed of without losing value.
Having sufficient trading activity to make buying or selling easy.
Flowing or sounding smoothly or without abrupt transitions or harsh tones.
Belonging to a class of consonants comprising the laterals and the rhotics, which in many languages behave similarly.
Fluid and transparent.

examples.text: Water is liquid.
examples.translation: 水是液體。

examples.text: Quicksilver, always liquid, corrodes metals.
examples.translation: 銀液，永遠呈液態，會腐蝕金屬。

examples.text: You should drink a lot of liquid.
examples.translation: 你應該喝大量的液體。

examples.text: Water is liquid. When it freezes, it becomes solid.
examples.translation: 水是液體。凍起來就成了固體。

examples.text: I don't like to use liquid laundry detergent.
examples.translation: 我不喜歡用洗衣精。

examples.text: A substance can be solid, gaseous, or liquid.
examples.translation: 一種物質可以是固態、氣態或液態。

etymology.text: From Middle English liquide, from Old French liquide, from Latin liquidus (“fluid, liquid, moist”), from liqueō (“to be liquid, be fluid”). Doublet of liquidus. As a term for a consonant, it comes from Latin liquida (cōnsōnāns), a calque of Ancient Greek ὑγρὸν (σύμφωνον) (hugròn (súmphōnon), “liquid consonant”).

senses.definition: filled or brimming with tears
applied to a fish depicted horizontally

examples.text: The red fish is swimming lazily in the lake.
examples.translation: 紅色的魚在湖裡懶洋洋地游泳。

examples.text: The red fish is swimming in the ocean.
examples.translation: 紅色的魚在海裡游。

etymology.text: From Middle English swymmynge. Equivalent to swim (“to move through water”, verb) + -ing (suffix forming gerunds).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 swymmynge，等於 swim（意為「在水中移動」，動詞）+ -ing（形成分詞的後綴）

senses.definition: A pigment (or dye)-based fluid used for writing, printing etc.
The black or dark-colored fluid ejected by squid, octopus etc, as a protective strategy.
A particular type, color or container of this fluid.
senses.native: 此流體的特定類型、顏色或容器

senses.definition: Publicity.
Tattoo work.
Cheap red wine.

examples.text: This blotting paper absorbs ink well.
The black ink stained the paper.
She was asked to write her name in ink.
examples.translation: 她被要求用墨水寫下她的名字。

examples.text: An octopus can release ink when it gets into danger.
examples.translation: 章魚遇到危險時會噴出墨汁。

examples.text: My ballpoint pen just ran out of ink.
examples.translation: 我的原珠筆沒墨了。

examples.text: Please replace the empty ink cartridge in the printer.
examples.translation: 請把印表機裡面的空的墨粉鼓換掉。

etymology.text: From Middle English ynke, from Old French enque, from Latin encaustum (“purple ink used by Roman emperors to sign documents”), from Ancient Greek ἔγκαυστον (énkauston, “burned-in”), from ἐν (en, “in”) + καίω (kaíō, “burn”). In this sense, displaced native Old English blæc (“ink”, literally “black”).

senses.definition: A container.
The part of the flower stalk (peduncle or pedicel) to which the floral parts are attached; a thalamus, a torus.
senses.native: 花莖上附著花部的部位；花托或花梗

senses.definition: A condensed rachis of a capitate or umbellate inflorescence at the end of the peduncle, to which all of the florets or pedicels are attached.
senses.native: 頂生於花莖末端、所有小花或花梗均附著其上的縮短花軸

senses.definition: A structure at the end of a branch of an alga containing conceptacles (reproductive organs).
senses.native: 藻類枝條末端包含生殖器官（概念囊）的結構

senses.definition: An organ that receives and holds a secretion.
senses.native: 接收並儲存分泌物的器官

senses.definition: A contact device installed at an outlet for the connection of an attachment plug (typically by receiving the plug's prongs) to supply portable appliances or equipment.
senses.native: 安裝於插座以連接插頭（通常接收插腳）供電給可攜式設備的接觸裝置

examples.text: The eye socket is the bone receptacle in which the eye fits.
examples.translation: 眼窩是裝載眼球的花托骨。

examples.text: The waterskin is a sheepskin or goat skin sewn in the shape of a bag and serving as a receptacle.
examples.translation: 水囊是用羊皮或牛皮縫製成袋狀，作為容器的皮囊。

examples.text: Thus, one of the loveliest of earthly paradises was doomed to be a receptacle for the very worst of malefactors.
examples.translation: 因此，這世上最美麗的樂園之一，注定要成為最惡劣罪犯的收容所。

examples.text: Maria Montessori invented the sorting box after observing that children enjoy fitting objects through receptacles of a similar shape.
examples.translation: 瑪麗亞·蒙台梭利觀察到兒童喜歡將物件放入形狀相似的容器中後，發明了分類盒。

examples.text: The old vase served as a unique receptacle for flowers.
examples.translation: 那隻舊花瓶被用作存放花朵的獨特容器。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The antique urn functioned as an elegant receptacle for ceremonial offerings.
examples.translation: 那座古董壺被用作盛放儀式供品的優雅容器。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From Middle English receptacle, from Anglo-Norman receptacle and Middle French receptacle (“organ containing a fluid; gathering place; water basin”) (modern French réceptacle), from Latin receptāculum (“animal enclosure, container, place of refuge, receptacle, repository, reservoir, shelter”), from receptāre (“to harbour, to receive, to shelter”) or receptō (“to receive back or again, to recover”), frequentative of recipiō (“to receive; to hold back, to reserve”) (from re- (“back, again”) + capi
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 receptacle，來自盎格魯諾曼語和中古法語（意為「含液體的器官；聚集處；水盆」），現代法語 réceptacle 則來自拉丁語 receptāculum。

senses.definition: That serves to decorate
That has no functional purpose.

examples.text: The bed is adorned with decorative pillows.
examples.translation: 床鋪上擺著裝飾性枕頭。

examples.text: In some cultures, antlers are used for decorative or ceremonial purposes.
examples.translation: 在某些文化中，鹿角被用於裝飾或儀式用途。

examples.text: There was a decorative pilaster to either side of the building's entrance.
examples.translation: 建築入口兩側各有一個裝飾性壁柱。

examples.text: To spice up the design, he added some decorative shapes with a dingbat font.
examples.translation: 為了增添設計感，他用了一種標點字體加入一些裝飾性圖形。

examples.text: Today Mary is wearing elegant decorative glasses.
examples.translation: 今天瑪麗戴著精緻的裝飾眼鏡。

examples.text: Tessellations have been used to create decorative motifs in both textiles and architecture since ancient times.
examples.translation: 自古以來，馬賽克圖案就被用於紡織品與建築的裝飾紋樣。

etymology.text: From Latin decorātus + -ive. Cognate with French décoratif.
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 decorātus 加 -ive。與法語 décoratif 同源。

senses.definition: A plant, tile, etc. intended for use as decoration.

etymology.text: From Latin decorātus + -ive. Cognate with French décoratif.
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 decorātus 加 -ive。與法語 décoratif 同源。

senses.definition: Any of a number of chemical elements in the periodic table that form a metallic bond with other metal atoms; generally shiny, somewhat malleable and hard, often a conductor of heat and electricity.
Any material with similar physical properties as those chemical elements, especially as a combination of several of them, such as an alloy.
A category of rock music encompassing a number of genres (including thrash metal, death metal, etc.) characterized by strong drumbeats and distorted guitars.
An element which was not directly created after the Big Bang but instead formed through nuclear reactions; any element other than hydrogen and helium.
Crushed rock, stones etc. used to make a road.
The ore from which a metal is derived.
A mine from which ores are taken.
A light tincture used in a coat of arms, specifically argent (white or silver) and or (gold).
Molten glass that is to be blown or moulded to form objects.
The substance that constitutes something or someone; matter; hence, character or temper.

examples.text: Coins are made of metal.
examples.translation: 硬幣是金屬做的。

examples.text: I have a metal table.
examples.translation: 我有一張金屬桌子。

examples.text: Why did you think that Tom liked heavy metal?
examples.translation: 你為什麼覺得湯姆喜歡重金屬樂隊？

examples.text: Nickel is a hard metal with a silvery luster.
examples.translation: 鎳是一種堅硬、銀光閃閃的金屬。

examples.text: Acids react chemically with metals.
examples.translation: 酸會和金屬物質起化學反應。

examples.text: The value of a coin depends on the weight of the metal used.
examples.translation: 錢幣的價值取決於所使用的金屬的重量。

etymology.text: From Middle English metal, a borrowing from Old French metal, from Latin metallum (“metal, mine, quarry, mineral”), itself a borrowing from Ancient Greek μέταλλον (métallon, “mine, quarry, metal”).

senses.definition: Characterized by strong drum-beats and distorted guitars.

examples.text: This ladder is metal.

etymology.text: From Middle English metal, a borrowing from Old French metal, from Latin metallum (“metal, mine, quarry, mineral”), itself a borrowing from Ancient Greek μέταλλον (métallon, “mine, quarry, metal”).

senses.definition: To make a road using crushed rock, stones etc.

etymology.text: From Middle English metal, a borrowing from Old French metal, from Latin metallum (“metal, mine, quarry, mineral”), itself a borrowing from Ancient Greek μέταλλον (métallon, “mine, quarry, metal”).

senses.definition: Of, relating to, or characteristic of metal.
Made of or containing metal.
senses.native: 由金屬製成或含有金屬的

senses.definition: Harsh, as if coming from two metals striking one another.
senses.native: 刺耳，如同兩塊金屬相互碰撞的聲音

senses.definition: Having the appearance of being of polished metal.

examples.text: My bicycle was painted metallic blue.
examples.translation: 我的腳踏車塗成了金屬藍色。

examples.text: Tom's new bicycle is metallic red.
examples.translation: 湯姆的新腳踏車是金屬紅色。

examples.text: It has a metallic luster.
examples.translation: 它具有金屬光澤。

examples.text: The moon shines with a metallic light.
examples.translation: 月亮散發出金屬般的光芒。

examples.text: A metallic note sounded in his voice.
examples.translation: 他的聲音中傳來一種金屬般的音符聲。

examples.text: He heard some sort of metallic buzzing.
examples.translation: 他聽到某種金屬嗡嗡聲。

etymology.text: From Latin metallicus, from metallum (“metal”), from Ancient Greek μέταλλον (métallon). Equivalent to metal + -ic.
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 metallicus，來自 metallum（金屬），源自古希臘語 μέταλλον。等同於 metal 加上 -ic 詞尾。

senses.definition: Made of bronze metal.
Having a reddish-brown colour.
Tanned; darkened as a result of exposure to the sun.

etymology.text: From French bronze (1511); from Italian bronzo (13th c.), of uncertain origin (q.v.). First use appears c. 1721 in the writings of Matthew Prior (for which, see citation below).
etymology.native: 源自法語 bronze（1511 年）；來自義大利語 bronzo（13 世紀），起源不明。首次使用約於 1721 年，見馬修·普爾的文集。

senses.definition: A small ticket or sign giving information about something to which it is attached or intended to be attached.
A name given to something or someone to categorise them as part of a particular social group.
A company that sells records.
A user-defined alias for a numerical designation, the reverse of an enumeration.
A named place in source code that can be jumped to using a GOTO or equivalent construct.
A charge resembling the strap crossing the horse’s chest from which pendants are hung.
A tassel.
A small strip, especially of paper or parchment (or of some material attached to parchment to carry the seal), but also of iron, brass, land, etc.
A piece of writing added to something, such as a codicil appended to a will.
A brass rule with sights, formerly used with a circumferentor to take altitudes.
The projecting moulding by the sides, and over the tops, of openings in mediaeval architecture.

examples.text: The contents of the box are listed on the label.
examples.translation: 箱子的內容在標籤上面寫著。

examples.text: Tom picked up the jar and read the label.
examples.translation: 湯姆拿起罐子讀標籤。

examples.text: Use a marker on the case label, not the disc.
examples.translation: 請在盒蓋標籤上使用記號筆，不要用在碟片上。

examples.text: He attached a "Fragile" label to the package.
examples.translation: 他把「易碎」標籤貼在包裝上。

examples.text: Observers note that animals don't conform to human labels.
examples.translation: 觀察者注意到動物不符合人類的標籤。

examples.text: In the first paragraph, she describes the labels she was tagged with, which have a negative connotation.
examples.translation: 在第一段中，她描述了自己被貼上的標籤，這些標籤具有負面含義。

etymology.text: From Middle English label (“narrow band, strip of cloth”), from Old French label, lambel (Modern French lambeau), from Frankish *lappā (“torn piece of cloth”), from Proto-Germanic *lappǭ, *lappô (“cloth stuff, rag, scraps, flap, dewlap, lobe, rabbit ear”), from Proto-Indo-European *leb- (“blade”). Cognate with Old High German lappa (“rag, piece of cloth”), Old English læppa (“skirt, flap of a garment”). More at lap.
etymology.native: 「label」源自中世英文，意為「窄帶、布條」，來源於古法文 label、lambel（現代法文 lambeau），再溯源自古弗蘭克語 *lappā（意為「撕裂的布片」），而古德語 *lappǭ、*lappô（意為「布料、碎布、翻邊、下垂的皮毛、耳廓」），源自印歐語系 *leb-（意為「刀片」）。與古高地德語 lappa（意為「布頭、布片」）、古英語 læppa（意為「裙襬、衣物的翻邊」）同源。詳見 lap。

senses.definition: To put a label (a ticket or sign) on (something).

examples.text: I soon came across a box labeled Terry Tate.
examples.translation: 我很快便發現了一個標有「特里·泰特」字樣的盒子。

examples.text: Oleg is always labeled as naive.
examples.translation: 奧列格總被標籤為天真。

examples.text: They labeled him deviant simply because he thought differently.
examples.translation: 他們僅因他想法不同，便將他標籤為異類。

examples.text: The shop assistant labeled all the products in the shop.
examples.translation: 店員將店內所有商品標上價格。

examples.text: Trump labeled Vietnam a currency manipulator.
examples.translation: 特朗普將越南標籤為貨幣操控者。

etymology.text: From Middle English label (“narrow band, strip of cloth”), from Old French label, lambel (Modern French lambeau), from Frankish *lappā (“torn piece of cloth”), from Proto-Germanic *lappǭ, *lappô (“cloth stuff, rag, scraps, flap, dewlap, lobe, rabbit ear”), from Proto-Indo-European *leb- (“blade”). Cognate with Old High German lappa (“rag, piece of cloth”), Old English læppa (“skirt, flap of a garment”). More at lap.
etymology.native: 「label」源自中世英文，意為「窄帶、布條」，來源於古法文 label、lambel（現代法文 lambeau），再溯源自古弗蘭克語 *lappā（意為「撕裂的布片」），而古德語 *lappǭ、*lappô（意為「布料、碎布、翻邊、下垂的皮毛、耳廓」），源自印歐語系 *leb-（意為「刀片」）。與古高地德語 lappa（意為「布頭、布片」）、古英語 læppa（意為「裙襬、衣物的翻邊」）同源。詳見 lap。

senses.definition: Having an absolute or (more often) relative lack of light.
Dull or deeper in hue; not bright or light.
Without moral or spiritual light; sinister, malevolent, malign.
Extinguished.
Deprived of sight; blind.
Transmitting, reflecting, or receiving inadequate light to render timely discernment or comprehension
Ambiguously or unclearly expressed.
Marked by or conducted with secrecy.
Having racing capability not widely known.
Conducive to hopelessness; depressing or bleak.

examples.text: The sky became darker and darker.
examples.translation: 天空變得越來越暗了。

examples.text: She was wearing dark brown shoes.
examples.translation: 她穿著深褐色的鞋子。

examples.text: It's getting darker and darker.
examples.translation: 越來越黑了。

examples.text: She likes to wear dark colours.
examples.translation: 她喜歡穿深顏色的衣服。

examples.text: What are you doing in a dark place like that?
examples.translation: 你在那麼暗的地方做什麼？

examples.text: It's really dark here. I can't see anything.
examples.translation: 這裡真的很暗，我什麼都看不到。

etymology.text: From Middle English derk, from Old English deorc, from Proto-West Germanic *derk (“dark”), of uncertain origin, but possibly from Proto-Indo-European *dʰerg- (“dim, dull”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰer- (“dull, dirty”).
etymology.native: 「dark」源自中世紀英文 derk，來源為古英語 deorc，再溯自古西日耳曼語 *derk（意為「黑暗」），起源不明，但可能來自印歐語系 *dʰerg-（意為「昏暗、黯淡」），而 *dʰer-（意為「黯淡、汙穢」）

senses.definition: A complete or (more often) partial absence of light.

examples.text: She groped for the light switch in the dark.
examples.translation: 她摸黑摸不到燈的開關。

etymology.text: From Middle English derk, from Old English deorc, from Proto-West Germanic *derk (“dark”), of uncertain origin, but possibly from Proto-Indo-European *dʰerg- (“dim, dull”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰer- (“dull, dirty”).
etymology.native: 「dark」源自中世紀英文 derk，來源為古英語 deorc，再溯自古西日耳曼語 *derk（意為「黑暗」），起源不明，但可能來自印歐語系 *dʰerg-（意為「昏暗、黯淡」），而 *dʰer-（意為「黯淡、汙穢」）

senses.definition: To grow or become dark, darken.

etymology.text: From Middle English derk, from Old English deorc, from Proto-West Germanic *derk (“dark”), of uncertain origin, but possibly from Proto-Indo-European *dʰerg- (“dim, dull”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰer- (“dull, dirty”).
etymology.native: 「dark」源自中世紀英文 derk，來源為古英語 deorc，再溯自古西日耳曼語 *derk（意為「黑暗」），起源不明，但可能來自印歐語系 *dʰerg-（意為「昏暗、黯淡」），而 *dʰer-（意為「黯淡、汙穢」）

senses.definition: Absorbing all light and reflecting none; dark and hueless.
Without light.
Belonging to or descended from any of various (African, Aboriginal, etc.) ethnic groups which typically have dark pigmentation of the skin. (See usage notes below.)
Belonging to or descended from any of various sub-Saharan African ethnic groups which typically have dark pigmentation of the skin.
Designated for use by those ethnic groups (as described above).
Of the spades or clubs suits.
Bad; evil; ill-omened.
Expressing menace or discontent; threatening; sullen.
Illegitimate, illegal, or disgraced.
Foul; dirty, soiled.

examples.text: The blackbirds' feathers are black.
examples.translation: 烏鶇的羽毛是黑色的。

examples.text: That black bird isn't a blackbird.
examples.translation: 那隻黑鳥不是烏鶇。

examples.text: This isn't Little Black is it?
examples.translation: 這不是小黑嗎？

examples.text: He always drinks black coffee.
examples.translation: 他總喝他的黑咖啡。

examples.text: I've had black rice congee thrice in one day!
examples.translation: 我一天吃了三次黑米粥！

examples.text: Is the water in the Black Sea actually black?
examples.translation: 黑海里的水事實上是黑的嗎？

etymology.text: From Middle English blak, black, blake, from Old English blæc (“black, dark", also "ink”), from Proto-West Germanic *blak, from Proto-Germanic *blakaz (“burnt”), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *bʰleg- (“to burn, shine”).

senses.definition: Disastrous, calamitous.
Disappointingly inadequate.
Causing despair; gloomy and bleak.
senses.native: 令人絕望；陰鬱而蕭瑟的

senses.definition: Depressing, dreary, cheerless.

examples.text: The house looked very dismal.
examples.translation: 那棟房子看起來非常蕭瑟。

examples.text: The rain made the autumn day dismal.
examples.translation: 雨讓秋天的日子陰沉沉的。

examples.text: The prospects for Japan's future look dismal.
examples.translation: 日本未來的前景看起來相當黯淡。

examples.text: The flyover provides a dismal view of slum dwellings.
examples.translation: 高架橋提供了貧民窟居民令人沮喪的視野。

examples.text: Edison's talking doll was a dismal failure.
examples.translation: 愛迪生的會話娃娃是一次令人失望的失敗。

examples.text: It was a dismal failure.
examples.translation: 這是一次令人沮喪的失敗。

etymology.text: From Middle English dismal, dismale, from Anglo-Norman dismal, from Old French (li) dis mals (“(the) bad days”), from Medieval Latin diēs malī (“bad days”).
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 dismal 與 dismale，來自盎格魯 - 諾曼語的 dismal，再源自舊法語的 (li) dis mals（意指「壞日子」），最終追溯至中世紀拉丁文的 diēs malī（意指「壞日子」）。

senses.definition: A substance composed of a large collection of bubbles or their solidified remains, especially
A collection of small bubbles created when the surface of a body of water is moved by tides, wind, etc.
A collection of small bubbles formed from bodily fluids such as saliva or sweat.
A collection of small bubbles on the surface of a liquid that is heated, fermented or carbonated.
A collection of small bubbles created by mixing soap with water.
A collection of small bubbles formed by mixing an extinguishing agent with water, used to cover and extinguish fires.
A food prepared in the form of a mass of airy bubbles.
A material formed by trapping pockets of gas in a liquid or solid.
The sea.
Fury, rage, ire.
Sneakers.

examples.text: Most shoe soles nowadays are made from foam.
examples.translation: 如今大多數鞋底都是泡沫材質。

examples.text: Beer isn't beer without a nice layer of foam.
examples.translation: 沒有漂亮泡沫層的啤酒就不算啤酒。

examples.text: I like my coffee with lots of foam on the top.
examples.translation: 我喜歡咖啡頂層有厚厚一層泡沫。

examples.text: The seat cushions were filled with foam rubber.
examples.translation: 座墊內填充的是泡沫橡膠。

examples.text: Tom unrolled his sleeping bag on his foam pad.
examples.translation: 湯姆把睡袋鋪在泡沫墊上。

examples.text: Tom put a foam pad under his sleeping bag.
examples.translation: 湯姆在睡袋下放了一個泡沫墊。

etymology.text: From Middle English fom, foom, from Old English fām, from Proto-West Germanic *faim, from Proto-Germanic *faimaz, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)poHy-m-os, from *(s)poH(y)- (“foam”). Cognate with German Feim (“foam”), Latin spūma (“foam”), Latin pūmex (“pumice”), Sanskrit फेन (phéna, “foam”), possibly Northern Kurdish fê (“epilepsy”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 fom、foom，來自古英語 fām，源自原始西日耳曼語 *faim，再源自原始德語 *faimaz，來自原始印歐語 *(s)poHy-m-os，源自 *(s)poH(y)-（意為「泡沫」）。與德語 Feim（泡沫）、拉丁語 spūma（泡沫）、拉丁語 pūmex（火山岩）、梵語 फेन (phéna，意為「泡沫」）同源，可能也與庫爾德語 fê（意為「癲癇」）有關。

senses.definition: To form or emit foam.

examples.text: He was foaming at the mouth.
examples.translation: 他嘴裡泡沫滿溢。

examples.text: James was practically foaming at the mouth.
examples.translation: 詹姆斯幾乎嘴裡泡沫滿溢。

examples.text: The river was foaming.
examples.translation: 河水泛著泡沫。

etymology.text: From Middle English fom, foom, from Old English fām, from Proto-West Germanic *faim, from Proto-Germanic *faimaz, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)poHy-m-os, from *(s)poH(y)- (“foam”). Cognate with German Feim (“foam”), Latin spūma (“foam”), Latin pūmex (“pumice”), Sanskrit फेन (phéna, “foam”), possibly Northern Kurdish fê (“epilepsy”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 fom、foom，來自古英語 fām，源自原始西日耳曼語 *faim，再源自原始德語 *faimaz，來自原始印歐語 *(s)poHy-m-os，源自 *(s)poH(y)-（意為「泡沫」）。與德語 Feim（泡沫）、拉丁語 spūma（泡沫）、拉丁語 pūmex（火山岩）、梵語 फेन (phéna，意為「泡沫」）同源，可能也與庫爾德語 fê（意為「癲癇」）有關。

senses.definition: Of a liquid or other substance, or a container holding it: to be boiled (vigorously); to become boiling hot.
Of a liquid, vapor, etc., or a container holding it: to foam or froth in an agitated manner, as if boiling.
Of a person: to be in an agitated or angry mental state, often in a way that is not obvious to others.
Of a place: to be filled with many people or things moving about actively; to buzz with activity; also, of people or things: to move about actively in a crowd or group.
Of a place: to have inhabitants in an angry or disaffected mood; to be in a state of unrest.
To overboil (something) so that it loses its flavour or texture; hence (figurative), to cause (the body, the mind, the spirit, etc.) to become dull through too much alcoholic drink or heat.
To soak (something) in a liquid; to drench, to steep.
To boil (something); especially, to cook (food) by boiling or stewing; also, to keep (something) boiling.
Of the stomach: to digest (food).

examples.text: The square was seething with people.
examples.translation: 廣場裡人聲鼎沸。

examples.text: He talks to me, I seethe inside.
examples.translation: 他跟我說話，我內心憤怒煩躁。

examples.text: The country seethed over the issue of national defense.
examples.translation: 國家對國防議題民怨沸騰。

examples.text: Mary is seething with rage she feels unable to express.
examples.translation: 瑪麗怒火中燒卻無法表達。

examples.text: Rodrigo was seething in anger.
examples.translation: 羅德里戈怒氣沖沖。

examples.text: When the scandal broke, the Congressman's constituents were seething.
examples.translation: 丑聞曝光後，眾議員的選民們民怨沸騰。

etymology.text: The verb is derived from Middle English sethen, seeth (“to boil, seethe; to cook; etc.”) [and other forms], from Old English sēoþan (“to boil, seethe; to cook; etc.”), from Proto-West Germanic *seuþan, from Proto-Germanic *seuþaną (“to boil, seethe”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂sewt-, *h₂sew-, *h₂sut- (“to move about, roil, seethe”).
etymology.native: 此動詞源於中古英語 sethen 與古英語 sēoþan，皆來自日耳曼語系中表示「沸騰」的詞根。

senses.definition: To fit, as for a specific end or purpose; make suitable or comfortable; adapt; adjust.
To construct by fitting together or uniting various parts; fabricate by union of constituent parts.
To bring or put into form or order; adjust the parts or elements of; compose; contrive; plan; devise.
To put together the structural elements of (a constructed object such as a building).
To place (a picture such as a painting or photograph) inside a decorative border.
To position visually within a fixed boundary.
To construct in words so as to establish a context for understanding or interpretation.
Conspire to falsely incriminate an innocent person.
To wash ore with the aid of a frame.
To move.
To proceed; to go.

examples.text: He was framed by his wife.
examples.translation: 他被妻子誣陷了。

examples.text: This will be framed and hung up on the wall.
examples.translation: 這件作品將被裝裱好掛在牆上。

examples.text: All have sworn him an oath that they should frame his will on earth.
examples.translation: 所有人都向他起誓，要依照他的意志在世上行事。

examples.text: The frame itself is worth more than the picture.
examples.translation: 畫框比畫還值錢。

examples.text: Once we finish framing the house, we'll hang tin on the roof.
examples.translation: 等我們完成房屋的裝裱，就該在屋頂鋪鐵皮了。

examples.text: The director frames the fishing scene very well.
examples.translation: 導演拍漁場場景的構圖非常出色。

etymology.text: From Middle English framen, fremen, fremmen (“to construct, build, strengthen, refresh, perform, execute, profit, avail”), from Old English framian, fremian, fremman (“to profit, avail, advance”), from Proto-West Germanic *frammjan, from Proto-Germanic *framjaną (“to further, promote, perform”), from Proto-Indo-European *promo- (“front, forward”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 framen, fremen, fremmen（意為「建造、強化、更新、執行、獲益」），來自古英語 framian, fremian, fremman（意為「獲益、前進」），再溯源自古西日耳曼語 *frammjan，再溯源自古德語 *framjaną（意為「推進、執行」），最終源自印歐語系 *promo-（意為「前進、向前」）。

senses.definition: The structural elements of a building or other constructed object.

examples.text: They painted the window frames yellow.
examples.translation: 她們把窗框塗成了黃色。

examples.text: The most important thing in art is the frame.
examples.translation: 藝術中最重要的是畫框。

examples.text: His portrait was mounted in the fancy frame.
examples.translation: 他的肖像畫掛在精緻的畫框裡。

examples.text: The frame is worth more than the painting.
examples.translation: 畫框比畫還值錢。

examples.text: This picture frame can make the picture rise in value.
examples.translation: 這個畫框能讓畫升值。

examples.text: The entire frame is made of iron.
examples.translation: 整個框架由鐵金屬製成。

etymology.text: From Middle English framen, fremen, fremmen (“to construct, build, strengthen, refresh, perform, execute, profit, avail”), from Old English framian, fremian, fremman (“to profit, avail, advance”), from Proto-West Germanic *frammjan, from Proto-Germanic *framjaną (“to further, promote, perform”), from Proto-Indo-European *promo- (“front, forward”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 framen, fremen, fremmen（意為「建造、強化、更新、執行、獲益」），來自古英語 framian, fremian, fremman（意為「獲益、前進」），再溯源自古西日耳曼語 *frammjan，再溯源自古德語 *framjaną（意為「推進、執行」），最終源自印歐語系 *promo-（意為「前進、向前」）。

senses.definition: A drawing or diagram conveying information.
The representation of any form, as by drawing, painting, modelling, carving, embroidering, etc.; especially, a representation of the human body.
A person, thing, or action representative of another
The appearance or impression made by the conduct or career of a person.
A human figure, which dress or corset must fit to; the shape of a human body.
A numeral.
A number, an amount.
A shape.
A visible pattern as in wood or cloth.
Any complex dance moveᵂ.
Distinguished appearance; magnificence; conspicuous representation; splendour; show.

examples.text: She has as fine a figure as I have ever seen.

senses.definition: The natural constitution, or physical structure, of a person.
The trained muscular structure of a person's body.
senses.native: 人體訓練過的肌肉結構

examples.text: He has a soccer-player physique.
examples.translation: 他擁有足球運動員般的體態。

examples.text: Himmler had a frail physique.
examples.translation: 希姆萊的體態十分虛弱。

examples.text: Tom has a great physique.
examples.translation: 湯姆擁有一副健美的體態。

examples.text: Fortunately, her physique was perfect.
examples.translation: 幸運的是，她的體態完美無缺。

examples.text: Tom has the perfect physique for a world-class rower.
examples.translation: 湯姆擁有世界級划船手所需的完美體態。

examples.text: William has a weaker physique than other boys his age.
examples.translation: 威廉的體態不如同齡的其他男孩強壯。

etymology.text: From French physique.
etymology.native: 源自法語 physique 一詞。

senses.definition: An individual who has been granted personhood; usually a human being.
A character or part, as in a play; a specific kind or manifestation of individual character, whether in real life, or in literary or dramatic representation; an assumed character.
A human of unspecified gender (in terms usually constructed with man or woman).
The physical body of a being seen as distinct from the mind, character, etc.
Any individual or formal organization with standing before the courts.
A linguistic category used to distinguish between the speaker of an utterance and those to whom or about whom they are speaking. See grammatical person.
Any one of the three hypostases of the Holy Trinity: the Father, Son, or Holy Spirit.
Any sapient or socially intelligent being.
Someone who likes or has an affinity for (a specified thing).
A worker in a specified function or specialty.
The human genitalia; specifically, the penis.

examples.text: People established churches and schools there.
examples.translation: 人們在那裡建立了教堂和學校。

examples.text: The Japanese people have renounced war.
examples.translation: 日本人放棄了戰爭。

examples.text: The Japanese are an industrious people.
examples.translation: 日本人是勤勞的民族。

examples.text: I'm always forgetting people's names.
examples.translation: 我總是忘記別人的名字。

examples.text: He liberated the people from bondage.
examples.translation: 他讓人們擺脫了奴役。

examples.text: People who will lie for you, will lie to you.
examples.translation: 會為你說謊的人，就會對你說謊。

etymology.text: From Middle English persoun, personne et al., from Anglo-Norman parsone, persoun et al. (Old French persone (“human being”), French personne), and its source Latin persōna (“mask used by actor; role, part, character”), perhaps a loanword from Etruscan 𐌘𐌄𐌓𐌔𐌖 (φersu, “mask”). In this sense, displaced native man, which came to mean primarily "adult male" in Middle English; see Old English mann. Displaced native Old English hād (“person, individual”). Doublet of parson and persona.
etymology.native: 「人」一詞源於中古英語的 persoun，其後可追溯至盎格魯 - 諾曼語的 parsone 與 persoone，再源自古法語 personne（意為「人類」）及現代法語 personne。

senses.definition: A hard earthen substance that can form rocks; especially, such substance when regarded as a building material.
A piece of such material: a block of stone, rock or a pebble.
A hard, stone-like deposit.
A gemstone, a jewel, especially a diamond.
A unit of weight equal to 14 pounds (≈6.3503 kilograms), formerly used for various commodities (wool, cheese, etc.), but now principally used for personal weight. Abbreviated as st.
The central part of some fruits, particularly drupes; consisting of the seed and a hard endocarp layer.
A playing piece made of any hard material, used in various board games such as backgammon and go.
A dull light grey or beige, like that of some stones.
A 42-pound, precisely shaped piece of granite with a handle attached, which is bowled down the ice.

examples.text: Don't throw stones into the river.
examples.translation: 不要扔石頭到河裡。

examples.text: She picked up beautiful stones.
examples.translation: 她撿了許多漂亮的小石頭。

examples.text: I build houses out of stone.
examples.translation: 我建石頭房子。

examples.text: What kind of stone is this?
examples.translation: 這是什麼石頭？

examples.text: He threw a stone at the big dog.
examples.translation: 他朝著大狗扔了塊石頭。

examples.text: Don't throw a stone at the dog.
examples.translation: 不要對狗丟石頭。

etymology.text: From Middle English ston, stone, stan, from Old English stān, from Proto-West Germanic *stain, from Proto-Germanic *stainaz (“stone”), from Proto-Indo-European *steyh₂- (“to stiffen”).
etymology.native: 來源於中世紀英文 ston、stone、stan，源自古英文 stān，再溯自古西日耳曼語 *stain，再溯自古德語 *stainaz（意為「石頭」），最終源自印歐語系 *steyh₂-（意為「變硬」）

senses.definition: Constructed of stone.

etymology.text: From Middle English ston, stone, stan, from Old English stān, from Proto-West Germanic *stain, from Proto-Germanic *stainaz (“stone”), from Proto-Indo-European *steyh₂- (“to stiffen”).
etymology.native: 來源於中世紀英文 ston、stone、stan，源自古英文 stān，再溯自古西日耳曼語 *stain，再溯自古德語 *stainaz（意為「石頭」），最終源自印歐語系 *steyh₂-（意為「變硬」）

senses.definition: As a stone (used with following adjective).

etymology.text: From Middle English ston, stone, stan, from Old English stān, from Proto-West Germanic *stain, from Proto-Germanic *stainaz (“stone”), from Proto-Indo-European *steyh₂- (“to stiffen”).
etymology.native: 來源於中世紀英文 ston、stone、stan，源自古英文 stān，再溯自古西日耳曼語 *stain，再溯自古德語 *stainaz（意為「石頭」），最終源自印歐語系 *steyh₂-（意為「變硬」）

senses.definition: To pelt with stones; especially, to kill by pelting with stones.

examples.text: Kill two birds with one stone.
examples.translation: 一石二鳥。

examples.text: That way I kill two birds with one stone.
examples.translation: 這樣子我一箭雙鵰。

etymology.text: From Middle English ston, stone, stan, from Old English stān, from Proto-West Germanic *stain, from Proto-Germanic *stainaz (“stone”), from Proto-Indo-European *steyh₂- (“to stiffen”).
etymology.native: 來源於中世紀英文 ston、stone、stan，源自古英文 stān，再溯自古西日耳曼語 *stain，再溯自古德語 *stainaz（意為「石頭」），最終源自印歐語系 *steyh₂-（意為「變硬」）

senses.definition: A hole in the ground.
An area at a racetrack used for refueling and repairing the vehicles during a race.

The section of a marching band containing mallet percussion instruments and other large percussion instruments too large to be marched, such as the tam-tam; the front ensemble. Can also refer to the area on the sidelines where these instruments are placed.
senses.native: 行進樂隊中演奏大鼓等打擊樂器的前排樂團；也可指這些樂器放置的旁側區域

senses.definition: A mine.

A hole or trench in the ground, excavated according to grid coordinates, so that the provenance of any feature observed and any specimen or artifact revealed may be established by precise measurement.
senses.native: 依照網格座標挖掘的地面孔洞或溝槽，用以精確測定所觀察到的特徵、樣本或文物的來源

senses.definition: A trading pit.
An armpit.
A luggage hold.
A small surface hole or depression, a fossa.
senses.native: 小型表面孔洞或凹陷，即窪地

senses.definition: The indented mark left by a pustule, as in smallpox.
senses.native: 膿包留下的凹痕，如天花病變處

senses.definition: The grave, underworld or Hell.

examples.text: Kalman was watching the fire pit.
examples.translation: 卡爾曼正注視著那個火坑。

examples.text: He fell into the bottomless pit.
examples.translation: 他掉進了無底的深淵。

examples.text: That family really is the pits!
examples.translation: 那家人簡直糟糕透頂！

examples.text: As a man, no a human being, you're the pits!
examples.translation: 身為人類，你簡直糟透了！

examples.text: I dug a huge pit with my shovel in just one day.
examples.translation: 我只用一天就用鏟子挖了一個大坑。

examples.text: He who digs a pit for his brother falls into it.
examples.translation: 誰若為兄弟挖坑，自己也會掉進去。

etymology.text: From Middle English pit, pet, püt, from Old English pytt, from Proto-West Germanic *puti, from Latin puteus (“trench, pit, well”), although there are phonetic difficulties.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 pit、pet 或 püt，再追溯至古英語 pytt，來自日耳曼語族原初詞 *puti，意即拉丁語 puteus（溝渠、坑洞或井），儘管存在音韻上的困難。

senses.definition: The act of reflecting or the state of being reflected.
The property of a propagated wave being thrown back from a surface (such as a mirror).
Something, such as an image, that is reflected.
Careful thought or consideration.
A representative manifestation or outcome of a condition, trend or trait.
Used to make an implied criticism.
The process or mechanism of determining the capabilities of an object at run-time.
The folding of a part; a fold.

examples.text: Spirituality begins with self-reflection.
examples.translation: 靈性從自我反省開始。

examples.text: Mary is looking at her reflection.
examples.translation: 瑪麗正看著自己的倒影。

examples.text: Reflections could be seen in the puddles.
examples.translation: 水窪裡可以看見倒影。

examples.text: A little reflection will show you that you are wrong.
examples.translation: 只要你細心想一想，就會明白自己的錯處了。

examples.text: My cat peers bemusedly at her reflection in the water.
examples.translation: 我的貓兒一臉迷惘地盯著自己在水中的倒影。

examples.text: I saw my reflection in the window.
examples.translation: 我在窗戶上看見了我的映像。

etymology.text: From Middle English refleccion, refleccioun, refleccioune, reflection, from Middle French reflection, reflexion, and its source Late Latin reflexiō, from the participle stem of reflectō. The current spelling is influenced by reflect. Equivalent to reflect + -ion.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 refleccion、refleccioun、refleccioune，來源為中世紀法文 reflection、reflexion，再源自拉丁文 reflexiō，出自 reflectō 的分詞語幹。現行拼寫受 reflect 影響，等同 reflect + -ion。

senses.definition: The act of contemplating; being highly concentrated in thought; musing.
Holy meditation.
The act of looking forward to a future event.
The state of being considered or planned.

examples.text: He watches the world in quiet contemplation.
examples.translation: 他靜心沉思著世界。

examples.text: Wisdom grows through contemplation.
examples.translation: 智慧透過沉思而增長。

examples.text: The mind balks in contemplation of the monuments of Egypt.
examples.translation: 埃及的紀念碑令人難以沉思。

examples.text: What serious contemplation are you in?
examples.translation: 你在進行什麼嚴肅的沉思？

examples.text: Silent contemplation is pleasant.
examples.translation: 靜心沉思令人愉悅。

examples.text: The young man was completely absorbed in the contemplation of her beauty.
examples.translation: 那年輕人完全沉浸在對她美貌的沉思中。

etymology.text: From Middle English contemplacioun, from Old French contemplation, from Latin contemplatio. By surface analysis, contemplate + -ion.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 contemplacioun，來自舊法語 contemplation，拉丁語 contemplatio。字面分析為 contemplate 加上 -ion。

senses.definition: Consideration of past times.

examples.text: In retrospect, I think you were right.
examples.translation: 回顧來說，我認為你是對的。

examples.text: This is embarrassing in retrospect.
examples.translation: 回顧來說，這令人尷尬。

examples.text: In retrospect, Tom wishes he had spent more time studying.
examples.translation: 回顧來說，湯姆希望自己花更多時間學習。

examples.text: In retrospect, that decision was a mistake.
examples.translation: 回顧來說，那個決定是個錯誤。

examples.text: In retrospect, I should have treated her with more respect.
examples.translation: 回顧來說，我本應對她更尊重。

examples.text: In retrospect, maybe I shouldn't have posted that photo in my blog.
examples.translation: 回顧來說，也許我不該在部落格貼那張照片。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin retrōspectum, from retrōspicio (“to look back at”), equivalent to retro- + -spect. Compare review.
etymology.native: 此詞源自拉丁語 retrōspectum，由 retrōspicio（「回顧」）組成，等同 retro- 加上 -spect。可與 review 相比。

senses.definition: A flexible tube conveying water or other fluid.
A stocking-like garment worn on the legs; pantyhose, women's tights.
senses.native: 穿在腿上的類似襪子的衣物；連褲襪、女式緊身褲

senses.definition: Close-fitting trousers or breeches, reaching to the knee.

examples.text: May I borrow your garden hose?
examples.translation: 我可以借你的園藝水龍頭嗎？

examples.text: Tom watered the garden with the garden hose.
examples.translation: 湯姆用園藝水龍頭澆花園。

examples.text: Tom drank the water as it came out the hose.
examples.translation: 湯姆喝著從水龍頭流出的水。

examples.text: He played a hose on the burning hotel.
examples.translation: 他用水龍頭對著著火的飯店噴水。

examples.text: The water stopped running because the hose has a kink in it.
examples.translation: 水停了，因為水龍頭彎曲了。

examples.text: He connected the rubber hose to the exhaust.
examples.translation: 他把橡膠水龍頭接在排氣管上。

etymology.text: From Middle English hose (“leggings, hose”), from Old English hose, hosa (“hose, leggings”), from Proto-West Germanic *hosā, from Proto-Germanic *husǭ (“coverings, leggings, trousers”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kewH- (“to cover”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 hose（意為「褲管、緊身褲」），來自古英文 hose, hosa（意為「褲子、緊身褲」），源自原始西日耳曼語 *hosā，再源自原始德語 *husǭ（意為「覆蓋物、緊身褲、長褲」），最終源自原始印歐語 *(s)kewH-（意為「覆蓋」）

senses.definition: To water or spray with a hose.
To spray as if with a hose; to spray in great quantity.
To deliver using a hose.
To provide with hose (garment)
To trick or deceive.
To break or destroy (a system), especially by wiping files or other content.
To cause an unfair disadvantage to a player or team through poor officiating; especially, to cause a player or team to lose the game with an incorrect call.

examples.text: Take this piece of rubber hose.
examples.translation: 拿這段橡膠水龍頭。

examples.text: Hose the lawn.
examples.translation: 用水龍頭澆草坪。

examples.text: The garden hose sprays water for watering plants.
examples.translation: 園藝水龍頭用來澆植物噴水。

examples.text: This hose, engineered for high pressure, serves the industrial pump.
examples.translation: 這根為高壓設計的軟管，用於工業泵。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The hose, a vital conduit, transports water through the complex irrigation network.
examples.translation: 這根重要的輸水管，負責將水輸送至複雜的灌溉網路。

etymology.text: From Middle English hose (“leggings, hose”), from Old English hose, hosa (“hose, leggings”), from Proto-West Germanic *hosā, from Proto-Germanic *husǭ (“coverings, leggings, trousers”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kewH- (“to cover”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 hose（意為「褲管、緊身褲」），來自古英文 hose, hosa（意為「褲子、緊身褲」），源自原始西日耳曼語 *hosā，再源自原始德語 *husǭ（意為「覆蓋物、緊身褲、長褲」），最終源自原始印歐語 *(s)kewH-（意為「覆蓋」）

senses.definition: Accesories or clothing that is worn on the foot; a shoe, sandal, etc.

examples.text: Shoes, slippers, and sandals are footwear.
examples.translation: 鞋子、拖鞋和涼鞋屬於鞋類。

examples.text: Have you already changed your footwear?
examples.translation: 您已經換過鞋了嗎？

examples.text: Clothes and footwear are sold here.
examples.translation: 這裡出售衣物和鞋類。

examples.text: Wear appropriate footwear to prevent any injuries.
examples.translation: 穿著合適的鞋類可預防受傷。

examples.text: I don't really understand footwear.
examples.translation: 我其實不太懂鞋類。

examples.text: Does Algeria produce footwear?
examples.translation: 阿爾及利亞生產鞋類嗎？

etymology.text: From foot + -wear.
etymology.native: 由「足」加上「鞋類」構成。

senses.definition: Assuming a tone of superiority, or a patronizing attitude.

examples.text: Donald was condescending to Jessica.
examples.translation: 唐納德對潔西卡態度傲慢。

examples.text: Please don't be so condescending.
examples.translation: 請別那麼傲慢。

examples.text: Heath can be so condescending.
examples.translation: 希斯可以那麼傲慢。

examples.text: Tom looked at Mary with a condescending smile.
examples.translation: 湯姆對瑪麗微笑，神情顯得傲慢。

examples.text: The boss spoke in a condescending tone when addressing the female staff members.
examples.translation: 主管對女員工說話時，語氣顯得傲慢。

examples.text: The English teacher's condescending attitude undermined the foreign students' motivation to improve.
examples.translation: 英文老師的傲慢態度削弱了外國學生提升的動機。

senses.definition: An act of condescension.
present participle and gerund of condescend
Knowing, clever, mischievous.
Cute, sly, prematurely wise.
Principal; primary.

examples.text: I attempted to hide my emotions, but an arch remark escaped my lips.
examples.translation: 我試圖掩飾情緒，但一句刻薄的話脫口而出。

examples.text: They were arch enemies.

etymology.text: From Middle English arch, arche, from Old French arche (“an arch”), a feminine form of arc, from Latin arcus (“a bow, arc, arch”). Doublet of arc and arco. Displaced native Old English bīeġels and Old English hwealf.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語的 arch 或 arche，來自舊法語 arche（拱門），是 arc 的陰性形式，再源自拉丁語 arcus（弓、弧、拱門）。這是 arc 與 arco 的同形異義詞。

senses.definition: Offensively condescending.

examples.text: Men are repelled by patronizing women.
examples.translation: 男人對奉承式的女性感到反感。

examples.text: I'm not patronizing you.
examples.translation: 我並非在奉承你。

examples.text: Stop patronizing me.
examples.translation: 別再奉承我了。

examples.text: Is this patronizing or meddling in someone else's business?
examples.translation: 「好為人師」還是「好管閒事」?

examples.text: I don't like your patronizing tone.
examples.translation: 我不喜歡你那種奉承式的語氣。

examples.text: I hate your patronizing attitude.
examples.translation: 我恨你那種奉承式的態度。

senses.definition: thuggish

examples.text: He is a thuggy guy, always yelling at others.
examples.translation: 他是一個粗魯的人，總是在對別人大吼大叫。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From thug + -y.
etymology.native: 來自 thug + -y。

senses.definition: Unevenly cut; having the texture of something so cut.

Likeness, resemblance.
Appearance, show, sign, expression.

examples.text: What is the likelihood of surviving?
examples.translation: 生存的可能性是多少？

examples.text: In all likelihood, I will win.
examples.translation: 極有可能我會贏。

examples.text: In all likelihood, I'll win.
examples.translation: 極有可能我會贏。

examples.text: What is the likelihood of your getting fired?
examples.translation: 你被解僱的可能性是多少？

examples.text: In all likelihood, they'll be away for a week.
examples.translation: 極有可能他們會缺席一週。

examples.text: In all likelihood, it will rain this afternoon.
examples.translation: 極有可能今天下午會下雨。

etymology.text: From Middle English liklihode, equivalent to likely + -hood.
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 liklihode，等同於 likely + -hood。

senses.definition: A currently unrealized ability (with the most common adposition being to).
The gravitational potential: the radial (irrotational, static) component of a gravitational field, also known as the Newtonian potential or the gravitoelectric field.

The work (energy) required to move a reference particle from a reference location to a specified location in the presence of a force field, for example to bring a unit positive electric charge from an infinite distance to a specified point against an electric field.
A verbal construction or form stating something is possible or probable.

examples.text: He has the potential to become world champion.

senses.definition: The condition of being susceptible; vulnerability.
senses.native: 易受影響的狀態；脆弱性

senses.definition: A way in which one is susceptible.
emotional sensitivity.
Being vulnerable to a treatment (usually an antibiotic or antifungal); also, the degree of such vulnerability (i.e., weak, moderate, or strong).
senses.native: 對治療（通常是抗生素或抗真菌藥）的易感性；亦指此類易感程度（即弱、中或強）

senses.definition: electric susceptibility, a measure of how easily a dielectric polarizes in response to an external electric field (compare permittivity).
senses.native: 電易感性，衡量絕緣體在外部電場作用下極化之容易程度的指標（與介電係數相比）

examples.text: Exposure to radiation causes susceptibility to mutations.
examples.translation: 輻射暴露會導致突變的易感性。

examples.text: I am very sick because I have a high susceptibility to colds.
examples.translation: 我病得很重，因為我對感冒特別容易感染。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: My sister is weak and has a big susceptibility to germs.
examples.translation: 我姐姐體弱且對病菌極易受感染。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The baby has a strong susceptibility to catching the flu.
examples.translation: 嬰兒對流感特別容易感染。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: People with low immunity often have a high susceptibility to infection.
examples.translation: 免疫力低的人通常對感染特別容易受影響。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: His susceptibility to criticism often causes unnecessary anxiety in social situations.
examples.translation: 他對批評的敏感常使他在社交場合產生不必要的焦慮。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

morphemes.native: 易受影響的狀態、脆弱性

etymology.text: From susceptible + -ity.
etymology.native: 由「易受影響」加上後綴「-ity」組成。

senses.definition: To assess a person or a situation.

examples.text: An adult aardvark can weigh up to 100 kilograms.
examples.translation: 成年土撥鼠的體重可達一百公斤。

examples.text: The antlers of a caribou can weigh up to 40 pounds.
examples.translation: 叉角羚的角可重達四十磅。

examples.text: You must weigh up the pros and cons.
examples.translation: 你必須比較利弊。

examples.text: A bunch of grapes can weigh up to two kilograms.
examples.translation: 一串葡萄可重達兩公斤。

examples.text: A male giraffe may weigh up to one and a half ton.
examples.translation: 雄性長頸鹿體重可達一噸半。

examples.text: On Kodiak Island, some bears can weigh up to a ton.
examples.translation: 在科迪亞克島，有些熊體重可達一噸。

senses.definition: Separate; select.
Separated from others of the same kind.
Separate from a mass and collected together along lines of fraction.
senses.native: 從群體分離並依分數收集

examples.text: People often segregate the two approaches, but they can often work together.
examples.translation: 人們常將兩種方法分開，但二者往往能協同運作。

examples.text: Racist politicians want to segregate schools again.
examples.translation: 種族主義政客希望再次分隔學校。

examples.text: We don't segregate in this county.
examples.translation: 我們這個縣不分隔。

examples.text: We segregate data to protect privacy and avoid misuse.
examples.translation: 我們分離資料以保護隱私並避免誤用。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Artists segregate their creative output by genre to maintain stylistic purity.
examples.translation: 藝術家按流派分類創作成果，以維持風格純粹。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: Scholars segregate research findings by methodology to ensure academic rigor.
examples.translation: 學者按研究方法分類成果，以確保學術嚴謹。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From Latin sēgregātus, perfect passive participle of sēgregō (“to separate”), from sē- (“apart”) + gregō (“to flock or group”), from grex (“flock”). Compare gregarious, aggregate.
etymology.native: 來自拉丁語 sēgregātus，是 sēgregō（意為「分離」）的完成式被動分詞，源自 sē-（意為「分開」）+ gregō（意為「聚群」），而 gregō 又來自 grex（意為「群體」）。可與 gregarious、aggregate 相比。

senses.definition: To separate.
In particular, to separate and organize by characteristics.
To separate (races, sexes, or other groups, especially black and white people), especially by social policies that directly or indirectly keep them apart.
senses.native: 分離（種族、性別或其他群體，尤指黑白人種）

examples.text: The buses in Montgomery were segregated.
examples.translation: 蒙哥馬利的公車分隔運行。

examples.text: He keeps his daughter segregated at home.
examples.translation: 他將女兒在家分隔居住。

examples.text: Why is the United States still segregated?
examples.translation: 美國為何仍持續分隔？

examples.text: This neighborhood is segregated.
examples.translation: 這個社區是分隔的。

examples.text: Many towns segregated into new counties.
examples.translation: 許多鎮分離成新縣。

examples.text: Large mining claims are segregated into smaller claims.
examples.translation: 大型礦權被分拆為較小的礦權。

etymology.text: From Latin sēgregātus, perfect passive participle of sēgregō (“to separate”), from sē- (“apart”) + gregō (“to flock or group”), from grex (“flock”). Compare gregarious, aggregate.
etymology.native: 來自拉丁語 sēgregātus，是 sēgregō（意為「分離」）的完成式被動分詞，源自 sē-（意為「分開」）+ gregō（意為「聚群」），而 gregō 又來自 grex（意為「群體」）。可與 gregarious、aggregate 相比。

senses.definition: An entity that is separated in some way from a reference group or entity.

examples.text: A segregate becomes conspicuous once it is removed from its aggregate.
examples.translation: 當一個分離體被移離其集合時，便會顯得突出。

examples.text: Experiments show clearly that genes segregate.
examples.translation: 實驗清楚顯示基因會分離。

examples.text: The government must segregate services by age group for fairness.
examples.translation: 政府必須按年齡分群提供服務以確保公平。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

etymology.text: From Latin sēgregātus, perfect passive participle of sēgregō (“to separate”), from sē- (“apart”) + gregō (“to flock or group”), from grex (“flock”). Compare gregarious, aggregate.
etymology.native: 來自拉丁語 sēgregātus，是 sēgregō（意為「分離」）的完成式被動分詞，源自 sē-（意為「分開」）+ gregō（意為「聚群」），而 gregō 又來自 grex（意為「群體」）。可與 gregarious、aggregate 相比。

senses.definition: To split or separate (something) into two or more parts.
To calculate the quotient number by which another one (the divisor) is multiplied to produce a second number (the dividend).
To separate into two or more parts.
To share (something) by dividing it.
To cause (a group of people) to disagree.
To be a divisor of.
To reproduce by either mitosis or meiosis.
senses.native: 透過有絲分裂或減數分裂進行複製

senses.definition: To disunite in opinion or interest; to make discordant or hostile; to set at variance.
senses.native: 在意見或利益上造成不和；使對立或敵對；使產生矛盾

senses.definition: To break friendship; to fall out.
To have a share; to partake.

To vote, as in the British parliament and other legislatures, by the members separating themselves into two parties (as on opposite sides of the hall or in opposite lobbies), that is, the ayes dividing from the nays.
senses.native: 在議會等立法機構中，成員分為兩派（如對坐於不同區域）進行表決

examples.text: We divided the money between us.
examples.translation: 我們平分這筆錢。

examples.text: Six divided by two equals three.
examples.translation: 六除以二得三。

examples.text: He divided his books into five categories.
examples.translation: 他把他的書分為五類。

examples.text: The mother divided the pie into eight pieces.
examples.translation: 母親將派分成八塊。

examples.text: Among Gen Zers (18 to 24 years old), three-quarters said they felt the United States is more divided than before.
examples.translation: 四分之三的 Z 世代 (18 至 24 歲) 表示，美國感覺起來比過去更分裂。

examples.text: This is because you approach everything as a total person, with no loose ends hanging out to signify divided intentions.
examples.translation: 這是因為你總是全身心處理每一件事情，沒有讓雞毛蒜皮的問題分散了你的目標。

relations.native: 部分；碎片；易損壞；不堅固；不耐用；易失敗或滅亡
部分；碎片；易損壞；不堅固；不耐用；易失敗或滅亡

etymology.text: PIE word
etymology.native: 原始印歐語詞根與「分開」相關。

senses.definition: To modify so as to create a difference or distinction.
To show or be the difference or distinction between things.
To recognize as different or distinct.
To calculate the derivative of a function.
To calculate the differential of a function of multiple variables.
senses.native: 計算多變量函數之微分

senses.definition: To perceive the difference between things; to discriminate.
senses.native: 感知事物間之差異；辨別

senses.definition: To teach a lesson in multiple different ways in order to meet the needs of more or less advanced students.
senses.native: 以多種方式教學，以滿足不同進階程度學生之需求

senses.definition: To (cause to) go through a process of development called differentiation; to make or become different in form or function.
senses.native: 經歷分化過程；使或成為形式或功能上不同

examples.text: Technology has differentiated our cultures.
examples.translation: 科技已使我們之文化產生差異。

examples.text: Asian communities are very differentiated.
examples.translation: 亞洲社群極具差異性。

examples.text: What differentiates you from our other candidates?
examples.translation: 什麼使您與其他候選者不同？

examples.text: What differentiates a hyena from a donkey?
examples.translation: 什麼使鬣狗與駱馬不同？

examples.text: I can't differentiate virtue from vice.
examples.translation: 我無法分辨美德與醜惡。

examples.text: Healthcare reform differentiates our guy from the other candidates.
examples.translation: 醫療改革使我們之候選人與其他候選人不同。

etymology.text: From New Latin differentiātus, perfect passive participle of differentiō (see -ate (verb-forming suffix) and -ate (noun-forming suffix)), from Latin differentia (“difference”); see difference.
etymology.native: 源自新拉丁語之分化詞，見差別。

senses.definition: In good enough shape to be shown or offered to other people; tidy; attractive.
Acceptable; worth considering.
Capable of being presented to a church living.

examples.text: Tom is presentable, isn't he?
examples.translation: 湯姆穿得還挺像樣的，對吧？

examples.text: They need to look more presentable.
examples.translation: 他們需要看起來更得體。

examples.text: Mary is presentable, isn't she?
examples.translation: 瑪麗看起來很得體，不是嗎？

examples.text: This Kabyle dress makes you very presentable.
examples.translation: 這件凱布利族服裝讓你顯得非常得體。

examples.text: Your clothes are all torn. You're really not presentable!
examples.translation: 你的衣服全破了，你真的不夠得體！

examples.text: He is as competent as he is presentable.
examples.translation: 他既有能力又很得體。

etymology.text: From Middle French presentable, from Old French, as if present + -able.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀法語 presentable，來自古法語，意為「可呈現」。

senses.definition: Pleasing to the taste, tasty.
Tolerable, acceptable.

examples.text: Fentanyl pills are more palatable to middle-class Americans than heroin.
examples.translation: 芬太尼藥丸比海洛因更受中產階級美國人歡迎。

examples.text: The pilot was revised to be more palatable to a mature audience.
examples.translation: 導演修改了劇本，使其更符合成熟觀眾的口味。

examples.text: For some instant noodles make a palatable, if not especially nutritious, meal.
examples.translation: 某些速食麵可以做成可口，甚至營養豐富的餐點。

examples.text: A palatable solution to the problem.
examples.translation: 解決這個問題的可行方案。

examples.text: This soup tastes very palatable and I love it.
examples.translation: 這湯味道很好，我愛吃。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

examples.text: The cake is so palatable that everyone wants a piece.
examples.translation: 蛋糕太好吃了，每個人都想嘗一口。
examples.license: AI 產生（標記為 AI 翻譯）

relations.native: 看似合理、可信或可接受的；可能為真
甜美而愉悅的；美味的；多汁的，鮮嫩的

etymology.text: From palate + -able.
etymology.native: 源自「舌頭」加上表示「可...的」後綴。

senses.definition: To cause a quality to become part of someone's nature.
To pour in (medicine, for example) drop by drop.

examples.text: My parents instilled etiquette in me.
examples.translation: 我的父母教我禮儀。

examples.text: Life's verses instill hope.
examples.translation: 生命的詩句喚起希望。

examples.text: We wanted to instill a feeling of hope.
examples.translation: 我們希望喚起希望的感覺。

examples.text: Instill confidence in your children.
examples.translation: 要讓孩子建立自信。

examples.text: The love of art was instilled into Tom at an early age.
examples.translation: 藝術的愛在湯姆年幼時便被灌輸。

examples.text: We must instill patriotism into the young people of today.
examples.translation: 我們必須將愛國情懷灌輸給今天的年輕人。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin instillō.
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 instillō。

senses.definition: To cause to become pregnant.
To fertilize.
To saturate, or infuse.
To fill pores or spaces with a substance.
senses.native: 用物質填滿孔隙或空間

senses.definition: To become pregnant.

examples.text: I impregnated his mind with new ideas.
examples.translation: 我用新想法浸透了他的心靈。

examples.text: Antonio married and impregnated a fourteen-year girl.
examples.translation: 安東尼奧結婚後使一名十四歲少女懷孕。

examples.text: His clothes were impregnated with the stench of manure.
examples.translation: 他的衣服浸透了糞便的臭味。

examples.text: This giraffe cow got impregnated in April.
examples.translation: 這頭雌長頸鹿於四月受孕。

examples.text: The bull impregnated the cow.
examples.translation: 公牛使母牛懷孕。

examples.text: I was abducted and impregnated by wolves who landed their flying saucer in my backyard.
examples.translation: 我被狼綁架並懷孕了，牠們降落在我後院的飛碟。

etymology.text: The adjective is first attested in 1540, the verb in 1605; borrowed from Medieval Latin impraegnātus, perfect passive participle of Latin impraegnō, see -ate (verb-forming suffix) and -ate (adjective-forming suffix). Doublet of impregn; participial usage of the adjective up until Early Modern English.
etymology.native: 此形容詞最早見於 1540 年，動詞見於 1605 年；借自中古拉丁語 impraegnātus，為拉丁語 impraegnō 的完成時被動分詞。

senses.definition: To create (a hole) by removing material with a drill (tool).
To practice, especially in (or as in) a military context.
To cause to drill (practice); to train, especially in military arts.
To repeat an idea frequently in order to encourage someone to remember it.
To investigate or examine something in more detail or at a different level
To throw, run, hit or kick with a lot of power.
To hit someone with a pitch, especially in an intentional context.
To have sexual intercourse with; to penetrate.
To shoot; to kill by shooting.

examples.text: They are drilling in our house.
examples.translation: 他們正在家裡鑽洞。

examples.text: Mr Smith drilled them in English pronunciation.
examples.translation: 史密斯先生用英語發音演練了它們。

examples.text: Politics is the drilling of very thick planks.
examples.translation: 政治是將厚木板鑽透的過程。

examples.text: Tom invested in an offshore drilling company.
examples.translation: 湯姆投資了一家離岸鑽探公司。

examples.text: He drilled a well in the orchard.
examples.translation: 他在果園裡鑽了一口井。

examples.text: The loud sounds of sawing, drilling and scraping reverberate around the room.
examples.translation: 鋸子、鑽頭和刮刀的刺耳聲音在房間內迴盪。

etymology.text: From Middle Dutch drillen (“bore, move in a circle”).
etymology.native: 源於中古荷蘭語 drillen，意為「鑽孔」或「圓形移動」。

senses.definition: To teach (a person) with a biased, one-sided or uncritical ideology; to brainwash.
To teach and instill (something, to a person) in a biased, one-sided way.
To teach; to instruct.

examples.text: I have been indoctrinated to hate Christianity.
examples.translation: 我已被灌輸了對基督教的憎恨。

examples.text: They are a bunch of indoctrinated morons.
examples.translation: 他們是一群被灌輸思想的傻瓜。

examples.text: I was indoctrinated to hate religion.
examples.translation: 我被灌輸了對宗教的憎恨。

examples.text: American military recruitment rates are down because this generation isn't as indoctrinated as previous ones.
examples.translation: 美國軍隊徵兵人數下降，因為這一代人不像前幾代人那樣易受洗腦。

examples.text: I was born in Israel in 1956 and I was indoctrinated into the Zionist discourse.
examples.translation: 我於 1956 年出生在以色列，並被灌輸進猶太復國主義的論述中。

examples.text: Purely autonomous robots were probably indoctrinated into a robot religion because the universe is about probabilities, not absolute values.
examples.translation: 純自主機器人可能已被灌輸成一種「機器人宗教」，因為宇宙是關於機率而非絕對價值。

relations.native: 給予或賜予（例如品質或屬性）

etymology.text: From in- + doctrine + -ate (verb-forming suffix). Compare French endoctriner.
etymology.native: 由前綴 in-、詞根 doctrine 及動詞後綴 -ate 組成。可與法語 endoctriner 相比。

senses.definition: To give or bestow (e.g. a quality or property).
To give a part or to share.
To make known; to show (by speech, writing etc.).
senses.native: 使為人所知；透過言語、書寫等顯示

senses.definition: To hold a conference or consultation.
To obtain a share of; to partake of.

examples.text: Let me impart these few words of wisdom to you.
examples.translation: 讓我將這幾句智慧話語傳授給您。

examples.text: He imparted all his knowledge to his son.
examples.translation: 他將所有知識都傳授給了兒子。

examples.text: He wants to impart his wisdom to you.
examples.translation: 他想將智慧傳授給您。

examples.text: Tom is eager to impart his knowledge.
examples.translation: 湯姆渴望將知識傳授出來。

examples.text: I enjoy imparting my wide knowledge on any subject and I like to think logically.
examples.translation: 我樂於將廣泛的知識傳授給任何人，並喜歡邏輯思考。

examples.text: The teachers didn't just impart knowledge to us; they also taught us how to think.
examples.translation: 老師不僅將知識傳授給我們，也教導我們如何思考。

morphemes.native: 給予或賜予（例如品質或屬性）

etymology.text: From Middle English imparten, borrowed from Middle French impartir, empartir, from Late Latin impartiō, impertiō, from im- (“in”) + Latin partiō (“divide”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀法語，再來自晚拉丁語。

senses.definition: To evoke, educe (emotions, feelings, responses, etc.); to generate, obtain, or provoke as a response or answer.
To use logic to arrive at truth; to derive by reason.
To draw out, bring out, bring forth (something latent); to obtain information from someone or something.

examples.text: That's sure to elicit a smile.
examples.translation: 那肯定會讓人微笑。

examples.text: We plan to elicit opinions from the public.
examples.translation: 我們計劃向大眾徵求意見。

examples.text: Everyone knows that luck and wealth elicit envy.
examples.translation: 人人都知道，幸運與財富會引發嫉妒。

examples.text: Tom tried to elicit a response from Mary.
examples.translation: 湯姆試圖從瑪麗那得到回應。

examples.text: It seems like they resorted to a strategy meant to elicit sympathy.
examples.translation: 他們似乎採用了旨在喚起同情心的策略。

examples.text: Benedito scratched behind his billy goat's ears, eliciting a contented bleat from the animal.
examples.translation: 本尼迪托抓了比利山羊的耳朵，山羊便發出滿足的咩聲。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin elicitus from eliciō (“draw forth”).
etymology.native: 源自拉丁語 elicitus，來自 eliciō（意為「拉出」）

senses.definition: Alternative spelling of badmouth.

examples.text: He's always bad-mouthing his wife.

senses.definition: A written list or inventory. (Now obsolete except in specific senses or set phrases; bill of lading, bill of goods, etc.)
A document, originally sealed; a formal statement or official memorandum. (Now obsolete except with certain qualifying words; bill of health, bill of sale etc.)
A draft of a law, presented to a legislature for enactment; a proposed or projected law.
A piece of paper money; a banknote.
A written note of goods sold, services rendered, or work done, with the price or charge owing; an invoice.
A paper, written or printed, and posted up or given away, to advertise something, as a lecture, a play, or the sale of goods

A writing that binds the signer or signers to pay a certain sum at a future day or on demand, with or without interest, as may be stated in the document; a bill of exchange. In the United States, it is usually called a note, a note of hand, or a promissory note.
A declaration made in writing, stating some wrong the complainant has suffered from the defendant, or a fault committed by some person against a law.
One hundred dollars.
One hundred pounds sterling.
A written note of goods sold, services rendered, or work done, listing the price or charge paid; a receipt.

etymology.text: From Middle English overschadwen, overschadewe, from Old English ofersċeadwian (“to overshadow”), equivalent to over- + shadow. Compare with West Frisian oerskaduwe (“to overshadow”), Dutch overschaduwen (“to overshadow”), German überschatten (“to overshadow”), Gothic 𐌿𐍆𐌰𐍂𐍃𐌺𐌰𐌳𐍅𐌾𐌰𐌽 (ufarskadwjan, “to overshadow”), and more distantly, Old Norse yfirskyggja (“to overshadow”), Danish overskygge (“to overshadow”), Swedish överskugga (“to overshadow”), Old English ofersċūwan (“to overshadow”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 overschadwen、overschadewe，來自古英語 ofersċeadwian（意為「遮蔽」），由 over- + shadow 組成。可與西弗里斯蘭語 oerskaduwe（意為「遮蔽」）、荷蘭語 overschaduwen（意為「遮蔽」）、德語 überschatten（意為「遮蔽」）、古高地德語 𐌿𐍆𐌰𐍂𐍃𐌺𐌰𐌳𐍅𐌾𐌰𐌽（ufarskadwjan，意為「遮蔽」）相對應，更遠古的則有古諾斯語 yfirskyggja（意為「遮蔽」）、丹麥語 overskygge（意為「遮蔽」）、瑞典語 överskugga（意為「遮蔽」），以及古英語 ofersċūwan（意為「遮蔽」）。

etymology.text: From Middle English eclipse, from Old French eclipse, from Latin eclīpsis, from Ancient Greek ἔκλειψις (ékleipsis, “eclipse”), from ἐκλείπω (ekleípō, “to abandon, go missing, vanish”), from ἐκ (ek, “out”) and λείπω (leípō, “to leave behind”). Doublet of eclipsis. See also ellipse, ellipsis.
etymology.native: 源於中古英語 eclipse，來自舊法語 eclipse，再源自拉丁語 eclīpsis，最終來自古希臘語 ἔκλειψις（ékleipsis，意為「日食」），由 ἐκλείπω（ekleípō，意為「放棄、消失」）構成，該詞由前綴 ἐκ（ek，意為「出」）與動詞 λείπω（leípō，意為「留下」）組成。

etymology.text: From Middle English brood, brod, from Old English brōd (“brood; foetus; breeding, hatching”), from Proto-Germanic *brōduz (“heat, breeding”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰreh₁- (“breath, mist, vapour, steam”).
